[Watch: Register your app in Play Console](https://app.arcade.software/share/xEQkFPgMTjAXxj6QlKme)

### App details

BLOCKERListing fields are missing or invalid.

What this means

One or more required fields for your Google Play listing are incomplete. Fields checked include:

- App name
- Short description, maximum 80 characters
- Full description, maximum 4,000 characters
- Privacy Policy URL
- App category
- Countries for distribution

How to resolve it

1. In Agency App Manager, go to **Distribution → Profile** and open **App Details**. Complete every required field.
2. Keep the short description under **80 characters** and the full description under **4,000 characters**.
3. Make sure the Privacy Policy URL is a live **https://** address that opens without a login.
4. Google also requires a content rating. Complete this in **Play Console → Store presence → Content rating**.

Verify the fix

Return to the checklist, tick **I have fixed the listed issues in App Store Connect / Play Console**, then select **Verify**. The check should now pass.

Video tutorial

[Watch: Complete your app details](https://app.arcade.software/share/wUVHPn1oYS8FKPE1TwZr)

### Personal & support information

BLOCKERContact fields are missing or invalid.

What this means

Developer contact details for your Play Store listing are incomplete. These appear on your listing under *Developer contact*.

How to resolve it

1. In Agency App Manager, go to **Distribution → Profile** and open **Personal info**.
2. Complete all required fields: first name, last name, phone number, email, support email, support URL, and address.
3. Save your changes.

Verify the fix

Return to the checklist, tick **I have fixed the listed issues in App Store Connect / Play Console**, then select **Verify**. The check should now pass.

Video tutorial

[Watch: Complete personal and support information](https://app.arcade.software/share/SHrHpJWoZciij9z6Fm7I)

## Frequently asked questions

I fixed the problem in App Store Connect, but the checklist still shows the issue. Why?

Results do not refresh on their own. Tick the confirmation box and select **Verify** to run the checks again. Google Play permission changes can also take a few minutes to apply.

Can I build my app while a warning is showing?

Yes. Warnings do not block your build. Two of the iOS warnings clear on their own once your agreements are active, and the Firebase warning only matters if you use Firebase features.

Do I need Firebase?

No. Firebase is optional for White Label Mobile Apps. If you are not using Firebase push notifications or analytics, the Firebase warning is safe to ignore.

Will an Apple issue stop my Android build?

No. The checklist runs separately for each store.

Why do my Bundle ID and package name have to match exactly?

Agency App Manager matches your app to your store account on that identifier alone, and the match is case-sensitive. Always copy the value rather than retyping it. Take particular care with your Google Play package name, which cannot be changed once the app is created.

Who can accept the Apple agreements?

Only the Account Holder for your Apple Developer account. If you have the Admin role, ask your Account Holder to complete this step.

## Related articles

The distribution workflow has three stages. This article covers stage 1 of 3.

- [Troubleshooting Upload to Store Issues for White Label Mobile Apps](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008551)
- [Troubleshooting Submit for Review Issues for White Label Mobile Apps](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008552)

title_en: How to Set Up and Use Agent Logs Monitor in HighLevel
source_md:
Agent Logs Monitor helps you track AI agent performance against measurable goals over a selected period. Instead of reviewing activity logs or historical metrics alone, you can see whether your agents are on pace to reach a target. With scheduled daily checks, progress charts, and email or webhook notifications, Monitor helps you stay informed about important outcomes. This guide covers creating monitors, configuring notification channels, reviewing daily checks, and managing monitor history in HighLevel.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Agent Logs Monitor?](#What-is-Agent-Logs-Monitor?)
- [Key Benefits of Agent Logs Monitor](#Key-Benefits-of-Agent-Logs-Monitor)
- [How To Setup Agent Logs Monitor](#How-To-Setup-Agent-Logs-Monitor)
  - [Access the Monitor Tab](#Access-the-Monitor-Tab)
  - [Create a New Monitor](#Create-a-New-Monitor)
  - [Configure the Tracking Window](#Configure-the-Tracking-Window)
  - [Choose AI Products and Schedule Daily Checks](#Choose-AI-Products-and-Schedule-Daily-Checks)
  - [Configure Monitor Notifications](#Configure-Monitor-Notifications)
  - [Review the Preview and Create the Monitor](#Review-the-Preview-and-Create-the-Monitor)
- [Configure Email and Webhook Notification Channels](#Configure-Email-and-Webhook-Notification-Channels)
  - [Create an Email Notification Channel](#Create-an-Email-Notification-Channel)
  - [Create a Webhook Notification Channel](#Create-a-Webhook-Notification-Channel)
  - [Manage Existing Notification Channels](#Manage-Existing-Notification-Channels)
  - [Understand Monitor Status and Daily Checks](#Understand-Monitor-Status-and-Daily-Checks)
  - [Read Monitor Cards and Status Indicators](#Read-Monitor-Cards-and-Status-Indicators)
  - [Review the Last Seven Daily Checks](#Review-the-Last-Seven-Daily-Checks)
- [Manage Existing Monitors](#Manage-Existing-Monitors)
  - [Edit Monitor Settings and Notifications](#Edit-Monitor-Settings-and-Notifications)
  - [Run a Manual Check](#Run-a-Manual-Check)
  - [View Monitor History and Switch Versions](#View-Monitor-History-and-Switch-Versions)
  - [Repeat, Restart, or Finish Monitoring Windows](#Repeat,-Restart,-or-Finish-Monitoring-Windows)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Agent Logs Monitor?**

Agent Logs Monitor is a goal-tracking feature that measures recorded AI agent activity against a defined target within a selected time window. It helps you understand not only how much activity has occurred, but also whether your agents are progressing at the pace needed to reach their goal.

Unlike the Agent Logs Metrics dashboard, which focuses on historical performance and activity trends, Monitor evaluates specific goals through scheduled daily checks.

For example, you can create a monitor to track **50 appointments booked within 30 days**, include only Conversation AI activity, and schedule a daily check at 9:00 AM. You can also configure notifications when progress falls behind or the target is reached.

Monitor supports different types of recorded AI activity, including:

- **Appointment activity:** Appointments booked, rescheduled, and canceled.

- **Conversation activity:** Conversations handled, conversation volume, and contacts reached.

- **Call activity:** Calls completed and supported Voice AI call metrics.

- **Automation activity:** Workflows triggered, SMS sent, and bot transfers.

- **Knowledge base activity:** Knowledge base lookups.

- **Performance rates:** Success rate, booking conversion, and supported voice call rates.

Count-based goals can track a target number or a maximum limit. Rate-based goals can track percentage targets. Certain metrics automatically determine the available comparison type.

---

## **Key Benefits of Agent Logs Monitor**

Monitoring AI agent outcomes against specific targets helps you identify performance gaps while there is still time to respond. With goal tracking, scheduled evaluations, and configurable notifications, you can review progress without manually calculating whether your agents are on schedule.

- **Goal-based performance tracking:** Set measurable targets for appointments, conversations, calls, and other AI agent outcomes.

- **Daily progress visibility:** Compare current performance against the expected pace required to finish within the selected tracking window.

- **Flexible monitoring periods:** Choose a predefined duration or configure a custom tracking window to match your business goals.

- **AI product-specific monitoring:** Track activity across all supported AI products or narrow a monitor to selected products.

- **Automated progress notifications:** Receive updates when a monitor becomes at risk, reaches its target, or completes its tracking window.

- **Email and webhook delivery:** Configure reusable notification channels to send updates to selected recipients or webhook endpoints.

- **Monitor history and version management:** Review previous monitor configurations, switch between versions, and retain historical results when goals change.

---

## **How To Setup Agent Logs Monitor**

Creating a monitor begins with selecting the outcome you want to measure. You then define the target, tracking period, AI product scope, and daily check schedule. The New monitor form provides a preview of your configuration before you create the monitor.

### 

### **Access the Monitor Tab**

The Monitor tab is available within Agent Logs, alongside the existing agent activity and performance reporting views. Opening this tab gives you access to the Monitor dashboard and notification channel settings.

- From the **Sub-Account view**, select **AI Agents** in the left navigation menu.
- Select **Agent Logs** from the top navigation.
- Click the **Monitor** tab.
- Select **Dashboard** to view your existing monitors.

### 

### **Create a New Monitor**

Each monitor begins with a metric and a comparison target. The metric determines which recorded AI agent activity is measured, while the comparison defines the result you want to achieve or maintain.

- From the **Monitor → Dashboard** view, select **"New Monitor"**
- In the **New monitor** form, select the metric you want to track.
- Review the comparison type associated with the metric. Depending on the selected metric, the monitor can use:

  - **Reach a number:** Track progress toward a target count.
  - **Stay under a cap:** Keep the measured count below a specified limit.
  - **Percentage target:** Track performance against a target rate.
- In **Number to watch**, enter the target value or percentage supported by the selected metric.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083733834/original/n4K4NXJUdhuFAFQzDxyd4AVTTwhPrXgdNg.png?1792488261)

### **Configure the Tracking Window**

The tracking window determines when a monitor begins and ends measuring activity toward its goal. Only activity recorded within the selected window contributes to progress, so earlier activity is not included automatically.

- Under **Time window**, select a duration:

  - 7 days
  - 14 days
  - 30 days
  - 60 days
  - 90 days
  - Custom
- Choose the **Start date**. You can begin monitoring today or schedule a future start date. The end date is calculated from the selected duration.
- To continue monitoring across consecutive periods, select **Repeat this monitor**.

When repetition is enabled, a new monitoring window starts automatically after the current window closes. The completed window remains available in history.

### 

### **Choose AI Products and Schedule Daily Checks**

Product scope determines which AI activity contributes to the target. The daily schedule determines when Monitor evaluates that activity and updates the saved progress.

- Under **Applies to**, choose **All products** or select the AI products you want to include. The available product options shown in the release include:

- Conversation AI
- Voice AI
- Agent Studio
- Managed Agent

- Under **Daily check at**, select the time when the monitor should evaluate progress.
- Select the appropriate **Timezone**.

Monitor evaluates the goal once daily at the scheduled time. Opening the Monitor page does not automatically trigger another check.

### 

### **Configure Monitor Notifications**

Monitor notifications help you receive updates when significant changes occur. You can select which events should generate notifications and where those messages should be delivered.

- In **Notify me when**, configure the notification events you want to monitor:

- **Status becomes at risk:** Sends an alert when progress enters the at-risk state.
- **Goal reached:** Sends an alert when the monitored target is achieved.
- **Tracking window ends:** Sends an update when the monitoring period closes.
- **Daily progress email:** Sends a recurring progress summary during the tracking window.

- For daily progress emails, choose whether to send them at the scheduled check time or at another selected time.
- Select the configured email or webhook notification channels that should receive the applicable updates.

### 

### **Review the Preview and Create the Monitor**

The preview summarizes how the monitor will evaluate your selected goal. Reviewing it before saving helps confirm that the measurement, schedule, and notification destinations match your intended configuration.

- Review the **Preview** panel on the right side of the New monitor form. Confirm:

- - Selected metric and comparison type.
  - Target number or percentage.
  - Tracking window and dates.
  - Included AI products.
  - Daily check time and timezone.
  - Selected notification settings and channels.

- Click **Create monitor** to save the configuration.

The monitor appears as an active card on the Monitor dashboard when its tracking window has started. A monitor with a future start date remains scheduled until that date.

## 

## 

## ****Configure Email and Web**hook Notification Channels**

Notification channels define where Monitor sends updates. You can configure email recipients or webhook endpoints once and select those channels when setting up individual monitors. Each channel has its own configuration and can be managed from the Notification channels tab.

### 

### **Create an Email Notification Channel**

Email channels let you send monitor notifications to a specified group of email addresses. Giving each channel a descriptive name helps you identify the correct recipient list when configuring a monitor.

- Select **Notification channels**.
- Click **Email** to open the **Add email channel** dialog.
- Enter a descriptive name in **Channel name**.
- Under **Email recipients**, enter the first recipient's email address.
- Click **Add** to include the address. Repeat this step for additional recipients.
- Click **Add channel** to save the email notification channel.

### 

### 

### 

### ****Create a Webhook Notif**ication Channel**

Webhook channels send monitor updates to a configured endpoint. They provide a way to deliver selected monitoring events to systems that accept webhook requests.

- Select **Notification channels**.
- Click **Webhook** to open the **Add webhook channel** dialog.
- Enter a descriptive **Channel name**.
- In **Endpoint URL**, enter the destination URL that will receive webhook requests.
- Select the appropriate **HTTP method**. The supplied interface shows **POST**.
- To include additional request headers, click **Add header** and enter the required header details.
- Mark a header as **secret** when it contains a value that should be treated as sensitive.
- Review the **Expected payload** section to see the webhook data structure.
- Optionally, click **Send test** under **Test delivery** to test the configured endpoint.
- Click **Add channel** to save the webhook notification channel.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083746512/original/F_G7BYkUu-6vI8iYJJnlKNu6r2IlIO2c1w.gif?1792493844)

### **Manage Existing Notification Channels**

The Notification channels dashboard provides a centralized view of configured delivery destinations. You can identify channel types, review whether a channel is associated with a monitor, and control enabled states.

- Click **Notification channels**.
- Review the existing channel cards. Each card identifies the channel type, such as **EMAIL** or **WEBHOOK**, and its monitor usage.
- Use the channel's toggle to enable or disable it.

The tab count reflects the number of configured channels, including channels marked **Not in use**. It does not represent the number of active monitoring alerts.

You can also edit existing channels and delete channels you no longer need.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083746209/original/X594aT2cD4fmcw8-dw7S0lncKY3yFNC68A.png?1792493715)

## 

## **Understand Monitor Status and Daily Checks**

The Monitor dashboard shows whether your AI agents are making sufficient progress toward their targets. Each monitor card combines the measured value, goal, time remaining, and expected pace so you can identify which goals may need attention.

### 

### **Read Monitor Cards and Status Indicators**

Monitor cards display saved evaluation results rather than running a new evaluation every time you visit the page. This provides a consistent view of the latest measured performance.

- Open **Dashboard**.
- Locate the monitor card for the metric you want to review.

- **Metric:** The outcome being tracked, such as Appointments booked.
- **Goal:** The configured target count, cap, or rate.
- **Current value:** Progress measured within the tracking window.
- **Progress percentage:** Progress toward the configured target.
- **Status:** Whether the monitor is on track, behind, at risk, or in another applicable state.
- **Pace for today:** The expected progress for the current point in the tracking window.
- **Tracking window:** Start and end dates, with the remaining time.
- **Daily check schedule:** When the monitor evaluates progress and when it was last checked.
- **Last 7 daily checks:** A compact chart of recent saved evaluations.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083748047/original/oG1CakZkIQTS6MzlpUaVnJ-VV2kdV5CDXA.gif?1792494475)

**Understanding Monitor Status**

Monitor uses status indicators to show how the measured value compares with the configured target and expected pace.

| Status | ​Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **On track** | For a reach-a-number goal, progress is at or above the expected steady pace for the current day. |
| **Behind** | Progress is below the expected pace but within 15% of that pace. |
| **At risk** | Progress is more than 15% below the expected pace, exceeds a configured limit, or falls below an applicable rate target. |
| **Achieved** | The monitored goal has been reached. |
| **Under the number** | Indicates that the measured value is below the specified number for an applicable limit-based comparison. |
| **Scheduled** | The configured tracking window has not started. |
| **Missed** | The monitoring window has ended without the configured goal being met. |

Status calculations depend on the goal's comparison type. Count-based targets use expected pacing, while cap-based and rate-based goals use their configured thresholds.

### 

### **Review the Last Seven Daily Checks**

Daily checks provide a more detailed view of how monitor performance changes over time. Comparing actual results with expected pace helps you understand whether the goal is progressing steadily.

- Select **Dashboard**.
- Locate the monitor you want to inspect.
- In **Last 7 daily checks**, click **View daily checks**.
- Review the **Daily checks** dialog.

The dialog contains a chart with two lines:

- **Actual:** The solid blue line showing the measured metric value at each saved check.
- **Expected pace:** The dotted line showing where the metric should be by that point to finish on time.

Below the chart, a table provides:

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Checked** | The date and time of the saved evaluation. |
| **Value** | The metric value recorded during the check. |
| **Change** | The difference from the previous saved check, including entries such as First check or No change. |

The history shows the last seven saved checks. It can include both scheduled checks and additional checks triggered manually.

---

## **Manage Existing Monitors**

Monitor settings can be updated as tracking goals change. You can adjust targets, modify schedules, review historical versions, and manually refresh measurements without losing the previous monitoring configurations.

### **Edit Monitor Settings and Notifications**

Editing a monitor lets you adjust its tracking configuration without creating an entirely separate metric. Previous versions remain accessible through monitor history.

- Inside the Monitor Dashboard, Find the monitor you want to modify.
- Click the **Edit** (pencil) icon on the monitor card.
- In the **Edit monitor** dialog, update the relevant settings:

  - Comparison type and target value, where supported.
  - Tracking window and repeat settings.
  - AI products included in the calculation.
  - Daily check time and timezone.
  - Notification events and assigned channels.
- Review the updated preview.
- Click **Save changes**.

**Turn Monitor Notifications On or Off**

You can also control notification delivery directly from the monitor card.

- From the **Sub-Account view**, select **AI Agents → Agent Logs → Monitor → Dashboard**.
- Locate the monitor card.
- Click the **bell icon** to turn notifications on or off.

Turning notifications off stops the monitor's email and webhook notifications without deleting the previously configured notification events. Scheduled daily checks continue to run.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083747043/original/USErHJvec1InmFn_K-T55YPyoJkTbdUQZg.png?1792494099)

### **Run a Manual Check**

Manual refresh is useful when you want to review updated progress before the next scheduled evaluation. Running a manual check updates the saved result but does not change the existing daily check schedule.

- From the **Sub-Account view**, select **AI Agents**.
- Click **Agent Logs**.
- Select **Monitor**.
- Open **Dashboard**.
- Find the monitor you want to check.
- Click the **Refresh** icon on the monitor card.
- Review the updated value and status after the check completes.

The new saved check can also appear in the monitor's daily check history.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083747211/original/Kuo41gaTmGLDiUGw3areJTFmrPrkFp26Xg.png?1792494154)

### **View Monitor History and Switch Versions**

Monitor history retains earlier configurations of the same tracked metric. You can review previous targets and activate another version without deleting the saved versions.

- From the Monitor Dashboard, Locate the monitor whose history you want to review.
- Click the **History** icon on its card.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083747627/original/1MT_v6uU46385re2S-u7ZadiSKEFYyYVpQ.png?1792494322)

- In the **History** dialog, review:

  - **ACTIVE NOW:** The currently active version, its goal, progress, status, tracking dates, and product scope.
  - **OTHER VERSIONS:** Previous configurations and their recorded outcomes.
- To switch to an eligible previous version, click **Make active** for that version.

Only one version of a metric is active at a time. Changing the active version does not delete the other saved versions.

The History dialog can also display **Restart** for completed versions.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083747409/original/eZpvaUxCLkoHbM80Oax_-WnoXwGNMmSdlw.png?1792494223)

### **Repeat, Restart, or Finish Monitoring Windows**

Monitoring windows define the period during which a goal is evaluated. You can configure a monitor to repeat automatically or manage it manually after its current window closes.

**Repeat a monitor automatically**

- From the **Sub-Account view**, select **AI Agents**.
- Click **Agent Logs**, then **Monitor**.
- Select **Dashboard**.
- Locate the monitor and click its **Edit** icon.
- Under **Time window**, enable **Repeat this monitor**.
- Click **Save changes**.

When the current tracking window closes, Monitor starts another window of the same duration automatically. The completed window remains in history.

**Restart a completed version**

- From the **Sub-Account view**, select **AI Agents**.
- Click **Agent Logs**, then **Monitor**.
- Open **Dashboard**.
- Find the relevant monitor and click its **History** icon.
- Locate the completed version under **OTHER VERSIONS**.
- Click **Restart** for that version.

**Manage a completed monitor**

When a non-repeating monitoring window ends, its completed card remains visible. The card displays the measured outcome, whether the goal was achieved or missed, and the dates of the completed window.

The completed card provides two actions:

- **Start new:** Begin another monitoring window.
- **Dismiss:** Clear the completed monitor card from the dashboard.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Will Monitor send another at-risk notification if performance recovers and later falls behind again?**

Yes. If the monitor leaves the at-risk state and subsequently becomes at risk again, another at-risk notification is sent when that event is enabled.

**Q: Can I use the same email or webhook notification channel for multiple monitors?**

Yes. A notification channel can be assigned to more than one monitor, allowing you to reuse an existing delivery destination.

**Q: What happens when I create a new monitor for a metric that already has one?**

The newly created monitor becomes the active version for that metric. The previous version remains available in History and can be made active again.

**Q: Do daily progress emails continue until the tracking window closes?**

Yes. When daily progress emails are enabled, they continue through the final day of the monitoring window. You can schedule them at the daily check time or another selected time.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Agent Logs Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007657-agent-logs-overview)

- [Agent Logs Metrics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007732-agent-logs-metrics)

- [Conversation AI - Agent Logs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007996-conversation-ai-agent-logs)

- [Voice AI Performance Reports](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007984-voice-ai-performance-reports)

title_en: Rentals - Additional Fees
source_md:
This article explains how **Additional Fees** work in HighLevel Rentals — what they are, how to create and manage them globally, how to attach them to listings, and how they appear to customers during booking. Additional Fees allow you to automatically include mandatory charges such as cleaning, service, resort, or damage waiver fees in rental bookings. With flexible pricing options, listing-specific overrides, and independent tax configuration, you can manage these charges without incorporating them into the base rental price.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Additional Fees?](#What-Are-Additional-Fees)
- [Key Benefits of Additional Fees](#Key-Benefits-of-Additional-Fees)
- [Additional Fee Pricing Types](#Additional-Fee-Pricing-Types)
- [How to Create a Global Fee Template](#How-to-Create-a-Global-Fee-Template)
- [How to View and Manage Additional Fees](#How-to-View-and-Manage-Additional-Fees)
- [How to Attach Fees to a Listing](#How-to-Attach-Fees-to-a-Listing)
- [How to Override a Fee at Listing Level](#How-to-Override-a-Fee-at-Listing-Level)
- [How Fees Appear in the Booking Widget](#How-Fees-Appear-in-the-Booking-Widget)
- [Additional Fees in Booking Summaries and Payments](#Additional-Fees-in-Booking-Summaries-and-Payments)
- [Fees and Taxes](#Fees-and-Taxes)
- [Inactive Fee Behavior](#Inactive-Fee-Behavior)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Additional Fees?**

Additional Fees are **mandatory charges** that are automatically applied to every booking for a listing where the fee is active and attached. Unlike optional add-ons, customers cannot remove or opt out of Additional Fees — they are automatically included in the booking total.

Common examples include:

- Cleaning fees
- Service fees
- Resort fees
- Damage waiver fees

Fees are configured as **reusable global templates** and can be attached to multiple listings. Each listing can also override the fee amount independently without affecting other listings.

Additional Fees can be configured as flat amounts or percentages of the base rental subtotal. Taxes can also be applied to fees independently of the base rental price, allowing businesses to maintain clear financial records.

Once attached to a listing, applicable Additional Fees are included in the total shown to customers and are displayed as separate charges in booking and invoice details.

```
Important: Additional Fees are mandatory and cannot be made optional for customers. Applicable fees are included in the booking total shown before checkout, helping customers understand their charges before completing a reservation.
```

---

## **Key Benefits of Additional Fees**

Additional Fees help rental businesses manage charges that are separate from the base rental price. Instead of manually adding expenses or adjusting rental rates to account for them, administrators can configure reusable fees that are automatically included in applicable bookings.

- **Automatic Fee Application:** Apply mandatory charges such as cleaning, service, or resort fees to every applicable booking without manual adjustments.
- **Reusable Fee Templates:** Create a fee once in the global catalog and associate it with multiple rental listings.
- **Flexible Pricing:** Choose between fixed amounts and percentage-based fees, including charges calculated per booking or per booking unit.
- **Listing-Specific Overrides:** Customize fee amounts for individual listings without changing the global template or affecting other listings.
- **Independent Tax Configuration:** Configure taxes on Additional Fees separately from the base rental price.
- **Transparent Booking Experience:** Display mandatory charges in the customer's booking total before checkout to reduce unexpected pricing differences.
- **Clear Payment Records:** Display fees as separate line items in booking summaries and invoices for easier review and reconciliation.

---

## **Additional Fee Pricing Types**

Additional Fees support flexible pricing options to accommodate different rental business requirements. You can charge a fixed amount for each booking, calculate charges based on rental duration, or apply a percentage of the base rental subtotal.

### **Flat Amount**

A Flat Amount fee applies a fixed monetary charge. Flat fees support two pricing units:

- **Per Booking:** A single fixed charge applied once per booking, regardless of the rental duration.
- **Per Booking Unit:** A charge applied for each booking unit, such as an hour, day, week, or month, based on the listing's configured booking unit.

**Example:** If a cleaning fee is configured as $50 per booking, the customer pays $50 regardless of the rental duration.

If an equipment maintenance fee is configured as $10 per booking unit and the customer books three daily units, the total maintenance fee is $30.

### **Percentage**

Percentage-based fees are calculated as a percentage of the base rental subtotal. This is useful for service charges or other fees that should increase or decrease with the rental value.

**Example:** If a rental has a base subtotal of $1,000 and a service fee of 5%, the service fee is $50.

| **Pricing Type** | **Example** | **Fee Charged** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flat - Per Booking | $50 cleaning fee | $50 once per booking |
| Flat - Per Booking Unit | $10/day for 3 daily units | $30 |
| Percentage | 5% of a $1,000 rental subtotal | $50 |

```
Percentage fees are calculated on the base rental subtotal, excluding other Additional Fees, taxes, and security deposits. They do not compound with other fees. When advanced pricing rules or discounts are applied, review the final fee amount in the booking summary.
```

---

## **How to Create a Global Fee Template**

Global fee templates are reusable configurations that can be attached to one or more rental listings. Creating fees from the global catalog helps maintain consistent charges across listings while reducing repetitive setup.

### **Step 1: Navigate to Additional Fees**

Go to **Calendars → Calendar Settings → Rentals → Additional fees**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084322278/original/sf6J03xwL4swswrX6yL-tPsEGj29k8gYzg.png?1793111223)

### **Step 2: Create a New Fee**

Click the **+ New additional fee** button in the top-right corner. The New additional fee modal will appear.

### **Step 3: Fill in the Fee Details**

Configure the following fields:

- **Name (required):** Enter the name that customers will see on the booking page and invoice (e.g., "Cleaning Fee" or "Resort Fee").
- **Status:** Set the fee to Active or Inactive to control whether it applies to new bookings.
- **Price:**Choose between:
  - **Flat amount:** A fixed monetary charge.
  - **Percentage (%):** A percentage of the base rental subtotal.
- **Fee Value:** Enter the amount or percentage based on your selected pricing type.
- **Pricing Unit:**Available when the pricing type is Flat amount. Choose:
  - **Per Booking:** Charge the amount once per booking.
  - **Per Booking Unit:** Charge the amount for each rental booking unit (hour, day, week, or month).
- **Tax:** Taxes can be configured for the fee after it has been created. See the [Fees and Taxes](#Fees-and-Taxes) section for more information.

### **Step 4: Attach to Listings (Optional)**

Before saving, you can attach the fee to one or more listings directly from the creation modal. Select the listings where the fee should apply. This eliminates the need to open each listing separately.

### **Step 5: Save the Fee**

### 

Click **Create additional fees** to save. The fee is now available in the global catalog and can be attached to other rental listings.

---

## **How to View and Manage Additional Fees**

The global Additional fees catalog provides a centralized place to review and manage reusable fee templates. You can check fee amounts, identify associated listings, update fee settings, and manage fee availability without opening each rental listing individually.

Go to **Calendars → Calendar Settings → Rentals → Additional fees**.

The table displays the following columns:

| **Column** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | The fee name shown to customers. |
| **Price** | The configured flat amount or percentage. |
| **Price Unit** | Per booking or per booking unit, where applicable. |
| **Listings Associated** | The listings associated with the fee. |
| **Status** | Whether the fee is Active or Inactive. |
| **Actions** | Options to edit or delete the fee. |

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084322569/original/MwfpMAKvRfX0LJw0lDsBseI1wrS6cFge3Q.png?1793111303)

**Filtering:** Use the **Filters** button to narrow the list by associated listings. This helps you identify the fees configured for a specific rental listing.

**Search:** Use the search bar to find a fee by name.

**Editing a Fee:** Click the **Edit** icon next to a fee to update its name, amount, pricing unit, tax configuration, status, or associated listings. You can add or remove listings directly from the edit modal without opening each listing individually.

Changes to a global fee template apply to associated listings unless a listing-specific amount override has been configured. See [How to Override a Fee at Listing Level](#How-to-Override-a-Fee-at-Listing-Level) for more information.

**Deleting a Fee:** Click the **Delete** icon to remove a fee template from the global catalog.

```
Deleting a global fee template removes it from its associated listings. Existing bookings that already include the fee retain their recorded fee details. Confirm existing-booking behavior before deleting fees used by active bookings.
```

---

## **How to Attach Fees to a Listing**

Additional Fees must be associated with a rental listing before they can be automatically applied to its bookings. You can attach one or more existing global fees from the listing's Inventory & Pricing settings or create a new fee directly from the fee selector.

### **Step 1: Navigate to Listings**

Go to **Calendars → Calendar Settings → Rentals → Listings**.

### **Step 2: Edit a Listing**

Click the **Edit (pencil)** icon next to the listing you want to configure.

### **Step 3: Go to the Pricing Tab**

Select the **Inventory & Pricing** tab, then scroll to the **Additional fees** section.

### **Step 4: Attach a Fee**

Click **+ Additional fee** to open the fee selector. You can:

- Select one or more existing fees from the global catalog using their checkboxes.
- Use the search field to locate a specific fee.
- Choose **Select all** to select all available fees.
- Click **+ New additional fee** to create a new fee from within the listing.

After selecting the required fees, click **Save** to confirm your selection.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084322636/original/IQ5nal7NICarQepc1j5UJ0349oDyT6XQYg.png?1793111337)

Once attached, the fee appears in the listing's Additional fees table. Review the fee name, amount, pricing unit, and status.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084322707/original/0r4F5YuJusL10vljDBYFZ-ULQif5sB3YEw.png?1793111364)

Click **Save changes** on the listing page to save the updated configuration.

```
Tip: You can attach multiple Additional Fees to a single listing. All active fees associated with the listing are automatically applied to applicable new bookings.
```

**To remove a fee from a listing:** Click the **Remove** action next to the fee in the listing's Additional fees table and save the listing changes. This detaches the fee from the selected listing without deleting its global template.

---

## **How to Override a Fee at Listing Level**

By default, an attached fee uses the amount configured in the global template. However, different rental listings may have different operating costs. Listing-level overrides allow you to customize the fee amount for a particular listing without affecting the global template or other listings using the same fee.

### **Step 1: Find the Fee in the Listing**

Open the listing and navigate to **Inventory & Pricing → Additional fees**.

Locate the fee you want to override.

### **Step 2: Edit the Amount**

Click the **Edit (pencil)** icon next to the fee amount.

An override modal will appear with the following information:

- **Fee Name:** Displays the name of the global fee. The name cannot be changed at listing level.
- **Price:** Enter the new amount or percentage for this listing.
- **Reset to Default:** Revert the overridden amount to the value defined in the global fee template.

### 

### **Step 3: Save Changes**

### 

Click **Save changes** to apply the override. The updated amount applies only to the selected listing. Other listings using the same global fee retain their existing fee amounts.

```
A listing-level override changes only the fee amount. It does not change the pricing unit defined by the global fee template.

If the global fee amount is updated after a listing-level override has been configured, the overridden amount remains in effect. Use Reset to default to restore the global fee amount.
```

---

## **How Fees Appear in the Booking Widget**

Additional Fees are displayed to customers before they complete a rental booking. The booking widget includes applicable fees in the total shown to customers, allowing them to review mandatory charges alongside the rental price and other applicable costs.

**Price Summary Display:**

Additional Fees are included in the booking price breakdown and may appear alongside applicable taxes and other charges.

```
Example Booking Summary:

Base Rental Price          $200.00
Additional Fees             $75.00
Taxes                       $23.75
---------------------------------
Total                      $298.75
```

**Important details:**

- Additional Fees are mandatory and cannot be removed or modified by customers during checkout.
- Applicable fees are included in the first booking total shown to the customer.
- Fees contribute to the total amount payable for the booking.
- Applicable taxes and refundable security deposits may also appear in the booking summary.
- Customers can review the charge breakdown before completing their reservation.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084322812/original/KrDFImYOrCwUQCPB-BTZaqxWioGyz2f_oA.png?1793111422)

```
Additional Fees are not added as unexpected charges at checkout. Applicable fees are already included in the displayed booking total before the customer completes payment.
```

---

## **Additional Fees in Booking Summaries and Payments**

In addition to appearing in the customer-facing booking widget, Additional Fees are reflected in rental booking records and invoices. This helps administrators review mandatory charges separately from base rental amounts, taxes, and refundable security deposits.

### **Review Additional Fees in a Booking**

To review Additional Fees associated with a booking:

1. Go to **Calendars → Appointment List View**.
2. Select **Rentals** from the available booking categories.
3. Locate the booking you want to review.
4. Click the **Edit (pencil)** icon to open its details.
5. Review the **Payment Summary** to identify the rental charges and applicable Additional Fees.

The Payment Summary provides a breakdown of the booking's financial details, which may include:

- Base rental charges
- Additional Fees such as cleaning or service fees
- Applicable taxes
- Refundable security deposits
- Total booking amount
- Payments received
- Remaining amount due

### 

### **Additional Fees on Invoices**

Additional Fees appear as identifiable line items on rental invoices rather than being incorporated into the base rental charge. When taxes are applied to Additional Fees, the applicable tax is calculated on the fee amount and shown separately.

This makes it easier for customers and administrators to understand which charges contribute to the booking total.

### **Review Additional Charges After Booking Changes**

When booking details are modified, the Payment Summary may display updated charges or an outstanding balance. Administrators can review the amount due, payment status, and collection information before saving the changes.

For example, a booking may show a pending **Additional charge** when an amount remains to be collected.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084322904/original/hTpVKht3PmLzSPWlKaTef9oEZmcvh-_98g.png?1793111473)

```
A pending Additional charge represents an outstanding payment amount. Review the booking's payment collection settings and status to determine whether further payment action is required. A pending charge is not necessarily caused by an Additional Fee.
```

For additional guidance on booking modifications, refer to [Rentals — Editing a Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006626-rentals-editing-a-booking).

---

## **Fees and Taxes**

Taxes can be applied to Additional Fees independently of the base rental price. This allows businesses to configure the appropriate tax on mandatory charges while keeping fees and their associated taxes distinguishable in booking summaries and invoices.

### **How to Configure Tax on an Additional Fee**

To configure tax on a fee:

1. Navigate to **Calendars → Calendar Settings → Rentals → Additional fees**.
2. Locate the fee you want to configure.
3. Click the **Edit** icon for that fee.
4. Select **Configure tax**.
5. On the linked product configuration page, attach the appropriate tax rate to the fee.
6. Save the tax configuration.

### **How Taxes Are Calculated on Additional Fees**

Tax on an Additional Fee is calculated using the applicable fee amount rather than the base rental price.

For example, if a cleaning fee is $100 and is subject to a 10% exclusive tax rate:

| **Charge** | **Amount** |
| --- | --- |
| Cleaning Fee | $100.00 |
| Tax on Cleaning Fee (10%) | $10.00 |
| **Total Fee Including Tax** | **$110.00** |

The applicable fee tax is included in the total shown to customers during booking and appears separately in the invoice breakdown.

```
Important: Taxes on Additional Fees are configured separately from taxes on the base rental price. This allows businesses to apply the appropriate tax configuration to each charge without combining the fee amount with the rental rate.
```

For more information about rental tax settings, refer to [Rentals — Taxes](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007423-rentals-taxes).

---

## **Inactive Fee Behavior**

Setting an Additional Fee to Inactive allows administrators to stop applying a fee to new bookings without removing the global template or its listing associations. This is useful when a charge is temporarily suspended or no longer required for new reservations.

**What happens when a fee is marked Inactive:**

- The fee remains attached to the listings where it was configured — it is not automatically removed.
- The inactive fee is not applied to new bookings created after the status change.
- Existing confirmed bookings retain the fee amounts previously recorded on those bookings.
- To reactivate the fee, edit its global template and change its status back to **Active**.
- Once reactivated, the fee can be applied to new bookings for its associated listings.

```
Deactivating a fee is different from deleting it. Inactive fee templates remain available in the global catalog and retain their listing associations. Confirm the effect on existing bookings before making changes to fees that have already been charged.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I make an Additional Fee optional for customers?**

No. Additional Fees are mandatory and cannot be made optional. If you need an optional charge that customers can select during booking, use the Add-ons feature instead.

**Q: If I update a global fee template's amount, does it update all listings?**

Yes. Changes to a global template apply to associated listings unless a listing has a listing-level amount override. Listings with overrides retain their customized amounts. Use the **Reset to default** option to restore the global amount.

**Q: Can I override the fee amount for one specific booking?**

Booking-level fee overrides are not currently supported. Fee amount overrides are configured at the listing level.

**Q: Are taxes on Additional Fees included in the customer-facing total?**

Yes. Applicable tax on fees is calculated and included in the total shown to customers. The tax is displayed separately from the fee amount in the booking's financial breakdown and invoice.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Rentals — Overview & How to Get Started](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006649-rentals-overview-how-to-get-started)
- [Rentals — Create & Edit Listings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006579-rentals-create-edit-listings)
- [Rentals — Configuring Pricing & Discounts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006611-rentals-configuring-pricing-discounts)
- [Rentals — Taxes](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007423-rentals-taxes)
- [Rentals — Overview of Bookings](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006622-rentals-overview-of-bookings)
- [Rentals — Editing a Booking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006626-rentals-editing-a-booking)

---

title_en: How to Set Up Different Domain Types in HighLevel: Websites, Email, WordPress & More
source_md:
HighLevel uses domains and subdomains for different products, including Websites, Funnels, WordPress, email sending, Client Portal, and agency branding. Choosing the correct domain type helps you connect the right service without creating conflicting DNS records.

This guide explains the different domain types used in HighLevel and helps you determine which one you need. For DNS records and step-by-step configuration, follow the linked setup guide for the specific HighLevel product you are connecting.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is a Domain?](#What-is-a-Domain?)
  - [What are Root & Sub-Domains](#What-are-Root-&-Sub-Domains)
  - [Seamlessly Connect Domains with Domain Connect](#Seamlessly-Connect-Domains-with-Domain-Connect)
    - [Manual Option](#Manual-Option)
- [Places to Add Domains](#Places-to-Add-Domains-to-in-HighLevel)
  - [Whitelabel Domain](#Whitelabel-Domain)
  - [API or Branded Domain](#API-or-Branded-Domain)
  - [Sites (Settings > Domains)](#Sites-(Settings-%3E-Domains))
  - [Email Sending Domain](#Email-Sending-Domain)
  - [Client Portal Domain (Communities, Courses)](#Client-Portal-Domain-(Communities,-Courses))
  - [WordPress](#WordPress)
- [Domain Glossary - Key Words to Know](#Domain-Glossary---Key-Words-to-Know)
- [Troubleshooting](#Troubleshooting)
  - [1. Check for Duplicate A Records:](#1.-Check-for-Duplicate-A-Records%3A)
  - [2. Confirm DNS Propagation](#2.-Confirm-DNS-Propagation)
  - [3. Review DNS Settings for Accuracy:](#3.-Review-DNS-Settings-for-Accuracy%3A)
  - [4. Verify Domain DNS Integration:](#4.-Verify-Domain-DNS-Integration%3A)
  - [5. Consider Other Potential Causes:](#5.-Consider-Other-Potential-Causes%3A)
  - [6. Seek Additional Assistance:](#6.-Seek-Additional-Assistance%3A)
- [FAQ](#FAQ)
  - [What If I do not have a domain?](#What-If-I-do-not-have-a-domain?)
  - [Can I use an existing domain for my email?](#Can-I-use-an-existing-domain-for-my-email?)
  - [Can I use WIX for my Dedicated Domain?](#Can-I-use-WIX-for-my-Dedicated-Domain?)
  - [My Cname record is not being recognized in Cloudflare.](#My-Cname-record-is-not-being-recognized-in-Cloudflare.)
  - [What if I have an existing domain?](#What-if-I-have-an-existing-domain?)

---

## **Which Domain Do I Need?**

Different HighLevel products use domains for different purposes. Identifying what you want to publish, brand, or authenticate helps you choose the correct domain configuration before making DNS changes.

| Domain Type | Use It For |
| --- | --- |
| **Website/Funnel Domain** | Publishing Websites, Funnels, Stores, Blogs, and other supported Sites experiences |
| **HighLevel-Purchased Domain** | Using a domain purchased and managed directly through HighLevel |
| **White Label Domain** | Providing an agency-branded HighLevel application/login URL |
| **API/Branded Domain** | Supporting applicable branded HighLevel services |
| **Dedicated Sending Domain** | Authenticating a domain used to send email through LC Email |
| **Client Portal Domain** | Providing a branded URL for the Client Portal |
| **WordPress Domain** | Publishing a WordPress site hosted through HighLevel |

# 

```
Important: The DNS records required for one domain type should not automatically be reused for another. Follow the setup instructions HighLevel provides for the specific product you are connecting.
```

---

# What is a Domain?

A domain serves as the digital address for online services like websites, email hosting, and more, by mapping them to IP addresses through DNS. Domain names are essential for your online presence, enhancing website accessibility and enabling email communication.

Domains are crucial for website hosting, white-label branding, configuring branded/API domains, email setup, and the Client portal. They form the foundation upon which HighLevel users build their digital presence.

## What are Root & Sub-Domains

When working with domains, it's important to distinguish between a root domain and a subdomain.

- **Root Domain**(Example: “mywebsite.com”)

  - The root domain is the primary address of your website, appearing after "www." in a URL (e.g., in "www.mywebsite.com," the root domain is "mywebsite.com"). It serves as the main entry point to your website.
- **Subdomain** (Example: "help.domain.com")

  - Subdomains are extensions of your root domain, directing users to specific sections or areas within your online infrastructure (e.g., "help.domain.com" for support). This allows for separate content, landing pages, and marketing campaigns without affecting the primary site. This setup is useful for ads, promotions, and utilizing different SEO strategies.

```
IMPORTANT NOTE: Be careful when adding root domains. Many users accidentally break their existing mailbox or site by adding a root domain already in use. We recommend adding a sub-domain if your root domain is used somewhere else.
```

---

## Seamlessly Connect Domains with Domain Connect

Domain Connect can automatically configure DNS records with supported domain providers, reducing the need to manually create records. When Domain Connect is available for your provider, follow the prompts in HighLevel to authorize and complete the connection.

To see more information about seamlessly connecting domains, please visit [How to Use the Domain Connect Feature](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000734-how-to-use-the-domain-connect-feature-)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095806/original/hrpCoz1Kx3xl9cE9J2HRAABgfYYjIdiccA.png?1717515282)

### Manual Option

**If your domain provider is not Google, Cloudflare, or GoDaddy**, manual DNS configuration is required. The system simplifies this process by generating the necessary record values for you to input into your domain provider's system. This ensures seamless integration of your domain with HighLevel, supporting branded domains, websites/funnels, dedicated domains, and the client portal.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095809/original/82lhQooK-BZRhn3IMxjM7GcSDZbSWjjPNg.png?1717515282)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095807/original/a8TzYf-3dnw-VbAwcvB557Klucd9jSYIRA.png?1717515282)

1) Now you open your DNS provider of choice and add the records in. Adding records are much the same, with some variation based on the provider. Go to your DNS manager and click add record.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095808/original/NeCo_2dJkC96cNq4SD_gjAtSvrk-e1PSEg.png?1717515282)

2) Select the record type provided by HighLevel

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095819/original/Mf13PeAVBfyHw2UVIcqy9npH7W7b2VFhmA.png?1717515282)

3) Input the Hostname into the “Name” field and Value/Target into the “target field”

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095817/original/c1IMDbugE355g-RMxp50EGWBTEHgDNHCuQ.png?1717515282)

4) Save the record. If utilizing Cloudflare the Proxy Status will need to be toggled off.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095821/original/4M9zVsq-xWiE6yTlyTBccTJRD7V3pRHMwQ.png?1717515282)

To learn more about this manual process, go [here](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001153720-how-to-set-up-root-domain-subdomain-for-your-funnels-websites-).

---

# Places to Add Domains to in HighLevel

Within HighLevel, there are many places to add a domain, let’s briefly explore each one. We will provide resources to learn more.

## Whitelabel Domain

Whitelabeling your desktop web app ensures that your customers interact with your domain instead of the default one. Simply follow four steps: create a CNAME in your DNS records, configure it in your HighLevel Agency account, upload your agency logo, and update your agency Terms & Conditions. Once your DNS record propagates, your customers

can access the app using your domain, seeing your branding elements like logo and terms & conditions.

```
A sub-domain is Recommended for whitelabeling. Most Commonly agencies will use "app" as the sub-domain for their whitelabel desktop app.
```

*Navigate to the Agency View > Settings  > Company Settings > Whitelabel*

For more information on setting up your Whitelabel Domain please visit [How to Set Up a Whitelabel Domain](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982207-how-to-set-up-a-whitelabel-domain-for-the-desktop-web-app)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080577419/original/pJtVMPba3s8y1kMogTs1wQOrer8YwHP4cg.png?1789034409)

---

## API or Branded Domain

Enhance your brand visibility and link deliverability by customizing system-generated links with our API/Branded Domains. By doing so, you can personalize links for forms, surveys, calendars, and more.

Custom API domains allow for branding of system-generated links, improving brand recognition and link deliverability. Configure API domains at the agency level company settings to establish a default branded domain for all sub-accounts.

*Navigate to the Agency View > Settings  > Company Settings > White Label*

At the sub-account level to customize domains for individual clients a branded domain can be set up. This will be done under the sub-account settings, within the business profile.

*Navigate to the Sub-Account > Settings  > Business Profile > Branded Domain*

*![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080577998/original/7GLW_9OzvZCCtGvqTJYkHNOAEBITvFpeOA.png?1789034623)*

For more information on the API/Branded Domain setup please view [How to Configure Brand System Generated Links](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001143244-how-to-configure-brand-system-generated-links-api-domain-)

```
For both the API and Branded Domains, utilize a sub-domain as utilizing a root domain here will cause your domain to point away from your website.
```

---

## Sites (Settings > Domains)

Sites Domains provide the public URLs used for HighLevel Websites, Funnels, Stores, Blogs, and other supported Sites experiences.

Manage these domains from:

**Sub-Account → Settings → Domains**

When connecting an external domain, follow the DNS records displayed by HighLevel for that configuration. After the required records are added at your DNS provider, return to HighLevel to verify and connect the domain.

## Domains Purchased Through HighLevel

Domains purchased through HighLevel can be managed directly within the platform, reducing the need to use a separate registrar for routine domain management. Use this option when the domain itself was purchased through HighLevel rather than connected from an external provider. For setup and management instructions, see Configure & Connect Domains Purchased Through HighLevel.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080578348/original/k2kvxh9HkteyBNSXoh_ei3TO6tXSnGLNcg.png?1789034734)

*Navigate to the Sub-Account > Settings  > Domains*

For more information on how to add a domain to a website please visit [How to Set Up a Root/Subdomain for Your Funnels/Websites](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001153720-how-to-set-up-root-domain-subdomain-for-your-funnels-websites-)

---

## Email Sending Domain

To maximize email marketing impact, prioritize sender reputation and deliverability. A dedicated sending domain in the LC Email system gives you control over email communications, enhancing brand credibility and reducing spam filter risks. This setup is ideal for customized notification emails and targeting specific categories, ensuring efficient delivery. To avoid conflicts with existing email services, configure your dedicated domain using a subdomain. Dedicated sending domains are key to maintaining a positive sender reputation and achieving effective email marketing with LC Email.

A Dedicated Sending Domain authenticates the domain used to send email through LC Email. Using a dedicated sending domain separates email authentication from domains used for Websites, Funnels, Client Portal, or other HighLevel products. Configure a sending domain from: Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain and IP → Add Domain HighLevel generates the DNS records required for the sending domain. Add the displayed records at your DNS provider, then return to HighLevel to verify the configuration. Always use the DNS values generated for your domain rather than copying records from another domain or an older configuration.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095829/original/hcq0UeChnG-9hDKlXxqS5zYyMdjHmZ4xNA.png?1717515282)

*For agency level email services navigate to the Agency View > Settings  > Email Services > Dedicated domain*

*For sub-account level email services navigate to the Sub-Account > Settings  > Email Services > Dedicated Domain*

For more information the Dedicated Email Sending Domain setup process please visit [How to Set Up a Dedicated Sending Domain](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001226115-how-to-set-up-a-dedicated-sending-domain-lc-email-)

---

## Client Portal Domain (Communities, Courses)

The client portal transforms client-business interactions by providing a secure, centralized platform in HighLevel for your Affiliates, Membership and Community management. The portal functions as a dynamic interface, centralizing affiliate manager commissions, community interactions, and membership course activity. It simplifies client engagement with custom domains and branding options, reinforcing brand-client relationships. Enhanced communication and client autonomy lead to greater satisfaction and loyalty.

This document guides you through setting up and customizing the portal to meet specific business needs, enabling clients to take autonomous actions.

Navigate to the Sub-Account > Sites  > ClientPortal > Settings

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080578699/original/qWhwx9HIyh0rgRbb_4jJECSA3jiZwhgqwQ.png?1789034831)

*![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080578814/original/FpK2O-Rwtgc9XCLlJg5nIcA3nOUS4yXNWA.png?1789034873)*

For more information on the Client Portal Setup please visit [How to Set Up the Client Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000193-how-to-set-up-the-client-portal-)

---

## WordPress

WordPress Hosting allows for the migration of an existing WordPress site, or for a new site to be created. After connecting the domain, users gain access to essential features like the WordPress Dashboard, User Management, Backup & Restore, and Advanced Settings.

Whether users are starting a new website or managing existing ones, this guide provides valuable instructions and insights to streamline the WordPress setup process effectively for your clients.

A WordPress Domain provides the public URL for a WordPress website hosted through HighLevel. WordPress domain routing is managed separately from standard Sites Domains. Go to: Sub-Account → Sites → WordPress Open the applicable WordPress site and use its domain-management options to connect the domain. Follow the DNS records generated for that specific WordPress configuration

For more information on Wordpress Domain setup please visit [Getting Started With Wordpress Client Side Setup Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001199648-getting-started-with-wordpress-client-side-setup-guide)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095831/original/xBtwh9LbbbyeTDtR7LOC2Tjixy-NKbmPwg.png?1717515282)

---

# Domain Glossary - Key Words to Know

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Example | Description |
| Domain | www.gohighlevel.com | The digital address for online services like websites, email hosting, and more |
| Root Domain | gohighlevel.com | The primary address of your website, appearing after "www." in a URL (e.g., in "www.gohighlevel.com," the root domain is "gohighlevel.com"). It serves as the main entry point to your website. |
| Subdomain | help.gohighlevel.com | Subdomains are extensions of your root domain, directing users to specific sections or areas within your online infrastructure (e.g., "help.domain.com" for support). |
| Hostname |  | The name/value utilized in the record, typically the subdomain utilized. This is what allows subdomains such as “help.gohighlevel.com” to act independently from “www.highlevel.com” |
| Data/Target/Value |  | The value which tells the URL to display intended website data. |
| Nameservers | GoDaddy, Cloudflare, Google, etc. | The directory which organizes and controls the DNS records. This is what tells the internet which Domain Provider, e.g. Godaddy, Cloudflare, etc, is controlling the Domain |
| DNS (Dedicated Name System) |  | The records that tell the internet when a certain URL is visited to populate a website, and allows email providers to send emails from the domain name. |
| TXT |  | TXT records are used for sending emails to prevent spam, and for protecting the domain by creating a domain verification. |
| MX |  | The Mail Exchange (MX) records tell emails where to be routed to. This is utilized to send and receive emails within HighLevel. |
| CNAME |  | A Cname record points to another domain. These records are commonly utilized when creating sub-domains |
| A Record |  | An A record points to an IP address that is hosting your website. These records are commonly utilized for your root domain to point to your primary website. |
| DMARC |  | A DMARC record is a TXT record that prevents email spoofing protecting your email sending from scammers and unauthorized use of the domain. |

---

# Troubleshooting Domain Connections

Domain connection issues are commonly caused by incorrect DNS records, conflicting records, incomplete DNS propagation, or records being added at a provider that is not currently managing the domain's nameservers.

If a domain is not connecting:

- Confirm which HighLevel product the domain is being connected to.
- Compare the records at your DNS provider with the DNS records currently displayed in HighLevel.
- Check for conflicting A or CNAME records using the same hostname.
- Confirm that you are editing DNS at the provider responsible for the domain's current nameservers.
- Allow applicable time for DNS changes to propagate.
- Return to HighLevel and retry the domain verification.

If the issue continues, follow the dedicated troubleshooting documentation for the applicable Website/Funnel, WordPress, Email, Client Portal, White Label, or other domain configuration.

---

# FAQ

## What If I do not have a domain?

You can purchase a domain directly through HighLevel or through a supported external domain registrar. After purchasing the domain, connect it to the applicable HighLevel product using that product's domain setup process.

## Can I use an existing domain for my email?

You can set up a dedicated domain for an existing domain. It is advised to utilize a sub-domain when setting up your domain for email sending within HighLevel to prevent it from affecting your current email services.

## Can I use WIX for my Dedicated Domain?

Wix does not allow for multiple MX records to be added of the same priority. In order to use a domain that is connected to Wix the nameservers will need to be changed to point to another domain host. For more information please see: [LC Email / Mailgun replies not working when using WIX as the domain provider](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001188738-lc-email-mailgun-replies-not-working-when-using-wix-as-the-domain-provider)

## My Cname record is not being recognized in Cloudflare.

Make sure the Cname record that is added into Cloudflare has the proxy toggled off in order to allow the record to propagate.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155027095826/original/MFQYCch3__QKBwKhSpCrSniblWBKnpgYCA.png?1717515282)

## What if I have an existing domain?

Yes. If your existing root domain is already connected to a website or another service that you want to keep, use an appropriate subdomain for the HighLevel product when supported. This allows the existing service and the new HighLevel experience to operate independently.

This article explains how to use the AI Image Generation action in workflows to create images with AI. You’ll find step-by-step configuration instructions, details on available models and settings, how to access the generated image, practical use cases, and answers to common questions.

```
Note: This is a premium action. Using this action will incur additional charges per execution.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is AI Image Generation Action in Workflows?](#What-is-AI-Image-Generation-Action-in-Workflows?)
- [Key Benefits of AI Image Generation Action](#Key-Benefits-of-AI-Image-Generation-Action)
- [Action Details](#Action-Details)
- [How to Use the AI Image Generation Action](#How-to-Use-the-AI-Image-Generation-Action)

- [Use Cases](#Use-Cases)
