title_en: Discover Courses and Offers in HighLevel Client Portal
source_md:
Discover helps you show your courses and offers to learners directly inside the HighLevel Client Portal. Instead of sharing a separate purchase link every time you create something new, you can make your courses and offers available in one place where learners can explore and purchase them. Learners can search for courses, view prices, and choose what they want to learn next. You can also decide which courses and offers appear in Discover.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Discover for Courses and Offers?](#What-is-Discover-for-Courses-and-Offers?)
- [Key Benefits of Discover for Courses and Offers](#Key-Benefits-of-Discover-for-Courses-and-Offers)
- [Understanding the Discover Page](#Understanding-the-Discover-Page)
- [How Course and Offer Visibility Works in Discover](#How-Course-and-Offer-Visibility-Works-in-Discover)
- [What Happens When a Course Appears in More Than One Listing?](#What-Happens-When-a-Course-Appears-in-More-Than-One-Listing?)
- [How Learners Can Search and Filter Courses](#How-Learners-Can-Search-and-Filter-Courses)
- [How Learners Can Purchase Courses and Offers From Discover](#How-Learners-Can-Purchase-Courses-and-Offers-From-Discover)
- [How to Set Up Discover for Courses and Offers](#How-to-Set-Up-Discover-for-Courses-and-Offers)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Discover for Courses and Offers?**

Discover is a feature in the HighLevel Client Portal that helps learners find new courses, course bundles, and communities.

The **Client Portal** is the place where your customers or learners log in to access their courses, communities, and other resources.

For example, imagine you sell three online courses. A learner purchases your first course and logs in to the Client Portal to start learning. With Discover enabled, that learner can also find your other available courses and purchase one that interests them.

You control which courses and offers are displayed using the **Show in Discover** setting.

**Discover has two main tabs:**

- **Communities:** Shows communities that learners can explore and join.
- **Courses:** Shows individual courses and bundles that learners can explore and purchase.

An **offer** is a product you create to sell access to one or more courses. In Discover, offers appear as **Bundles**.

---

## **Understanding the Discover Page**

The Discover page is where learners can browse the courses, bundles, and communities available to them. Understanding how this page works helps you decide how your content should be displayed and what learners will see when they visit.

### **Communities and Courses Tabs**

At the top of the Discover page, learners can switch between two tabs.

**Communities**

This tab shows available communities.

Each community card can display:

- Community name
- Number of members
- Membership price, such as Free or a monthly fee

Learners can browse the communities they are interested in joining.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609209/original/CP_yX-N8KrUn4dDMK6g2FW3rzckWryfqBw.png?1792383767)

**Courses**

This tab shows available individual courses and course bundles.

Each listing appears as a card with basic information to help learners decide whether they want to explore it.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609298/original/e0hzAKZU5-g8aqlVZoy3uOazoh0vkhsWqg.png?1792384083)**

---

### **Understanding Course Cards**

A course card is the small preview box learners see when browsing Discover.

Depending on the course, it may display:

- **Thumbnail:** The image representing the course.
- **Title:** The name of the course.
- **Price:** How much the course costs, or whether it is free.
- **Language:** The language used in the course.
- **Difficulty:** Whether the course is suitable for beginners, intermediate learners, or advanced learners.
- **Topic:** The subject covered by the course.

Learners can move their mouse over an individual course card to see more information, including the course description.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609356/original/mIZlycMPWMjg79P-r1VBVb62tycxsgxvVg.png?1792384293)**

```
Note: Offers are displayed with a Bundle label so learners can tell the difference between an individual course and an offer.
```

---

## **How Course and Offer Visibility Works in Discover**

Enabling Discover does not automatically make all your courses and offers visible. You need to choose which products you want learners to find.

HighLevel provides a **Show in Discover** setting for individual courses and published offers.

When the setting is turned on, the selected course or offer can appear in Discover.

When the setting is turned off, that particular course or offer is not listed through Discover.

### 

### **Showing Individual Courses**

You can choose to display an individual course directly in Discover.

For example, if you sell a beginner photography course, you can enable Show in Discover so learners who have not enrolled can find it while browsing.

This setting is available in the course's **Pricing** tab, where you also configure how much learners pay for the course.

Individual course pricing can include:

- **Free:** Learners do not need to pay for the course.
- **One Time:** Learners pay once to purchase the course.
- **Recurring:** Learners make repeated payments based on the configured pricing.

The available pricing options depend on the course pricing features supported in your account.

### 

### **Showing Offers as Bundles**

You can also show published offers in Discover.

An offer lets you sell access to course content as a product. For example, you might create an offer that includes multiple courses for one price.

When an offer appears in Discover, learners see it as a **Bundle**.

This helps learners recognize that they are purchasing an offer rather than an individual course.

```
Important: The offer must be published before you can make it available through the Show in Discover option.
```

## **What Happens When a Course Appears in More Than One Listing?**

Sometimes you may sell a course individually and also include that same course in an offer.

For example:

- You sell **Photography Basics** as an individual course for $30.
- You also create a **Photography Starter Bundle** containing Photography Basics and another course for $50.

If Photography Basics is already listed in Discover and you try to list the bundle, HighLevel may display an **Overlapping discover listings** warning.

This warning lets you know that a course included in the offer is already available in Discover through its individual pricing.

You will see two options:

- **Dismiss:** Close the warning without confirming the overlapping listing.
- **Confirm:** Continue with the offer listing even though the course is already available separately.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609542/original/hjkn_gqmnytu3SC3q8dsNNauyFy1xRScig.png?1792384942)**

```
Tip: If your course and bundle have different pricing or provide different value, showing both may make sense. Review your pricing before confirming so learners understand what they are purchasing.
```

---

## **How Learners Can Search and Filter Courses**

Discover includes search and filter options to help learners find courses that match their interests. These tools are especially helpful when you have several courses or offers available.

### 

### **Searching for a Course**

Learners can use the search bar at the top of the Client Portal to search for communities and courses.

For example, someone interested in photography can search for a photography-related course instead of scrolling through every available listing.

### 

### **Filtering Courses**

On the Courses tab, learners can use the following filters:

- **Free:** Show only courses and bundles that are available for free.
- **Language:** Find courses available in a preferred language.
- **Difficulty:** Find courses based on their experience level.
- **Topic:** Find courses related to a particular subject.

For example, a learner who is new to photography can use the Difficulty filter to look for beginner-level courses.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609583/original/j6pgiIOyA2BMBiSZxZjZ0RtulbtLDv9j2Q.png?1792385020)**

---

## **How Learners Can Purchase Courses and Offers From Discover**

When learners find something they want to purchase, they can open its checkout page directly from Discover. This makes it easier to move from exploring content to enrolling in a course or purchasing a bundle.

A **checkout page** is where learners review the course or offer they selected, enter their details, and continue with the purchase.

To purchase a course or offer:

1. Log in to the **Client Portal**.
2. Click **Discover** in the left sidebar.
3. Select the **Courses** tab.
4. Browse the available courses and bundles.
5. Click the course or bundle you want.
6. Review its details and price on the checkout page.
7. Enter the required information, such as your name and email address.
8. Click **Proceed to checkout** and follow the remaining instructions to complete the purchase.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609630/original/B3fJQhUoQbESYS1r0QUirfNlB4MN3ED61w.png?1792385106)**

---

## **How to Set Up Discover for Courses and Offers**

Before learners can browse your courses and offers, you need to enable Discover and choose which products should appear. The setup involves a few settings in your HighLevel account.

Follow the steps below in order to make sure Discover is available and your courses are displayed correctly.

### 

### **Step 1: Enable Discover in Labs**

First, enable the Discover feature in HighLevel Labs.

**Labs** is where HighLevel makes certain new features available before they become generally available to all accounts.

1. Log in to your **HighLevel account**.
2. Open **Labs**.
3. Navigate to **Subaccounts**.
4. Find **Discovery of Course and Offers**.
5. Enable the feature for the sub-account where you want to use it.

Once the feature is enabled, you can continue configuring Discover.

```
Note: These instructions apply to the Labs release described here. The location and availability of this feature may change after its wider release.
```

### 

### **Step 2: Enable Discover in Client Portal Settings**

Next, allow learners to access Discover from the Client Portal.

Even if you have enabled the feature in Labs, you still need to enable the Discover app in your Client Portal settings.

1. Switch to the **sub-account** where your courses are located.
2. From the left menu, click **Memberships**.
3. Open **Client Portal**.
4. Select **Settings**.
5. Find the **App Permissions** area.
6. Locate **Discover** in the list of apps.
7. Check the box next to Discover to enable it.
8. Save your changes.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609669/original/NEfNL314udYY0VELwtGnbPO-7aaw71jLjw.png?1792385170)**

After saving, learners can access Discover from the sidebar of their Client Portal.

```
Important: This step enables the Discover page. It does not automatically display all your courses. You will choose which courses and offers to display in Steps 4 and 5.
```

  

### 

### **Step 3: Make Discover the First Page Learners See (Optional)**

You can choose which page opens first when learners enter their Client Portal.

This is called the **default landing page**.

For example, if Discover is the default landing page, learners will see the available courses and communities first instead of having to select Discover from the sidebar.

To set Discover as the default landing page:

1. Go to **Memberships → Client Portal → Settings**.
2. Scroll to **Select default landing page**.
3. Open the dropdown menu.
4. Select **Discover**.
5. Click **Save Settings**.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609695/original/4t62s2q9utcemRV6vv_-k7fFY4GdUh9ilA.png?1792385236)**

```
Note: This step is optional. If you do not set Discover as the default landing page, learners can still open it from the Client Portal sidebar.
```

  

### 

### **Step 4: Show an Individual Course in Discover**

Now choose which individual courses you want learners to find.

Before starting, make sure you have created a course and configured its pricing using the available Course Pricing options.

To show a course in Discover:

1. In your HighLevel sub-account, click **Memberships**.
2. Navigate to **Courses**.
3. Open the course you want to display.
4. Select **Pricing** from the course menu.
5. Check that your course has the correct pricing:

   - **Free** if learners can access it without payment.
   - **One Time** if learners pay once.
   - **Recurring** if learners make recurring payments.
6. Find the **Show in Discover** option.
7. Turn the toggle **ON**.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609753/original/JcZYiTwRkE93jMWdawO8euQhmic10LvVkA.png?1792385304)**

Once enabled, the course can appear in Discover for learners who have not enrolled in it.

```
Tip: If you do not see the Pricing tab, check whether direct Course Pricing is available in your account. You can learn more in Course Pricing: Sell Courses Without an Offer.
```

### 

### **Step 5: Show a Published Offer in Discover**

If you have created an offer, you can also make it visible in Discover.

Offers appear as Bundles, so learners can browse packaged courses alongside individual courses.

Before starting, make sure the offer has been created and published.

To show an offer in Discover:

1. Go to **Memberships → Courses**.
2. Open the relevant course and select **Offers**, or open the appropriate offer editor.
3. Select the published offer you want to display.
4. Find **Show in Discover** in the offer settings.
5. Turn the toggle **ON**.
6. If an overlapping listing warning appears, review the course mentioned in the message.
7. Click **Confirm** if you want to continue with the overlapping listing.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083609796/original/fjZm6tcH-qlmJuUSPqrWhR5xcEOJjmpvIw.png?1792385344)**

Your published offer can now appear in Discover with a Bundle label.

### 

### **Step 6: Check What Learners See**

After setup, it's a good idea to check the Discover page from a learner's point of view.

This helps you confirm that your courses and offers are displayed correctly before learners begin browsing.

1. Open your **Client Portal**.
2. Log in with a learner account that has not already enrolled in the course you want to check.
3. Click **Discover** in the sidebar.
4. Open the **Courses** tab.
5. Look for the course or bundle you enabled.
6. Check that the title, thumbnail, price, and course information are correct.
7. Try the filters to check how the course appears.
8. Click the course or bundle to confirm that its checkout page opens.

If a course is missing, check that the Discover app is enabled and that Show in Discover is turned on for the course or published offer.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why can't I see Discover in my Client Portal?**

A: Check that Discover has been enabled in Labs and that its checkbox is selected in Client Portal App Permissions. Save your settings and refresh the portal. Availability may depend on the feature rollout.

**Q: I enabled Discover, but my courses are not showing. What should I do?**

A: Opening the Discover app does not automatically display every course. Go to the course's Pricing tab and turn on Show in Discover. Also check that pricing is configured and that you are testing with a learner who has not already enrolled.

**Q: Will all my courses appear automatically when I turn on Discover?**

A: No. You decide which courses and published offers appear by enabling Show in Discover for each one.

**Q: Can I display a free course in Discover?**

A: Yes. Courses configured with the Free pricing option can be displayed in Discover when the required visibility setting is enabled.

**Q: Can I sell a course without creating an offer?**

A: Yes, if direct Course Pricing is available in your HighLevel account. You can set a price in the course's Pricing tab and enable Show in Discover.

**Q: Why am I seeing an Overlapping discover listings warning?**

A: This warning appears when an offer includes a course that is already discoverable through its individual pricing. Review both listings before deciding whether to confirm the offer.

**Q: Can I turn off Discover for a course later?**

A: Yes. Open the course's Pricing tab and turn off Show in Discover to stop listing that course through Discover. For offers, use the corresponding toggle in the offer settings.

**Q: Do I have to make Discover my default landing page?**

A: No. This is optional. Learners can still open Discover from their Client Portal sidebar when the app is enabled.

**Q: Is Discover the same as GoKollab Discover?**

A: No. Client Portal Discover helps your learners find courses, offers, and communities through your Client Portal. GoKollab Discover is a separate marketplace experience for discovering creators and their content.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [App Permissions in Client Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002136-app-permissions-in-client-portal-enabling-disabling-a-child-app)
- [Course Pricing: Sell Courses Without an Offer](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008978-course-pricing-sell-courses-without-an-offer)
- [How to Build Courses / Membership Sites](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001141015-how-to-build-courses-membership-sites)
- [Getting Started – Launch a Course](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005072-create_ticket)
- [How to Set Up the Client Portal](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000193-how-to-set-up-the-client-portal-)
- [Introducing the All-New GoKollab Discover](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009066-introducing-the-all-new-gokollab-discover)

title_en: Restaurant Orders: How to Manage Orders and Payments
source_md:
Restaurant Orders in HighLevel brings pickup, delivery, and dine-in orders into one place, making it easier to track and manage your restaurant's daily operations. You can view incoming orders, update preparation statuses, manage dine-in orders, and collect payments without switching between multiple tools. This article explains how to navigate Restaurant Orders, process orders, and manage payments from start to finish.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is Restaurant Orders?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-Is-Restaurant-Orders?)
- [Key Benefits of Restaurant Orders](#Key-Benefits-of-Restaurant-Orders)
- [Before You Start](#Before-You-Start)
- [How to Access and Navigate Restaurant Orders](#How-to-Access-and-Navigate-Restaurant-Orders)
  - [Open Restaurant Orders](#Open-Restaurant-Orders)
  - [Understand the Order Tabs](#Understand-the-Order-Tabs)
  - [Find and Filter Orders](#Find-and-Filter-Orders)
- [How to Manage Order Statuses](#How-to-Manage-Order-Statuses)
- [How to Manage Dine-in Orders and Payments](#How-to-Manage-Dine-in-Orders-and-Payments)
- [How to Find Completed and Canceled Orders](#How-to-Find-Completed-and-Canceled-Orders)
- [Restaurant Settings That Affect Orders](#Restaurant-Settings-That-Affect-Orders)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is Restaurant Orders?**

Restaurant Orders is a centralized workspace where your team can manage orders throughout their lifecycle, from receiving an order to preparing, serving, or delivering it. It helps staff stay organized and track each order's progress while keeping order and payment information accessible.

Orders can originate from two sources:

- Pickup and delivery: Customers place orders through your published restaurant website.
- Dine-in: Staff create orders for seated guests through Reservations and send them to the kitchen. Each round of items ordered appears separately in Restaurant Orders.

Each order displays important information, including order type, items, preparation status, timing, customer details, total amount, and payment status.

---

## **Key Benefits of Restaurant Orders**

Managing all restaurant orders from a central location helps your team coordinate food preparation, reduce missed orders, and provide a smoother customer experience.

- **One list for every order:**Pickup, delivery and dine-in orders sit side by side, so nothing is missed.
- **One click to the next step:**The button next to each status moves the order forward, for example from Accepted to In progress.
- **Guests stay informed:**Guests get updates when their order is received, accepted, ready, on its way or delivered, based on your notification settings.
- **See what is late:**Turn on Running late to see only the orders that are behind.
- **Payments in the same place:**Take payment for a table from its order, by card or recorded by hand.

---

## **Before You Start**

A few restaurant settings must be configured before your team can begin processing orders. The requirements depend on whether you offer online ordering, dine-in service, or both.

- Menu: Add your restaurant's menu items so customers and staff can select them when placing orders.
- Restaurant website: Publish your restaurant website to make online ordering available. Until it is published, the Orders page may display Ordering off.
- Payments: Connect a supported payment provider to accept online or card payments.
- Dine-in setup: Configure your restaurant's floor layout and tables in Reservations before taking dine-in orders.

---

## **How to Access and Navigate Restaurant Orders**

The Restaurant Orders workspace organizes orders by their progress and provides filters to help your team focus on what needs attention. Understanding the available tabs and controls makes it easier to manage orders during busy service hours.

### **Open Restaurant Orders**

1. In your HighLevel sub-account, click Restaurants in the left navigation.
2. Select Restaurant Orders.  
     
   **![Click Restaurants, then Restaurant Orders.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084888144/original/se_dCsPaKTuiF72mNrTF-CuhMmD3Iihe9A.png?1793747189 "Click Restaurants, then Restaurant Orders.")**
3. The Active tab opens by default, displaying orders currently being processed.

If your restaurant has not received any orders, the page displays Your orders show up here, along with options to add a menu and configure online ordering.

```
Tip: Expand Restaurant Orders in the navigation panel to access individual tabs, such as Scheduled or Completed.
```

---

### **Understand the Order Tabs**

Orders are grouped into tabs based on their current stage, allowing staff to focus on active work while keeping scheduled and historical orders accessible.

| Tab | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Active | Orders currently being processed, from new orders through fulfillment. Dine-in orders remain active until the table's bill is paid. |
| Scheduled | Orders customers have placed in advance for a later time. |
| Completed | Finished orders, including dine-in tables that have paid and closed. |
| All | Displays orders across all stages. |
| Canceled | Orders that have been canceled. |

---

### **Find and Filter Orders**

Filters help staff quickly locate specific orders, monitor delays, and prioritize work without searching through the entire order list.

- **Today or All dates:** Choose the dates to show.
- **Type:** Show All types, or only Pickup, Delivery or Dine-in orders.
- **Status:**Show orders at one step. Each status shows how many orders it holds.
- **Filters:**Filter by Payment status.
- **Running late:**Turn it on to show only the orders running late.
- **Search orders:** Find an order by what you know about it.
- **Refresh:** Load the newest orders.

The order list displays columns for Order, Status, Type, Items, Timing, Customer, Total, Payment, and Actions.

Completed orders display Outcome and Finished instead of Status and Timing.

Click Manage columns to customize the information visible in the list.

**![The Active tab. The button next to each status moves the order to its next step.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887574/original/DzswSBPjSLDsbixQfyCt5IyQyDaWtb5yNA.png?1793745459 "The Active tab. The button next to each status moves the order to its next step.")**

---

## **How to Manage Order Statuses**

Each order follows a sequence of statuses that reflects its preparation and fulfillment progress. Updating these statuses helps your team coordinate kitchen operations and, for pickup and delivery orders, communicate progress to customers.

### **How an Order Moves**

### 

Pickup and delivery orders placed through your website initially appear as New and wait for your team to accept them.

Dine-in orders follow a slightly different process. When staff send an order round to the kitchen, it enters Restaurant Orders with the Accepted status.

The typical fulfillment flow depends on the order type:

- Pickup: New → Accepted → In progress → Ready to collect → Collected.
- Delivery: New → Accepted → In progress → Ready for delivery → On its way → Delivered.
- Dine-in: Accepted → In progress → Ready to serve → Served.

**![The steps for pickup, delivery and dine-in orders.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887591/original/25CgVj5Fuqmf3lkJLKB3csYYBYBTI5WPoA.png?1793745548 "The steps for pickup, delivery and dine-in orders.")**

### **Move an Order to the Next Status**

Order statuses can be updated using the action button beside each order or by selecting a status directly.

1. Open Restaurants → Restaurant Orders.
2. Locate the order in the Active tab.
3. Click the action button next to its current status.
4. The order advances to the next stage.

![Click a status to choose any step for a dine-in round.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887605/original/2rf4RuuetOhW8GnqrMO1vnGTK7_rmuq7KA.png?1793745594 "Click a status to choose any step for a dine-in round.")

For dine-in orders, the following actions are available:

| Current Status | Action | New Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accepted | Start preparing | In progress |
| In progress | Mark ready | Ready to serve |
| Ready to serve | Mark served | Served |

To select a different status manually, click the order's current status and choose an option from the dropdown.

For dine-in rounds, the available options include New, Accepted, In progress, Ready to serve, Served, and Void round.

```
Note: Pickup and delivery customers can receive notifications when their orders reach certain stages, such as Order accepted or Ready to collect. These messages depend on the customer notification settings configured for your restaurant.
```

### **View Order Details**

Opening an order provides additional information about its items, status, customer, and payment. For dine-in orders, it also helps staff review the table's activity and manage additional rounds.

1. Locate an order in Restaurant Orders.
2. Click the order to open its details.
3. Review the available information and actions.

Dine-in order details include the table and area, party size, seating time, reservation, individual rounds, ordered items, guest information, and bill.

You can also click the three-dot menu beside an order to access quick actions.

For an open dine-in table, these include:

- View table
- Add round
- Take payment
- Open on the floor

For completed tables, available actions include View table, Open on the floor, and View guest history.

**![A dine-in order’s details, with Add round and Take payment at the bottom.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887918/original/CGe-gwysyVEGUt3MdjXIQXpFahl1BdpJcw.png?1793746549 "A dine-in order’s details, with Add round and Take payment at the bottom.")**

---

## **How to Manage Dine-in Orders and Payments**

Dine-in orders are managed through individual rounds associated with a seated table. Each round is sent to the kitchen separately, while the overall table bill combines the charges for the visit. This allows staff to handle multiple rounds of food and drinks before collecting payment.

### **Create and Send a Dine-in Order**

Staff create dine-in orders from Reservations, where they can select menu items, customize them, and send each round to the kitchen.

1. In Reservations, open a seated table and go to Order.
2. Click Add round, then tap each item the table orders. Items with choices, such as add-ons, open first so you can pick them, add a Kitchen note and set the Quantity.
3. Check the round. You can add one more of an item, remove it, or edit it. The Round subtotal shows the total, and tax is added to the bill.
4. Click Send to kitchen. The round appears in Restaurant Orders with an Accepted status, labeled with its table and round number, such as Table T4 – Round 1.

To add another round, open the three-dot menu next to the table's order and select Add round.

Each round is tracked separately, but the table's bill includes the charges from its rounds.

**![How a dine-in order moves from table to kitchen to payment.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887752/original/JcMbtVGBAXA1YfeDKIBo3Xuv2cwUCh6kGg.png?1793746093 "How a dine-in order moves from table to kitchen to payment.")**

### **Collect Payment for a Dine-in Table**

### 

A dine-in order remains in the Active tab until the table's bill is paid, even when all food has been served. Staff can collect payment directly from Restaurant Orders or from the table in Reservations.

1. **Click the three-dot menu next to the order and choose Take payment, or click Take payment in the order’s details.**
2. **Check the Amount due. Click View bill to see every item.**
3. **Choose a tip: No tip, one of your suggested amounts (for example 15%), or Custom.**
4. **Search for the guest, or add them as a new guest with a phone number or email. A guest is needed to take payment.**
5. **Choose how the guest pays. Charge a card uses your card payment provider. Record manually is for a payment you took another way: choose Cash, Card, Cheque, Bank transfer or Other, and add an optional Note, like a terminal receipt number.**
6. **Optional: to split the bill, choose Record manually and lower the Amount to what this guest pays. Take payment again for the rest. A card payment always pays the full amount due.**
7. **Click Charge or Record. The button shows the amount.**

****![Take payment: choose a tip, then charge a card or record a payment you took another way.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887782/original/NGQj_rmSf0J1sIT7gbcWooeCSiIM8YoA_w.png?1793746175 "Take payment: choose a tip, then charge a card or record a payment you took another way.")****

```
Important: Card payments require a connected payment provider. If no provider is connected, the system displays No payment provider found. You can still use Record manually to record payments collected through another method.
```

**Once the table's full bill is paid:**

- The payment status changes to Paid.
- The table is closed.
- The booking is marked as completed.
- The order moves from Active to Completed.

---

## **How to Find Completed and Canceled Orders**

Completed and canceled orders remain accessible for reviewing previous transactions, checking fulfillment outcomes, and looking up customer order information.

1. **Click Completed, Canceled or All.**
2. **Choose All dates to see orders from before today.**
3. **Use Type, Filters or Search orders to narrow the list.**

**Completed orders show their Outcome, for example Closed for a table that paid, and when they Finished. Click the three-dot menu and choose View guest history to see a guest’s past visits**

****![The Completed tab shows each order’s outcome and when it finished.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084887823/original/_uScfiCie80ZmlGRquguXbPrht1n_jJQNw.png?1793746349 "The Completed tab shows each order’s outcome and when it finished.")****

## **Restaurant Settings That Affect Orders**

Restaurant Settings determine how orders are accepted, prepared, paid for, and communicated to customers. Keeping these settings up to date helps your team manage order availability, fulfillment times, and notifications accurately.

| Setting | What It Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Prep time | The estimated preparation duration used to calculate when an order should be ready. |
| Pickup and Delivery | Ordering availability, operating hours, scheduled orders, price markup, delivery areas, fees, and downtime. |
| Checkout and payments | Payment provider configuration, live payment mode, and available tip options. |
| Notifications → Internal | On-screen alerts, sounds for new orders, and staff notifications. |
| Notifications → Customer | Messages customers receive as pickup and delivery orders progress. |

These options are managed through Restaurant Settings.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why does Restaurant Orders display "Ordering off"?**

The restaurant website may not be published yet. Publish your restaurant website and ensure your online ordering settings are configured. Dine-in orders can still be created from seated tables in Reservations.

**Q: Why is a served dine-in order still showing as Active?**

A dine-in order remains active until the table's bill is fully paid, even if all rounds have been served.

**Q: Can I accept cash payments for dine-in orders?**

Yes. Select Take payment, choose Record manually, select Cash, and record the amount received.

**Q: How will my staff know when a new online order arrives?**

New orders can trigger on-screen notifications and sounds until an order is accepted. Configure staff alerts under Restaurant Settings → Notifications → Internal.

**Q: What order notifications can customers receive?**

Pickup notifications can include Order received, Order accepted, Ready to collect, Collected, and Order canceled. Delivery notifications can include Order received, Order accepted, On its way, Delivered, and Order canceled. Available messages are managed under Restaurant Settings → Notifications → Customer.

**Q: Can I modify the suggested tip amounts?**

Yes. Open Restaurant Settings → Checkout and payments to adjust the suggested tip amounts and default tip.

**Q: Can customers place orders in advance?**

Scheduled orders can be enabled through the restaurant's pickup and delivery settings. Advance orders are displayed under the Scheduled tab.

**Q: Can I see previous orders from a particular customer?**

Yes. Use the All or Completed tab and the available search and filters. For completed dine-in orders, the View guest history action provides access to past guest visits.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Restaurant Setup Guide: Get Ready to Take Orders and Reservations](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009586-restaurant-setup-guide-get-ready-to-take-orders-and-reservations?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Create a Restaurant Menu in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009587-how-to-create-a-restaurant-menu-in-highlevel?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Restaurant Reservations: Manage Bookings, Tables, and Guests](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009589-restaurant-reservations-manage-bookings-tables-and-guests?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Restaurant Website: How to Customize and Publish Your Site](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009590-restaurant-website-how-to-customize-and-publish-your-site?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How to Manage and Customize a Restaurant Menu in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009592-how-to-manage-and-customize-a-restaurant-menu-in-highlevel?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Reselling Products - Global Tax Compliance
source_md:
Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products helps agencies configure tax collection, tax invoices, and tax reports for products and services resold to sub-accounts. Powered by Stripe Tax, this feature supports tax handling across 100+ countries from the HighLevel dashboard. This article explains how the feature works, what agencies need before setup, how collection modes and usage tax treatments apply, how taxable products and Stripe Tax Codes are configured, and where to access tax invoices and reports.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products?](#What-is-Global-Tax-Compliance-for-Reselling-Products?)
- [Key Benefits of Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products](#Key-Benefits-of-Global-Tax-Compliance-for-Reselling-Products)
- [Prerequisites](#Prerequisites)
- [Important Tax Responsibility Notice](#Important-Tax-Responsibility-Notice)
- [How Stripe Tax Works](#How-Stripe-Tax-Works)
- [Collection Modes](#Collection-Modes)
- [Tax Treatment on Usage Products](#Tax-Treatment-on-Usage-Products)
- [Taxable Products and Stripe Tax Codes](#Taxable-Products-and-Stripe-Tax-Codes)
- [Global Default Settings](#Global-Default-Settings)
- [Tax Invoices and Reports](#Tax-Invoices-and-Reports)
- [How To Setup Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products](#How-To-Setup-Global-Tax-Compliance-for-Reselling-Products)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products?**

```
Important: Tax Remittance Is Your Responsibility. This feature helps you collect and report taxes accurately. Remitting the collected taxes to the relevant tax authorities is the agency's responsibility.
```

Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products helps agencies configure tax collection, tax invoices, and tax reports for products and services resold to sub-accounts. Powered by Stripe Tax, this feature supports tax handling across 100+ countries and helps agencies manage tax settings directly from the HighLevel dashboard.

Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products allows agencies to manage sales tax, VAT, GST, and other applicable tax collection across multiple jurisdictions when reselling products to sub-accounts. It supports US state-level registrations, Canadian province-level registrations, EU VAT, OSS Union, OSS Non-Union, IOSS, and VAT/GST regimes across Asia Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa.

This feature applies to resold products such as usage-based products, SaaS subscriptions, and marketplace apps. Agencies can collect taxes from sub-accounts on wallet recharges or based on actual monthly usage, manage tax registrations and product tax codes, generate tax invoices, and download tax reports by sub-account and jurisdiction.

---

## **Key Benefits of Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products**

- **100+ Countries Supported:** Configure tax collection across supported Stripe Tax jurisdictions, including US state-level sales tax, Canadian GST/HST/PST by province, EU VAT, OSS Union, OSS Non-Union, IOSS, and VAT/GST regimes across Asia Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa.
- **Stripe Tax-Powered Calculations:** Use Stripe Tax to calculate taxes based on business address, tax registrations, product tax codes, and the sub-account billing address.
- **Automatic Jurisdiction Sync:** Jurisdictions registered in Stripe Tax sync into HighLevel automatically.
- **Flexible Collection Modes:** Choose Automatic collection through Stripe Tax or Manual handling outside HighLevel for each jurisdiction.
- **Usage Tax Treatment Options:** Apply tax when a sub-account recharges its wallet or based on actual monthly usage.
- **Full Product Coverage:** Configure taxability for usage-based products, SaaS subscriptions, and marketplace apps.
- **Product Tax Code Mapping:** Map products to Stripe Tax Codes for jurisdiction-level classification.
- **Global Default Settings:** Configure defaults once so new jurisdictions inherit them automatically.
- **Tax Invoices and Reports:** Generate invoices per sub-account and jurisdiction, download reports by period, and export reports in bulk ZIP format.
- **Sub-Account Invoice Access:** Allow sub-accounts to access their own invoices from their billing section.

---

## **Prerequisites**

Please review the following before configuring Tax Compliance:

1. **All sub-accounts must have a valid billing address:** Tax jurisdiction matching depends entirely on the sub-account's billing address, including a valid zip code. If a sub-account does not have a valid address on file, the system cannot determine which tax rules apply and taxes will not be collected. Make sure all relevant sub-accounts have this configured before enabling tax collection.
2. **You****must have a connected Stripe account:** Tax Compliance uses Stripe Tax for all tax registration, calculation, and reporting. Your agency's Stripe connected account is required for all tax operations.
3. **Jurisdictions must be registered in Stripe Tax first:** Before configuring tax collection for a jurisdiction in HighLevel, you must complete the registration for that jurisdiction in Stripe. HighLevel will then sync and display your registered jurisdictions automatically.
4. **Stripe Tax may have additional charges:** Enabling Automatic collection mode uses Stripe Tax for calculations. Depending on your Stripe plan, Stripe Tax may apply additional per-transaction fees. Review your Stripe plan before enabling automatic mode.

---

## **Important Tax Responsibility Notice**

```
Note: Always consult a qualified tax advisor before relying on this feature for compliance purposes. HighLevel and Stripe Tax do not guarantee the accuracy of tax calculations.
```

Tax tools can help automate collection and reporting, but they do not replace professional tax guidance. Agencies are responsible for understanding where they must register, how collected taxes should be verified, and when taxes must be remitted to the appropriate tax authorities.

Tax calculations are provided through Stripe Tax, a third-party provider. HighLevel makes no representations, warranties, or guarantees regarding the accuracy, completeness, or reliability of any tax calculations.

**Agencies are solely responsible for:**

- Registering with applicable tax authorities
- Configuring tax registrations in Stripe Tax
- Verifying all tax calculations before filing or remitting taxes
- Remitting collected taxes to the correct tax authorities
- Confirming tax treatment for their products, services, jurisdictions, and business model

---

## **How Stripe Tax Works**

Stripe Tax determines tax rates by evaluating the agency’s business information, registered jurisdictions, product classifications, and the billing location of the sub-account being charged. This helps automate tax calculation while still requiring the agency to confirm that their tax setup matches their legal obligations.

Global Tax Compliance is powered by Stripe Tax. Stripe uses the agency’s business address, tax registrations, product tax codes, and the sub-account’s billing address to determine and apply tax rates on transactions across supported jurisdictions.

Stripe maintains tax research resources to monitor law changes across supported countries. HighLevel does not independently verify these rates.

Before configuring tax collection for a jurisdiction in HighLevel, complete the registration for that jurisdiction in Stripe Tax. HighLevel then syncs and displays registered jurisdictions automatically.

---

## **Collection Modes**

Collection modes determine whether HighLevel applies tax automatically through Stripe Tax or whether the agency handles tax outside the platform. Choosing the correct mode is important because it controls whether HighLevel applies tax for a registered jurisdiction.

- **Automatic:** Stripe Tax applies rates to transactions based on the agency’s configuration, tax registrations, product tax codes, and the sub-account’s billing address.
- **Manual:** HighLevel applies no tax for that jurisdiction. The agency handles tax calculation, collection, invoicing, reporting, and remittance entirely outside HighLevel.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070632977/original/7Y46OAPdSOY5cB6wIlDkhQqs0vjEMVNC7Q.jpeg?1777995840)

---

## **Tax Treatment on Usage Products**

Usage products can be taxed when wallet funds are added or after actual monthly usage is calculated. The right option depends on how the agency wants to collect tax for usage-based products and how their tax advisor recommends handling wallet-based billing.

| Treatment | How It Works |
| --- | --- |
| **On Recharge** | Tax is calculated and charged when the sub-account adds funds to their wallet. For example, a $10 top-up at 20% tax means the sub-account is charged $12, with $10 going to the wallet and $2 applied to tax. |
| **At Month End** | Tax is calculated based on actual monthly usage and charged to the wallet at the start of the following month. If the wallet balance is too low, it can go negative and trigger an auto-recharge. |

If you switch from On Recharge to At Month End, the switch is scheduled for a future date to avoid mid-period disruptions. Both the old and new treatment will have defined date windows showing when each treatment is active.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070630109/original/cBPEft1VKDqleP2pPJBioJdrYMZ6lXv-8w.jpeg?1777994573)

---

## **Taxable Products and Stripe Tax Codes**

Product taxability controls which resold products are subject to tax in each jurisdiction. Stripe Tax Codes help classify products correctly so Stripe Tax can apply jurisdiction-specific rules based on the product type.

Agencies can configure taxability for:

- Usage-based products, including SMS, WhatsApp, AI, calls, and email
- SaaS subscriptions
- Marketplace apps

For each jurisdiction, choose which products are taxable. You can use preset tax codes matched from Stripe, customize tax codes per product, or mark specific products as non-taxable.

Products can also be configured in Global Settings and overridden per jurisdiction when needed. Jurisdiction-specific settings can have their own collection mode, tax treatment, and product taxability configuration.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070630170/original/ZajZWmsfsie9YpTFBzgFi2ECqZZ-4OVJrg.jpeg?1777994608)

---

## **Global Default Settings**

Global defaults reduce repetitive setup when agencies collect tax across multiple jurisdictions. New jurisdictions can inherit these defaults automatically, while still allowing agencies to adjust individual jurisdiction settings when needed.

Use Global Settings to configure default tax behavior once. New jurisdictions inherit these settings automatically, helping keep collection mode, tax treatment, and product taxability consistent as new registrations are added.

Each jurisdiction can still be configured separately when a specific region requires different tax handling.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/ndDGMdoPkV6djFCWA660+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+21.11.51.png)

---

## **Tax Invoices and Reports**

Tax invoices and reports give agencies the records needed to review collected taxes by sub-account, jurisdiction, and period. These records support reporting workflows, but agencies remain responsible for filing and remitting taxes to the correct authorities.

Global Tax Compliance generates tax invoices per sub-account and jurisdiction. Agencies can view tax reporting data in the Tax Reports tab, download individual reports by period, or request a bulk ZIP file sent to their email.

Sub-accounts can access their own invoices from their billing section.

**Important:** This feature handles tax collection and reporting only. Tax remittance to the relevant tax authorities is the agency’s responsibility.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/6ZpJBjZkQmhmyAlrcqQC+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.55.42.png)

---

## **How To Setup Global Tax Compliance for Reselling Products**

Proper setup ensures HighLevel can display registered jurisdictions, apply the selected collection mode, and generate the correct invoice and reporting records. Complete Stripe Tax registration first, then configure each jurisdiction in HighLevel.

[동영상](https://watchclueso.com/embed/src4boharqz86905)

1. Go to **Agency** **Settings.**  
     
   **![](https://jumpshare.com/share/fajkx50IJGp7iucaYydU+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+19.42.05.png)**
2. Click on **Stripe >****Tax Compliance**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/dAbN9IVMFJIk3tKmVA35+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+19.43.44.png)
3. **Review** the **tax** **jurisdictions** **synced** from **Stripe** **Tax**.

   - These are the jurisdictions you have configured in Stripe Tax.
   - **Learn more from Stripe:** <https://docs.stripe.com/tax/how-tax-works>  
       
     ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/H9ZxYymVg0fB2W7qqoiw+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.20.50.png)
4. Click on the **Action**button for the jurisdiction where you want to start collecting taxes.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/7tCpXrQDYNg6gwo6dKuB+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.23.35.png)
5. Select the **Collection Mode**.

   - Choose **Automatic** to use Stripe Tax calculations. (**Stripe Charges Apply**)
   - Choose **Manual** if your agency will handle tax calculation, collection, invoicing, reporting, and remittance outside HighLevel.
6. Click on **Next**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/CCUKaopFfXUCIOX5qJOV+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.34.48.png)
7. Select **Tax Treatment on Usage Products**.

   - Choose **At Wallet Recharge** to apply tax when the sub-account adds funds to their wallet.
   - Choose **At Month End** to apply tax based on actual monthly usage at the start of the following month.
8. Click on **Next**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/NX5aD8AbYCb2VzxvEXvh+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.39.20.png)
9. Select **Taxable Products**.

   - Use preset Stripe Tax Codes, customize codes per product, or mark products as non-taxable.
   - Choose which products are subject to tax for the jurisdiction.
10. Click on **Next**.  
      
    ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/HWVbtibaIoXoi2RRAckg+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.42.48.png)
11. Complete the **Legal Confirmation**.

    - Read the Terms of Service and legal confirmation.
    - **Check** the "**I understand and agree to the terms outlined above"** box.
    - This acknowledges that tax calculations are handled by Stripe Tax and that HighLevel does not guarantee tax accuracy.
12. Type **I Agree** (ALL CAPS) and click on **Finish Setup**.  
      
    ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/jCN7d4GecBXf5X9E5jIC+/Screen+Shot+2026-05-05+at+20.45.27.png)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Which countries and jurisdictions are supported?**

Global Tax Compliance supports 100+ countries through Stripe Tax. US state-level and Canadian province-level registrations are supported with jurisdiction-specific matching logic. Supported regions also include EU VAT, OSS Union, OSS Non-Union, IOSS, and VAT/GST regimes across Asia Pacific, Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa.

**Q: Can I have different tax settings for different jurisdictions?**

Yes. Global Settings provide defaults, but each jurisdiction registration can have its own collection mode, tax treatment, and product taxability configuration.

**Q: What happens if I switch from On Recharge to At Month End?**

The switch is scheduled for a future date to avoid mid-period disruptions. Both the old and new treatment will have defined date windows showing when each is active.

**Q: Can I exempt specific products from tax?**

Yes. In both Global Settings and per-jurisdiction configuration, you can mark specific usage-based products, subscription products, or marketplace apps as non-taxable.

**Q: How are tax reports generated?**

Tax reports are automatically generated based on collected tax data. You can view them in the Tax Reports tab, download individual reports, or request a bulk ZIP file sent to your email.

**Q: Do I need a Stripe account?**

Yes. Tax Compliance uses Stripe Tax for tax registration, calculation, and reporting. Your agency’s connected Stripe account is required for tax operations.

**Q: What if my sub-accounts do not have a billing address?**

Tax jurisdiction matching will not work without a valid billing address, including zip code, on the sub-account. Taxes will not be collected for those sub-accounts until an address is added.

**Q: Does HighLevel remit collected taxes for agencies?**

No. Global Tax Compliance helps with tax collection, invoices, and reports. Remitting collected taxes to the relevant tax authorities is the agency’s responsibility.

**Q: What happens when a jurisdiction is set to Manual?**

HighLevel applies no tax for that jurisdiction. The agency handles tax calculation, collection, invoicing, reporting, and remittance outside HighLevel.

**Q: Can sub-accounts access their own tax invoices?**

Yes. Sub-accounts can access their own invoices from their billing section.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Automatic Tax Calculation with Stripe for SaaS Subscriptions:](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007789)
- [Rebilling, Reselling, and Wallets Explained](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002095)
- [How to Manage Stripe Payment Methods inside HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005164)
- [How to Configure International Automatic Taxes in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005563)
- [Reselling and Rebilling through SaaS V2 Payment Providers](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005083)

title_en: How to Analyze Workflow Campaigns in HighLevel
source_md:
Workflow Campaigns in HighLevel help you monitor the performance of automated emails sent through workflows. By analyzing delivery, opens, clicks, replies, and other engagement metrics, you can understand how contacts interact with emails at different stages of your automation. HighLevel provides multiple reporting views to help you compare workflow email performance, evaluate individual email actions, and identify opportunities to improve your automated communications.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Workflow Campaigns?](#What-are-Workflow-Campaigns?)
- [Key Benefits of Workflow Campaigns](#Key-Benefits-of-Workflow-Campaigns)
- [Unified Email Statistics for Workflow Campaigns](#Unified-Email-Statistics-for-Workflow-Campaigns)
- [Individual Email Action Statistics](#Individual-Email-Action-Statistics)
- [Workflow-Level Communication Statistics](#Workflow-Level-Communication-Statistics)
- [Workflow Builder Stats View](#Workflow-Builder-Stats-View)
- [How to Access and Analyze Workflow Campaigns](#How-to-Access-and-Analyze-Workflow-Campaigns)
- [View Statistics for an Individual Email Action](#View-Statistics-for-an-Individual-Email-Action)
- [View Workflow-Level Statistics](#view-workflow-level-statistics)
- [Analyze Email Actions Using Workflow Builder Stats View](#Analyze-Email-Actions-Using-Workflow-Builder-Stats-View)
- [Edit Workflow Emails After Reviewing Statistics](#Edit-Workflow-Emails-After-Reviewing-Statistics)
- [Export Workflow Email Statistics](#export-workflow-email-statistics)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Workflow Campaigns?**

Workflow Campaigns represent emails sent through email actions within HighLevel workflows. Rather than tracking an automated sequence as a single email, HighLevel provides reporting for individual email actions, helping you understand how each message performs throughout the workflow.

Workflow email statistics can be accessed through the unified Email Statistics dashboard, individual email actions in the Workflow Builder, and workflow-level communication reports. These reporting options help you evaluate both overall engagement and the effectiveness of specific automated messages.

---

## **Key Benefits of Workflow Campaigns**

Analyzing automated email performance helps you understand which messages are reaching contacts and generating engagement. By reviewing workflow email statistics, you can identify delivery issues, compare individual email actions, and make informed adjustments to improve your automation strategy.

- **Unified Email Reporting:** Review Workflow Campaigns alongside Email Campaigns and Bulk Actions from one Email Statistics dashboard.
- **Individual Email Insights:** Track the performance of specific email actions within a workflow to identify stronger- and weaker-performing messages.
- **Engagement and Delivery Monitoring:** Review opens, clicks, replies, bounces, rejected events, and other available activity to understand how contacts interact with automated emails.
- **Workflow-Level Visibility:** Review communication performance for individual workflows, including available email and SMS statistics.
- **Performance Analysis:** Use reporting insights and exported workflow email statistics to analyze results and identify opportunities to improve automated communications.

---

## **Unified Email Statistics for Workflow Campaigns**

The unified Email Statistics dashboard provides a centralized view of email performance across HighLevel. Filtering the dashboard to Workflow Campaigns allows you to evaluate automated email activity without combining it with standalone Email Campaigns or Bulk Actions.

The dashboard includes several reporting components:

| **Reporting Component** | **Purpose** |
| --- | --- |
| Engagement Summary | Provides an overview of email delivery and engagement activity. |
| Performance Analysis | Displays trends for available email performance metrics across the selected reporting period. |
| Top Performing Emails | Identifies individual emails generating stronger engagement, based on available ranking metrics. |
| Source Filter | Allows you to focus on Workflow Campaigns or compare supported email sources. |
| Date Range Filter | Limits reporting to the selected period. |

**Understanding Workflow Results in Top Performing Emails**

When reviewing Top Performing Emails, HighLevel evaluates each workflow email action individually rather than ranking the entire workflow as one email.

For example, a workflow containing a welcome email, a reminder email, and a follow-up email can have three separate entries in the reporting results, depending on their activity and the selected filters.

This makes it easier to identify which automated messages generate stronger open or click engagement.

---

## **Individual Email Action Statistics**

Individual email-action statistics provide detailed information about how a specific automated email performs. Reviewing these metrics helps you determine whether contacts are receiving, opening, clicking, or responding to particular emails in a workflow.

HighLevel supports the following workflow email statistics, subject to the available reporting events and sending configuration:

| **Metric** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Accepted | Email events accepted for processing by the sending service. |
| Delivered | Emails reported as successfully delivered to the recipient's mail server. |
| Opened | Recorded email open activity through supported tracking. |
| Clicked | Recorded recipient interactions with tracked email links. |
| Replied | Replies associated with the email, where supported by the sending and tracking configuration. |
| Bounced | Emails that could not be delivered successfully. |
| Unsubscribed | Contacts who used an unsubscribe mechanism to opt out of email communications. |
| Complained | Recipients who reported an email as spam, where the event is available. |
| Rejected | Emails rejected during processing or delivery by the applicable sending system. |

The individual workflow email statistics view defaults to **Last 30 days**.

**How to Interpret Email Engagement**

Comparing these metrics can help you identify opportunities for improvement.

- A high number of accepted events with fewer delivered events may indicate delivery problems requiring investigation.
- Strong open activity with relatively few clicks may indicate that recipients are interested in the email but are not interacting with its links.
- A high number of bounces or complaints may indicate an issue with contact data quality, sending practices, or audience expectations.
- Differences in engagement between workflow email actions can help you identify which messages may benefit from changes to their content or calls to action.

```
Important: An accepted email is not necessarily a delivered email. Open and click statistics also depend on tracking availability and should not be interpreted as definitive proof that a recipient read or engaged with the message.
```

---

## **Workflow-Level Communication Statistics**

Workflow-level statistics provide a broader view of communication activity within an individual workflow. Unlike the unified Email Statistics dashboard, this reporting view can include both email and SMS performance, helping you evaluate how different communication actions contribute to the workflow.

HighLevel provides access to these reports from the Workflow List.

**What Workflow-Level Statistics Include**

- **Email Performance:** Available delivery and engagement results for email actions used within the workflow.
- **SMS Performance:** Available communication statistics for SMS actions.
- **Historical Activity:** Statistics can include data from January 1, 2023 onward.
- **Deleted Action History:** Statistics for email or SMS actions that were previously used and later deleted can remain available.

Workflow-level reporting is available for individual workflows, not entire workflow folders. For additional details, see [Comprehensive Workflow Stats](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003972-comprehensive-workflow-stats).

---

## **Workflow Builder Stats View**

Workflow Builder Stats View allows you to inspect available statistics directly from the workflow canvas. This helps you analyze the performance of triggers and communication actions while reviewing how the automation is structured.

Stats View supports two different types of reporting:

| **Reporting Type** | **What It Measures** |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger Statistics | Contact enrollment activity, including Attempted, Matched, and Unmatched events. |
| Communication Action Statistics | Available delivery and engagement information for communication actions, including workflow emails. |

Trigger statistics and email engagement statistics serve different purposes. For example, a contact matching a workflow trigger does not necessarily mean an email was delivered or opened.

**Editing Limitation**

You cannot edit a workflow while Stats View is active. To make changes to email actions or other workflow components, return to the regular Workflow Builder editing mode. For more information about navigating and editing workflows, see [Workflow Builder Walkthrough](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001254-workflow-builder-walkthrough).

---

## **How to Access and Analyze Workflow Campaigns**

HighLevel provides multiple ways to access workflow performance data. Selecting the appropriate reporting interface ensures that you are analyzing the right metrics, whether you want to compare automated email activity across workflows or investigate a particular email action.

**Access Workflow Campaigns from the Unified Email Statistics Dashboard**

The unified dashboard is useful when you want to review automated email engagement across workflows or compare workflow email performance over a selected period.

1. Go to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**.
2. Open the source filter and select **Workflow Campaigns**.
3. Select the reporting date range.
4. Review **Engagement Summary**, **Performance Analysis**, and **Top Performing Emails**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083544528/original/NrZrnMoMDbW-t12HRUFs-LygZVj7366XwQ.gif?1792170601)

**Note:** Top Performing Emails evaluates individual workflow email actions rather than the entire workflow.

---

## **View Statistics for an Individual Email Action**

Viewing individual email-action statistics helps you investigate the results of a particular automated message. This is useful when a workflow contains multiple emails or when one step appears to have unusually low engagement.

1. Navigate to **Automation → Workflows**.
2. Open the workflow you want to analyze.
3. Select the **Email** action you want to review.
4. In the right-hand panel, click **Statistics**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083547714/original/EpOB2PYtlC5SYh6vkOYSgzaFLOwfyI4RGw.png?1792173756)

5. Review the available email delivery and engagement metrics.
6. Use the reporting controls, where available, to examine the relevant reporting period.

Individual email-action statistics default to the last 30 days.

---

## **View Workflow-Level Statistics**

Workflow-level statistics let you review email and SMS performance for an individual workflow without opening Workflow Builder.

1. Go to **Automation → Workflows**.
2. Locate the workflow you want to analyze.
3. Click the expand arrow next to the workflow name.
4. Click **Stats** to view the workflow's communication statistics.
5. Review the available email and SMS statistics.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083545441/original/4hZpVEOGhzjqTOPaMghNizPKhsNsqU3uLA.gif?1792171498)

**Note:** Workflow-level statistics are available for individual workflows, not entire folders. Historical reporting can include activity from January 1, 2023 onward, including statistics from previously deleted email and SMS actions.

---

## **Analyze Email Actions Using Workflow Builder Stats View**

Stats View helps you connect reporting data with the layout of your automation, making it easier to identify the actions you want to investigate.

1. Navigate to **Automation → Workflows**.
2. Open the workflow.
3. Turn on **Stats View** from the top-left corner.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083546709/original/aVC8ens7eUptSX2RXwsRymSnZUe5hAHLSw.png?1792172799)

4. Select the Email action you want to analyze.
5. Review its available delivery and engagement statistics.
6. Click a statistic to open the corresponding detailed report, where available.
7. Exit Stats View before making changes to the workflow.

---

## **Edit Workflow Emails After Reviewing Statistics**

Making changes based on performance results can help improve the effectiveness of automated communications. Reviewing individual email-action metrics before editing helps you focus on the messages most likely to benefit from optimization.

1. Open the workflow through **Automation → Workflows**.
2. If Stats View is enabled, turn it off to return to editing mode.
3. Select the Email action you want to update.
4. Review its content, configuration, and relevant tracking settings.
5. Make the necessary changes.
6. Save your changes and confirm the workflow's intended publication status.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083546197/original/iyF6TIdpbSVMYXWlkddFJyDqNmf90UnUjQ.png?1792172294)

If you are using a reporting interface that provides an **Edit Workflow** option, select it to navigate to the associated workflow in the Workflow Builder.

```
Important: Editing an email action does not guarantee an immediate improvement in its statistics. Evaluate future email activity after making changes to determine whether engagement improves.
```

---

## **Export Workflow Email Statistics**

Export workflow email statistics as a CSV file when you need to analyze performance outside HighLevel or share reporting data. Workflow exports provide statistics for individual email actions.

1. Go to **Marketing → Emails → Statistics**.
2. Select **Workflow Campaigns** from the source filter and choose the reporting date range.
3. Click **Export**. If a separate export-type selection appears, choose **Workflows Only**.
4. Enter the email address or addresses that should receive the report and submit the export request.
5. Open the email containing the CSV download link.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083545135/original/Pt5A1S9goN9ArqfLs6h21HPzCA1GVtE5ZA.png?1792171216)

Export download links remain valid for **30 days**. For more information, see [Exporting Email Campaign Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007499-exporting-email-campaign-data).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why do I see multiple entries for the same workflow in Top Performing Emails?**

HighLevel evaluates individual workflow email actions separately. If a workflow contains multiple email actions, they can appear as separate reporting entries instead of one combined workflow result.

**Q: Why are some workflow email statistics missing?**

Available metrics depend on the sending provider, tracking configuration, and recorded email events. Confirm that the email was sent, verify the selected date range, and review the applicable tracking settings. See [Troubleshooting Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001208601) for additional diagnostics.

**Q: Why can't I edit an Email action while viewing workflow statistics?**

Workflow Builder Stats View is designed for analyzing workflow activity. Editing is disabled while this mode is active. Exit Stats View before modifying email actions or other workflow components.

**Q: Can I view email statistics for a workflow that is no longer active?**

Previously recorded statistics may still be available for workflow email actions, depending on the relevant reporting period and retained history. A draft or inactive workflow will not generate new automated sends merely because its statistics are being viewed.

**Q: What happens to reporting data if an Email action is deleted?**

HighLevel's workflow-level reporting retains historical statistics for email and SMS actions that were previously used and later deleted. This allows users to review historical communication activity even when those actions are no longer part of the current workflow.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005552-all-in-one-dashboard-for-email-marketing)
