- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Advanced Analytics in the Social Planner?**

Advanced Analytics provides a centralized view of your social media performance across supported platforms. You can monitor engagement, compare account performance, and use reporting insights to improve your social media strategy.

---

## **Key Benefits of Social Planner Advanced Analytics**

Advanced Analytics helps you understand audience engagement and identify opportunities to improve your social media content.

- **Comprehensive Social Media Insights:**Track the number of posts, likes, comments, followers, impressions, and reach across many social media platforms from a single dashboard.
- **Visualize your Social Post Performance:** Interactive graphs showcase post trends and weekly performance.
- **Engagement Breakdown:** Get a detailed view of engagement metrics such as total likes, comments, and shares, broken down per platform.
- **Platform Comparisons:** Identify which platform drives more engagement, helping you tailor your content strategy accordingly.
- **Impressions and Post Reach:** Measure your content’s visibility with Reach and Impressions tracking.
- **Gender and Age Demographics:**See your audience breakdown in terms of age groups and gender, providing valuable data to optimize your content for the right audience.

---

## **Where to Find Social Planner Advanced Analytics** To access the analytics dashboard, navigate to **Marketing** >**Social Planner** >**Statistics.** ---

## **Supported Social Media Platforms and Limitations**

Metric availability varies on each platform. Use the notes below to set expectations and keep analytics flowing without interruption.

#### **Supported Platforms**

Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, Pinterest, TikTok, Google Business Profile (GBP), Threads and Bluesky.

#### **Permissions and Reauthentication Alerts**

Receive real-time alerts when your connected accounts require re-authentication to access analytics. This ensures continuous access to up-to-date insights without interruptions. Users will be able to see the statistics from the next day / when they reconnect their accounts with upgraded permissions.

#### 

#### **Post Specific Statistics**

Post Specific statistics are shown in the post details modal (Planner - List View)

- Platforms supported: Facebook, Instagram, Tiktok personal, LinkedIn page.
- Platforms to be supported: Youtube, Pinterest.
- Platforms not supported: Google Business profile, TikTok Business, LinkedIn profile, communities.

#### **Platform‑Specific Notes**

TikTok

- Only BUSINESS profiles are supported
- May take 1 or 2 days to reflect data due to the TikTok API availability.

Pinterest

- Takes n-2 days to reflect the correct data. (Similar behaviour is observed on hootsuite and other portals owing to API constraints)

LinkedIn

- Only Linkedin pages are supported not the Linkedin profiles owing to API constraints.
- Verify Total followers - Followers data will be available only until n-2 days (n being the current day).

Threads

- Impressions and Post Reach not supported
- No follower count, gender data, or advanced engagement metrics
- T-1 day delay for the metrics except the post count

  

Bluesky

- Impressions are supported
- Follower metrics, demographics, and advanced engagement breakdowns not supported
- T-1 day delay for the metrics except the post count

```
Demographics are not supported by any of the newly released Platforms
```

#### **Metric Availability by Platform**

| Metric | Facebook | Instagram | LinkedIn | Youtube | Pinterest | TikTok | GBP | Threads | Bluesky |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No. of Posts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Likes | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Comments | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Followers | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Impressions | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Post Reach | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Engagement | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Top Performing Posts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Gender Demography | ❌ | ✅\* | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

\*Instagram demographics require ≥ 100 followers; follower-related stats may be limited below that threshold.

---

## **Filter by Platform and Account**

To filter based on accounts, open the dropdown in the upper-left and **check the boxes** for the accounts you want included in the metrics.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084839547/original/bg1Ta6CMqG30uQj3j0fZ-LPf815Rb4YV1Q.png?1793709716)

Use the selector bar on the left to filter results based on social media platform. Choose **All** for a cross‑platform rollup, or select a specific platform (e.g., Threads, Bluesky) to narrow results.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155061043032/original/uui0jDzPG9_II7CyMfIsBWTsOUzJz8xQsw.png?1766178607)

---

## **Available Reports and Metrics**

```
Tip: Hover over the tooltip (i) next to any metric for definitions, supported platforms, and time‑range details.
```

### **KPI Overview**

Track the number of posts, likes, followers, impressions and comments across all platforms at a glance.

- **Number of Posts:** Total number of posts published across all selected social accounts.
- **Total Likes:** Total likes on posts published across all selected accounts.
- **Total Followers:** Total unique followers who joined across all selected social accounts.
- **Impressions:** Total unique impressions on published posts across all selected social accounts.
- **Comments:** Total count of comments on published posts across all selected social accounts.

  

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084839714/original/wLrZEi2E8xAyBCRth27fWXwu4QwAUQf2MA.png?1793709752)**

### **Social Post Performance**

Visualize your Social Post Performance with an interactive graph, showcasing published posts (bars) alongside daily totals for impressions, likes, and comments (lines) so you can track posting trends and weekly performance at a glance.

- **Bar Graph (Weekly Posts):**Show the number of posts published per week across all selected social media platforms.
- **Line Graph (Engagement):**The overlaying line graphs represent the total number of interactions (comments, likes, and shares) per day, regardless of when the posts were published.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840015/original/PTx7sABmWqAAJsC9bAC6-tTx6jsJX9qRaQ.png?1793709790)

### **Link Clicks by Socials**

The total number of link clicks from posts published across all selected social accounts by social platform.

```
Important: Tracking is available only for shortened links created through the Social Planner. Click here for more information on the link shortener.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064028648/original/MsUUFrK6GBBUjaPUJrpm4n38saHa7jkRlw.png?1770062729)

### **Link Performance**

Track the performance of your shortened links across all social platforms, including total clicks per link belonging to a campaign.

```
Important: Tracking is available only for shortened links created through the Social Planner. Click here for more information on the link shortener.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155064028719/original/uBekIUwZT6cQSHkajXK6XzcvhGQTVQyTWQ.png?1770062860)

### **Number of Posts**

This depicts the platform-wise total number of posts published across all selected social accounts. It shows the current week's posts compared to the previous week's.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840127/original/GdYAGWJynCT2WpPyrETa4vCy7LwjQvPAyQ.png?1793709830)**

### **Engagement**

The unique number of likes, comments, and shares received by posts published broken down by platform. The engagement percentage reflects the change in this week's data compared to the previous week.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840147/original/_F7xe4KMbum7tVZaSsIB0R1YbR38iwDRPg.png?1793709855)**

### **Impressions**

Impressions shows the number of times any published post was displayed on a person's screen. Impression percentage reflects change in this week's data compared to the previous week.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840223/original/QIIwpe8vLoQW_NvdXtgh42RZxPeg409Gow.png?1793709899)**

### **Post Reach**

Analyze post reach to understand the number of people who have seen any content from your page/account/about your page on their screen. This includes posts, check-ins, ads, social information from people who interact with your page, and more. The post reach percentage reflects the change in this week's data compared to the previous week.

For Google Business Profile, this number reflects the total number of Call Clicks, Website Clicks, Food orders, Bookings, Food Menu Clicks and Direction Requests.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840468/original/PwEb0P7gmjs4GvI1PCOy59O-ieD3Bcmc6A.png?1793710012)**

### **Top Performing Posts**

Use this report to see your top all-time posts. Top-performing posts are the posts with the highest number of likes among published social posts from the social planner. Click the Eye icon next to any post to view that post within the Social Media platform.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840467/original/CO7vy53LNMNkU94j78Z5t6t7rZzxsJMpGw.png?1793710012)**

### **Engagement Stats**

Get a detailed view of engagement metrics such as total likes, comments, and shares, broken down per platform. Use the selector ribbon to switch between Total Engagement, Total Followers and Total Likes. This report can be used to identify which platforms best drive engagement, helping you tailor your content strategy accordingly.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840558/original/VN1J9-T1vQZIJS4eqFN8XfgH1JSCZwyBAg.png?1793710050)**

### **Gender Demography**

Use this report to dive into detailed demographic data, including the gender distribution (male, female, and unknown) and age range insights. Demographic data is only available for those viewers who has shared the data for calculation to the respective Social Media Platforms.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084840703/original/KhXv3fsP34kidrmc5y27-Y8jD9EwMKjKsg.png?1793710096)

```
Important: This metric is not available for Instagram users with fewer than 100 followers.
```

---

## **Important Considerations**

Understanding reporting limitations helps you interpret performance data accurately.

- **Metric Availability:** Some metrics are unavailable due to platform API restrictions.
- **Reporting Delays:** Analytics may take one or more days to update, depending on the platform and metric.
- **Account Requirements:** LinkedIn dashboard analytics require Pages, while TikTok dashboard analytics support Business accounts. Post-specific statistics may have different requirements.
- **Instagram Demographics:** Demographic insights require at least 100 followers.
- **Account Authorization:** Some accounts may require reconnection or updated permissions to continue displaying analytics.
- **Post Sync:** Engagement insights for supported synchronized posts refresh approximately every 24 hours.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What types of metrics can I track using Social Planner analytics?**You can track various metrics, including engagement rates, post reach, impressions, clicks, and overall performance of your social media content. This data helps you assess the effectiveness of your strategies.

**Q: Is there a way to compare the performance of different posts?**Yes, the analytics dashboard allows you to compare the performance of individual posts over time, helping you identify trends and determine which types of content resonate best with your audience.

**Q: Can I export the analytics data for reporting purposes?**No, Social Planner currently doesn't provide option to export your analytics but we plan to support this in coming quarters for exporting data in various formats, making it easy to create reports and share insights with your team or stakeholders.

**Q:How often is the analytics data updated?**The analytics data is typically updated in real time, allowing you to monitor your social media performance continuously and make timely adjustments to your strategy.

**Q: Are there any tips for interpreting the analytics data effectively?**When interpreting analytics data, focus on key performance indicators (KPIs) that align with your goals. Look for patterns over time, compare similar posts, and consider external factors that may influence engagement.

**Q: What time range can I view in Social Planner Analytics?**You can currently view analytics data on a weekly basis only.

---

title_en: Understanding Attribution Source
source_md:
In the article below, we will walk through attribution in HighLevel and even where to go to set up your ad reporting. Let's hop in!

[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/JKiU8xDCAaI?&wmode=opaque)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Attribution?](#What-is-Attribution?)
- [What is "First" or "Latest" Attribution?](#What-is-)
- [Where to Locate Contact Attribution Data?](#Where-to-Locate-Contact-Attribution-Data?)
- [Types of Attribution Sources](#Types-of-Attribution-Sources)
  - [Paid Search (Google Ads)](#Paid-Search-(Google-Ads))
  - [Paid Social (Facebook & Instagram Ads)](#Paid-Social-(Facebook-&-Instagram-Ads))
  - [Direct Traffic](#Direct-Traffic)
  - [Organic Search](#Organic-Search)
  - [Social Media](#Social-Media)
  - [Referrals](#Referrals)
  - [Others](#Others)
  - [CRM UI](#CRM-UI)
  - [Third-Party](#Third-Party)
- [What Events Record Attribution?](#What-Events-Record-Attribution?)
- [How is Attribution Source Determined?](#How-is-Attribution-Source-Determined?)
- [Ad Reporting Setup](#Ad-Reporting-Setup)
  - [Facebook and Instagram Ads Reporting Setup](#Facebook-and-Instagram-Ads-Reporting-Setup)
  - [Google Ads Reporting Setup](#Google-Ads-Reporting-Setup)
- [Troubleshooting Ad Reporting Issues](#Troubleshooting-Ad-Reporting-Issues)

---

# **What is Attribution?**

Attribution provides a breakdown of which channels or sources a contact came from. With this information, we will be able to identify growth opportunities and determine which channels offer the most potential.

For example, if we are running Facebook and Google Ads, we would like to know which is more effective at generating leads into HighLevel. Attribution can make this happen.

---

## **What is "First" or "Latest" Attribution?**

When attributing a contact to a specific source it is common to consider the first and lastest attribution. Both are always stored on every single contact.

**First Attribution** - is the first time a contact interacts with our system, when this happens we record attribution data for that session. For example: Someone fills out a Contact Us Form.

**Latest Attribution** - is the most recent recorded interaction with us, when this happens we record attribution data for this most recent session as well. For example: After filling out a Contact Us form they then decide to purchase our product via a HighLevel Two-Step Order Form. When this happens, the latest attribution data will be recorded.

*\*The latest attribution will always change based on the last recorded interaction. However, the first attribution will not.*

Now that we know what First and Latest Attribution is, we need to know where it is stored.

---

# **Where to Locate Contact Attribution Data?**

Rather it is the first or latest attribution data, you can locate this information in the bottom right of all contacts from the contact record.

Within the Sub-Account, go to Contacts > select a **contact record** > then locate the attribution data at the bottom right column under the **activity** tab.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48247964170/original/VSgXZHb-pBWW3cGC7emsU4xKKLFyaKQJ3g.gif?1661800754)

### 

**For contact creation, the first and latest attribution is defined as:**

```
- First attribution: The contact's first interaction is recorded in the system. This is usually their first visit to your website or an interaction with any of the sources listed above.  
  
- Latest attribution: The contact's last interaction before they were converted to a contact in the system
```

---

#### 

# **Types of Attribution Sources**

Below we will walk through each of the Attribution Sources you will see on the contact’s ***First******Attribution***or ***Latest Attribution***value will be one of the following:

- [Paid Search](#Paid-Search)
- [Paid Social](#Paid-Social)
- [Direct Traffic](#Direct-Traffic)
- [Organic Search](#Organic-Search)
- [Social Media](#Social-Media)
- [Referrals](#Referrals)
- [Others](#Others)
- [CRM UI](#CRM-UI)
- [Third-Party](#Third-Party)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155015178854/original/LaAFs5bfFxyo0Su56GWkBEkyyD7o2l6oQA.png?1702496706)

## **Paid Search (Google Ads)**

Traffic categorized under *Paid search* comes from paid search campaigns (e.g., Google AdWords). This will help in analyzing the Google Ad Reporting.

**It needs to have the UTM parameters matching (It is case-sensitive)**

{YourLandingPageUrl.com}?utm\_source=adwords&utm\_medium={adname}&utm\_campaign={campaignname}&utm\_content={adgroupname}&utm\_keyword={keyword}&utm\_matchtype={matchtype}&campaign\_id={campaignid}&ad\_group\_id={adgroupid}&ad\_id={creative}

Google Ads UTM Parameters

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | **Key** | **Value** | **Type** | **Example** |
| UTM Source | utm\_source | adwords |  |  |
| UTM Medium | utm\_medium | {adname} |  |  |
| UTM Campaign | utm\_campaign | {campaignname} | manual, changeable | summer\_sale |
| UTM Content | utm\_content | {adgroupname} |  |  |
| Match Type | utm\_matchtype | {matchtype} |  |  |
| Campaign ID | campaign\_id | {adgroupid} | set by Google Ads, constant | 123456789 |
| Ad Group ID | ad\_group\_id | {adgroupid} |  |  |
| Ad ID | ad\_id | {creative} |  |  |

For more information, see[How to Set Up Google Ad Reporting](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219312-how-to-set-up-google-ad-reporting).

## **Paid Social**

Traffic categorized under *Paid social* comes from a paid social campaign. This will help in analyzing the Facebook Ad Reporting if the leads are coming from Facebook

**It needs to have the UTM parameters matching (It is case-sensitive)**

{YourLandingPageUrl.com}?utm\_source=fb\_ad&utm\_medium={{adset.name}}&utm\_campaign={{campaign.name}}&utm\_content={{ad.name}}&campaign\_id={{campaign.id}}

Facebook and Instagram Ads UTM Parameters

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | **Key** | **Value** | **Type** | **Example** |
| UTM Source | utm\_source | fb\_ad |  |  |
| UTM Medium | utm\_medium | {{adset.name}} |  |  |
| UTM Campaign | utm\_campaign | {{campaign.name}} | manual, changeable | summer\_sale |
| UTM Content | utm\_content | {{ad.name}} |  |  |
| Campaign ID | campaign\_id | {{campaign.id}} | set by Facebook Ads, constant | 123456789 |

For more information see, [How to Setup Facebook Ad Reporting](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001204042-how-to-set-up-facebook-ad-reporting).

## **Direct Traffic**

Traffic categorized under *Direct traffic* does not have an indication of its source (See row 8 above). Typically, these people typed the URL directly in their browser or removed all query parameters before entering a site.

To view the source URLs for these visitors, click the Direct traffic source.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48247964541/original/eIy9MeT34UCvxRzk02GYCS7qwWMvBizWbQ.gif?1661800923)

## **Organic Search**

Traffic categorized under *Organic Search* comes from non-paid search results in known search engines, such as Google, Bing, Yahoo, and Duckduckgo.

To view the keywords used in the search engine, click the Organic search source in the Sources table.

When there are Unknown keywords (SSL), it is likely due to the search engine encrypting user data. For example, Google encrypts all the search terms entered by their users.

## **Social Media**

Traffic categorized under Organic social comes from social media websites or apps. An example is when a visitor shares your content or website on their social media account, and their followers visit your content or visit the links inside your messages on social media.

## **Referrals**

Traffic categorized under Referrals comes from external sites that link to your website. It should not be a search engine or social media site. A referring domain may have multiple pages that link to your site.

## **Others**

When a lead is generated through various channels such as incoming calls, SMS, emails, WhatsApp messages, or Facebook messages, it is important to display all the information in one place. This helps keep track of all the leads and ensures that none fall through the cracks. By having a centralized system to manage all the leads, businesses can ensure they are not missing out on potential customers.

## **CRM UI**

When a lead is created manually through the HighLevel App CRM, its source is defined as this. This categorization helps in identifying leads that were created manually within the HighLevel App CRM only.

## **Third-Party**

When a lead is created by a third-party tool like Zap, its source is defined as this. This categorization helps identify leads created through third-party integration.

---

# **What Events Record Attribution?**

Within the same session, a contact must do one or more of the following actions:

1. Form/Survey Submission
2. Calendar Booking Submission
3. Chat Widget (After Submitting Contact Info)
4. Order Form Submission (One or Two-Step)

HighLevel Forms, Surveys, Calendars, Chat Widgets, and Order Forms capture attribution data when a contact completes a supported action.

Supported third-party forms can also capture attribution data when they are tracked through **External Tracking**. External Tracking automatically detects supported DOM-based forms and captures attribution data such as UTM parameters, page URLs, and session data.

For setup requirements and supported form types, see [Tracking External Forms with GoHighLevel.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006092)

---

# **How is Attribution Source Determined?**

When you want to understand why a contact attribution source was added by HighLevel to the contact, you need to understand what we look for when determining attribution data.

All attribution events follow a set of rules to categorize traffic into a specific source, and we check the full page URL and the referring domain, if available, against these rules.

They are applied in this order:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Order | Rule | Source |
| 1 | The "utm\_source" parameter contains the word “adwords” for Google Ad. | Paid Search |
| 2 | The "gclid", "wbraid" or "gbraid" parameter is present, as they are Google click IDs.  The "msclkid" parameter is present, it is the Microsoft click ID for Bing/Yahoo | Paid Search |
| 3 | The "utm\_source", "utm\_medium", or "utm\_campaign" parameter is present and the referring domain is google.com. | Paid Search |
| 4 | The "utm\_source" parameter contains the word “fb\_ad” for Facebook Ad.  We have deprecated utm\_source=facebook, **please use "fb\_ad". The "utm\_source" parameter contains the word “linkedin\_ad” for Linkedin Ads, "twitter\_ad" for Twitter Ads and "reddit\_ad" for Reddit.** **The "ctwa\_clid" is present for whatsapp conversations** | Paid Social |
| 5 | The referring domain is a social media site. | Social Media |
| 6 | Referring domain is a search engine. (Google, Yahoo, Bing, Duckduckgo) | Organic Search |
| 7 | Referring domain is not a social media site or search engine. | Referral |
| 8 | No referring domain or tracking URL. | Direct Traffic |
| 9 | This shows up if the lead came from an Incoming Call/SMS/Email/WhatsApp/Facebook message or any other source not covered above. | Others |
| 10 | Lead is manually created within the CRM system | CRM UI |
| 11 | Lead is generated from a third-party integration tool like Zap | Third-Party |

Now that we can see how HighLevel chooses to apply a specific attribution source, let's walk through each attribution source together.

---

# **Ad Reporting Setup**

When you need to set up your Paid Ads attribution tracking, please see the following documentation for Facebook, Instagram, and Google Ads Set Up.

## Facebook and Instagram Ads Reporting Setup

To set up Facebook and Instagram ads attribution, please visit [Facebook Ad Reporting Setup](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001204042-how-to-set-up-facebook-ad-reporting).

Additional Facebook Ads Resources

[How to set up a Funnel Event Pixel for Facebook Conversion API](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001236281-how-to-set-up-a-funnel-event-pixel-for-facebook-conversion-api-)

[How to set up and install a Meta Pixel](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/952192354843755?id=1205376682832142)

[Facebook Conversion Leads Walkthrough](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001233833-facebook-conversion-leads-walkthrough)

[Facebook Conversions API Trigger in Workflows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001185099-facebook-conversions-api-trigger-in-workflows)

## Google Ads Reporting Setup

To set up Google Ads Attribution, please visit [Google Ad Reporting Setup](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219312-how-to-set-up-google-ad-reporting).

Additional Google Ads Resources

[Google Analytics 4 Tracking](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001234199-google-analytics-4-tracking)

[Understanding Google Ad Reporting Terminology](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219241-understanding-google-ad-reporting-terminology)

[Troubleshoot Guide For Google Ad Reporting](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219996-troubleshoot-guide-for-google-ad-reporting)

For any additional assistance, you can contact us 24/7. In addition, please note you may need to consult an ad specialist for more advanced reporting and attribution setup for external reporting and attribution tracking.

---

# **Troubleshooting Ad Reporting Issues**

If your attribution data is not being recorded in HighLevel after you have set up your [Facebook or Instagram Ad Reporting](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001204042-how-to-set-up-facebook-ad-reporting) or your [Google Ad Reporting](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219312-how-to-set-up-google-ad-reporting), we can try the following troubleshooting steps to fix this...

1. **Check for Spaces or Misspellings in the Final URL**

   When creating your UTM parameters, be sure to check for any misspellings, extra spaces from copying, or case sensitivity. The examples provided should be used, it is best to copy and paste them. Take a moment to confirm it was done correctly. Also, the examples are case sensitive, meaning an upper case or lower case being present where it shouldn't be will cause errors in attribution.

   Final URL = The URL a contact clicks on from their ad, which takes them to where they take the next action on your site or form.
2. **Confirm that Submissions Happen on the Final URL**For the UTM parameters to be recorded, when a user lands from an ad they cannot move from this page. For example, if someone lands on a page and then clicks a button that moves them to another page to submit a form, no attribution data from URMs can be added. So we need to keep them on this page when they fill out the form.  
     
   A workaround would be to add a pop-up or a section with the submission form to ensure the data is captured.
3. **Do NOT add any custom UTM parameters to Facebook, Instagram, or Google Ads. Please be sure to use our HighLevel UTM templates as instructed in the setup directions.**  
   Please do not add custom UTM parameters to the templated examples provided in the setup guides. This could cause issues and may result in missing data or failure to record any data.

title_en: RCS Sender Registration & Verification Guide
source_md:
RCS Messaging Compliance

RCS Sender Registration & Verification Guide

Everything you need to register an RCS sender: Google registration, country-specific checks, and Aegis verification for US carriers.

Overview

Rich Communication Services (RCS) allows businesses to send branded, interactive messages to customers. Unlike traditional SMS, RCS supports verified business profiles, brand logos, images, buttons, and other rich messaging features.

Before a business can start sending RCS messages, its sender must complete a registration and verification process. This helps ensure that businesses are legitimate, recipients have provided appropriate consent, and messaging campaigns comply with carrier requirements.

RCS registration involves two main stages: **Google RCS Registration** and **Country-Specific Registration**, where applicable. For US carriers, this includes **Aegis verification**.

## Understanding the Two-Part Registration Process

Part A · Mandatory

Google RCS Registration

Google RCS registration is mandatory for all businesses that want to send RCS messages, regardless of the country in which they operate. During this process, businesses must provide the following information:

**Business Information**

- Business or brand name
- Official business website
- Business contact information
- Business description and industry

**Authorized Representative**

- Full name of the authorized representative
- Business email address
- Contact information
- Role or designation within the company

**Opt-In and Opt-Out Information**

- How customers provide consent to receive RCS messages
- Where the opt-in process takes place, such as a website form, booking page, or registration form
- How customers can unsubscribe from future messages
- Links to the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service

**Messaging Use Case**

- Purpose of the messages
- Types of messages customers will receive
- Events or actions that trigger messages
- Sample messages demonstrating the intended communication

**Notification Settings**

- Email address or contact details for receiving registration updates and notifications

Important

The opt-in process must be live and accessible during registration. Carriers or verification teams may test the opt-in flow to confirm that customers are providing appropriate consent.

Part B · Where Applicable

Country-Specific Registration

Depending on the destination country, additional registration and verification may be required. For example, businesses sending RCS messages to major US carriers must complete additional verification requirements.

For US registration, businesses generally need to provide:

**Legal Business Information**

- Registered legal business name
- Employer Identification Number (EIN) or applicable registration number
- Registered business address
- Business industry and company type
- Official business website

The information submitted should match the company's official registration records.

**Campaign Information**

- Description of the messaging campaign
- Intended audience
- Message triggers
- Sample messages
- Opt-in and opt-out process

**Additional Verification (Aegis)**

For US carrier registration, Aegis, a third-party verification provider, may verify the business and its authorized representative. See [Section 2: Aegis Verification](#section-2) for full details.

Note

Failure to provide accurate information may result in registration delays or requests for additional documentation.

## Aegis Verification for US Carriers

**Aegis** is a third-party brand verification (vetting) provider used by major US carriers to confirm that a business sending RCS messages is legitimate before its sender is launched on their networks. If you plan to send RCS messages to US recipients, expect your registration to go through Aegis verification in addition to Google's review.

**What Aegis verifies**

**Business identity** — the legal business name, EIN or registration number, and registered address match official records.

**Brand and website** — the brand name and website are live, belong to the business, and accurately represent it.

**Authorized representative** — the listed contact is a real person who works for the business and is authorized to register on its behalf. Agency cannot put their email id for this verification.

**Use case and consent** — the messaging use case follows carrier policies and the opt-in process meets CTIA messaging guidelines.

**How Aegis verification works**

Stage 1

Registration is forwarded for vetting

Once your submission passes the initial review, the US registration details are sent for Aegis verification.

Stage 2

Business records are checked

Aegis compares the legal business information, website, and brand details against official and public records.

Stage 3

The authorized representative is contacted

Aegis may email the authorized representative to confirm their identity and that the business has requested the RCS sender. The representative should respond as soon as possible — an unanswered request can stall the registration.

Stage 4

Results are shared with carriers

The verification outcome is passed to the US carriers, which use it in their final approval decision.

**To pass Aegis verification, make sure that:**

- The authorized representative uses a **company-branded email address** on the same domain as the business website.
- The business details match official registration records exactly.
- The messaging use case complies with applicable carrier policies.
- The opt-in process meets applicable CTIA messaging guidelines and is live for testing.

Common Reasons Aegis Verification Fails

- The legal business name or address does not match EIN or state registration records.
- The representative uses a free email address (for example, Gmail or Yahoo) instead of a business domain.
- The website is not live, is under construction, or does not match the brand name.
- The opt-in flow cannot be accessed or tested by reviewers.
- The authorized representative does not respond to the verification email.

Tip

Ask your authorized representative to watch their inbox (including spam and promotions folders) after submission so the Aegis verification email isn't missed.

## How the RCS Registration Process Works

The registration process follows several stages.

Step 1

Submit the Registration

The business completes the required Google RCS and country-specific registration details through the applicable registration interface.

Step 2

Initial Review

Our compliance team reviews the submitted information for completeness and compliance before forwarding the application for the relevant verification and approval processes. During this review, the team may identify:

- Missing or incorrect business information
- Incomplete messaging use cases
- Unclear opt-in language
- Missing Privacy Policy or Terms of Service links
- Incorrect branding assets

If changes are required, the business may be asked to update the application.

Step 3

Google, Aegis, and Carrier Review

After the initial review, the registration is evaluated by Google and the applicable carriers or verification providers — including Aegis for US carriers. The review may include:

- Verification of business identity
- Validation of the brand name and branding assets
- Confirmation of the authorized representative (Aegis, for US)
- Testing of the opt-in process
- Review of sample messages and campaign descriptions
- Confirmation of compliance with applicable messaging policies

Carriers may request clarification or additional information before approving the sender.

Step 4

Approval and Activation

Once all applicable approvals are completed, the RCS sender can be activated for supported destinations. The business can then begin sending RCS messages using the approved sender, subject to platform availability and carrier support.

Note

Google approval alone does not necessarily mean that the sender is approved for every country or carrier. Additional country-specific approvals, such as Aegis verification for US carriers, may still be required.

## Key Requirements for Successful Registration

Requirement 1

Branded Sender Identity

RCS messages are associated with a branded sender profile rather than relying solely on a traditional phone number. Businesses should prepare:

- Official brand name
- Business logo
- Banner image
- Business description
- Official website

Branding information should accurately represent the business.

Requirement 2

Clear and Explicit Opt-In

Customers must understand that they are consenting to receive messages from the business. The consent language should clearly mention:

- The business or brand name
- Types of messages customers will receive
- Message frequency, where applicable
- Message and data rates, where applicable
- How customers can opt out

For website forms, the messaging consent checkbox should be **unchecked by default** so customers actively provide consent.

Example Opt-In Language

"I agree to receive text messages from [Business Name], including appointment reminders, account updates, and promotional offers. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to unsubscribe or HELP for assistance. View our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service."

Consent for promotional messages should be obtained where required, and consent should not be made a condition of purchase when applicable rules prohibit it.

Requirement 3

Functional Opt-In and Opt-Out Processes

The opt-in flow must be accessible and functional during verification. Businesses should ensure that:

- The opt-in form is publicly accessible or can be tested by reviewers.
- Consent is clearly presented before submission.
- Customers can unsubscribe by replying STOP.
- HELP requests receive appropriate assistance information.
- Opted-out contacts are excluded from future messages.

Requirement 4

Clear Messaging Use Case

The messaging use case should explain why messages are sent and what recipients can expect. For example:

**Use Case:** Appointment confirmations and reminders.

**Description:** Customers who book appointments through the business website and explicitly consent to receive messages will receive booking confirmations, appointment reminders, and scheduling updates.

**Sample Message:**

"Hi [First Name], your appointment with [Business Name] is confirmed for [Date] at [Time]. Reply here if you need assistance. Reply STOP to unsubscribe."

The submitted sample messages should accurately reflect the messages the business intends to send.

## Tracking Registration Status

Businesses can monitor their registration status through the registration interface in the platform. Depending on the registration stage, the sender may have statuses such as:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | Registration has not yet been submitted. |
| Pending review | The application is being reviewed. |
| Action required | Additional information or corrections are needed. |
| Approved | The applicable registration has been approved. |
| Rejected | The registration did not meet the applicable requirements. |

Good to Know

Status names may vary depending on the provider and registration stage. Businesses may also receive email notifications when their registration status changes or additional action is required.

## Best Practices to Avoid Registration Delays

To improve the chances of successful registration:

1. **Verify business details:** Ensure that the legal name, address, and registration information match official business records.
2. **Use a branded business email:** Provide an authorized representative's email address associated with the business domain, especially for US (Aegis) verification.
3. **Respond to Aegis promptly:** Make sure the authorized representative watches for and replies to any verification email from Aegis.
4. **Keep the opt-in flow live:** Make sure reviewers can access and test the consent process.
5. **Use clear consent language:** Identify the business, message purpose, and unsubscribe instructions.
6. **Provide accurate sample messages:** Samples should match the messaging use case described in the application.
7. **Prepare appropriate branding assets:** Use clear, high-quality logos and banners that meet the provider's specifications.
8. **Review compliance requirements:** Ensure that messages follow applicable local regulations and carrier policies.
9. **Monitor registration updates:** Respond promptly to requests for corrections or additional documentation.

You're All Set

RCS registration ensures that businesses are verified and that their messaging practices meet Google, carrier, and applicable regulatory requirements. The process consists of Google RCS registration and any additional country-specific verification, such as Aegis verification for US carriers.

Once the necessary approvals are obtained and the sender is activated, the business can begin communicating with customers through RCS on supported networks and devices.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is Google RCS registration required for every business?

Yes. Businesses must complete the applicable Google RCS sender registration before sending RCS business messages.

Q: Is country-specific registration mandatory?

It depends on the destination country and its carrier requirements. For example, additional verification is required for major US carriers.

Q: What is Aegis, and why is it verifying my business?

Aegis is a third-party verification provider used by major US carriers. It confirms that your business, website, and authorized representative are legitimate before your RCS sender is approved for US networks.

Q: Do I need Aegis verification if I don't send messages to the US?

No. Aegis verification applies to US carrier registration. Other countries may have their own country-specific requirements.

Q: Can I use a Gmail or Yahoo address for the authorized representative?

This is not recommended. Use a company-branded email address on the same domain as your business website. Free email addresses are a common reason for Aegis verification delays or failures.

Q: What should the authorized representative do if they receive an email from Aegis?

Respond as soon as possible and follow the instructions in the email. Verification may not proceed until the representative confirms their identity and the registration request.

Q: Can I start sending messages immediately after submitting the registration?

No. The sender must complete the applicable approval and activation process before sending RCS messages.

Q: What happens if my registration is rejected?

The registration may need to be corrected and resubmitted. Common reasons include inconsistent business information, unclear opt-in processes, insufficient campaign details, or compliance concerns.

Q: Do carriers verify the opt-in process?

Yes. Reviewers may test the opt-in flow to ensure that customers are providing appropriate consent.

Q: How long does RCS registration take?

The approval timeline varies depending on the country, carrier, completeness of the application, and whether additional verification (such as Aegis) is required. There is no single guaranteed approval timeline.

Q: Is RCS registration tied to a phone number?

No. RCS business messaging uses a branded sender identity. Registration is associated with the business and its sender profile rather than an individual SMS phone number.

title_en: Email Statistics – Summary Page
source_md:
The Email Statistics Summary Page in HighLevel provides a detailed overview of an individual email campaign's performance. It helps you track email delivery, opens, clicks, bounces, unsubscribes, and other important engagement metrics. You can also analyze engagement trends, review attributed conversions and revenue, and examine recipient-level activity. These insights help you evaluate campaign effectiveness, identify delivery issues, and make informed decisions to improve future email campaigns.

The Summary Page is part of the individual campaign statistics experience. Unlike the unified Email Statistics dashboard, which combines data from Email Campaigns, Workflows, and Bulk Actions, the Summary Page focuses on the performance of a specific email campaign.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Key Benefits of the Email Statistics Summary Page](#Key-Benefits-of-the-Email-Statistics-Summary-Page)
- [Understanding Email Summary Metrics](#Understanding-Email-Summary-Metrics)
- [Engagement Analysis Chart](#Engagement-Analysis-Chart)
- [How to Interpret the Engagement Analysis Chart](#How-to-Interpret-the-Engagement-Analysis-Chart)
- [How to Access the Email Statistics Summary Page](#How-to-Access-the-Email-Statistics-Summary-Page)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **Key Benefits of the Email Statistics Summary Page**

Understanding how recipients interact with your email campaigns helps you identify what works and where improvements are needed. The Summary Page brings together delivery, engagement, and conversion information, making it easier to evaluate campaign performance without reviewing individual contact records separately.

- **Monitor Email Delivery Performance:** Track delivered, bounced, and skipped emails to identify potential delivery issues and evaluate how effectively your campaigns reach recipients.
- **Measure Recipient Engagement:** Review email opens, clicks, replies, and unsubscribes to understand how contacts interact with your content.
- **Analyze Engagement Trends:** Visualize delivery, open, and click activity over time to recognize engagement patterns and assess campaign performance.
- **Track Conversions and Revenue:** Monitor eligible purchases, attributed revenue, and Revenue per Recipient (RPR) to evaluate how email campaigns contribute to sales.
- **Review Contact-Level Activity:** Identify contacts who opened, clicked, replied, unsubscribed, or experienced delivery issues.
- **Support Data-Driven Improvements:** Use email performance insights to refine audience targeting, messaging, and calls to action for future campaigns.

---

## **Understanding Email Summary Metrics**

The Summary Page displays important email performance metrics that help you evaluate different stages of an email campaign. Reviewing these metrics together provides a clearer picture of delivery success, recipient engagement, and potential issues that may affect campaign results.

**Delivered**

Delivered represents emails that were successfully accepted by recipients' email servers. A delivered email is not necessarily placed in the recipient's primary inbox. It may be routed to another folder, such as Promotions or Spam.

**Delivery Rate Formula:**

(Delivered Emails ÷ Total Emails Sent) × 100

For example, if 950 out of 1,000 sent emails were delivered, the delivery rate would be 95%. A lower-than-expected delivery rate may indicate problems with email addresses, sender reputation, or recipient-server acceptance.

```
Note: Delivery statistics depend on the configured email service provider and the availability of delivery events.
```

**Opened**

Opened represents recipients who triggered a tracked email open event. HighLevel uses unique opens to measure how many individual recipients opened an email, rather than counting every repeated open from the same recipient.

**Open Rate Formula:**

(Unique Opens ÷ Delivered Emails) × 100

For example, if 200 recipients opened an email out of 800 delivered emails, the open rate would be 25%. Open rates can help you evaluate subject lines, sender recognition, and overall audience interest.

```
Important: Open tracking relies on supported tracking methods and email client behavior. Privacy features, such as automatic image loading, can affect open statistics. A recorded open does not guarantee that the recipient read the email.
```

**Clicked**

Clicked represents recipients who interacted with tracked links in an email campaign. Unique clicks count each recipient once for applicable click activity, even when they click multiple times.

**Click Rate Formula:**

(Unique Clicks ÷ Delivered Emails) × 100

For example, if 80 recipients clicked a link out of 800 delivered emails, the click rate would be 10%. Click activity can help you evaluate the relevance of your email content, offers, and calls to action.

**Note:** Click statistics depend on supported link tracking and the configured email sending provider.

**Conversion**

Conversion represents eligible purchases or conversions attributed to an email campaign based on HighLevel's email attribution rules. HighLevel uses qualifying email interactions and a configurable attribution window to determine whether a purchase should be credited to a campaign.

The default attribution window is five days. The conversion or order rate represents the proportion of eligible recipients associated with attributed conversions, using the calculation applicable to the reporting view.

A conversion may not be attributed to the campaign if the purchase occurs outside the configured attribution window or does not meet the attribution requirements. For additional details, see [Understanding Email Conversion and Revenue Attribution](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001701-understanding-email-conversion-and-revenue-attribution).

**Soft Bounced**

Soft Bounced represents emails that could not be delivered because of a temporary issue. Common reasons include:

- The recipient's mailbox is full.
- The recipient's email server is temporarily unavailable.
- The receiving server is experiencing a temporary delivery problem.

Soft bounces may be retried depending on the email provider's delivery behavior. A temporary delivery failure does not always indicate that the recipient's email address is invalid.

**Hard Bounced**

Hard Bounced represents emails that could not be delivered because of a permanent delivery issue. Common reasons include:

- An email address does not exist.
- A recipient's domain is invalid.
- The receiving server permanently rejects the message.

Hard bounces can indicate problems with contact information or email list quality. Regularly reviewing invalid addresses and maintaining a clean contact list can help protect email sending health.

**Unsubscribed**

Unsubscribed represents recipients who opted out of future email communications using the unsubscribe mechanism in an email.

**Unsubscribe Rate Formula:**

(Unsubscribed Recipients ÷ Delivered Emails) × 100

For example, if five recipients unsubscribe from 1,000 delivered emails, the unsubscribe rate would be 0.5%. An increase in unsubscribes may indicate that the content is not relevant to the audience or that emails are being sent too frequently.

**Skipped**

Skipped represents emails that HighLevel did not attempt to send to certain recipients because of an applicable restriction or sending issue. Possible reasons include:

- The contact has an applicable Do Not Disturb (DND) setting.
- The contact is excluded from the send because of an applicable restriction.
- An internal processing issue prevents the sending attempt.

Skipped emails differ from bounced emails because a bounce occurs after an email delivery attempt reaches the sending or receiving process.

Review skipped recipients to identify whether contact settings or sending restrictions prevented delivery.

**Spam**

Spam represents email messages reported as spam by recipients. Spam complaints are an important indicator of recipient dissatisfaction and may affect sender reputation.

An increase in spam complaints may suggest problems with audience relevance, sender recognition, or messaging expectations.

To reduce complaints, send emails to appropriate audiences, make messages relevant, and provide a clear unsubscribe option.

---

## **Engagement Analysis Chart**

The Engagement Analysis Chart helps you visualize how recipients interact with an email campaign over time. Comparing delivery, open, and click activity can reveal changes in engagement and help you evaluate the timing and effectiveness of your campaign.

The chart displays three main engagement metrics:

- **Delivered:** Shows recorded successful email deliveries.
- **Opened:** Shows recorded email open activity.
- **Clicked:** Shows recorded email link-click activity.

These metrics are represented by separate lines, allowing you to compare engagement activity over the available reporting period.

---

## **How to Interpret the Engagement Analysis Chart**

The chart can help you recognize engagement patterns and identify opportunities to improve future campaigns.

- **Review Delivery Activity:** Identify when email deliveries were recorded and whether delivery activity occurred as expected.
- **Compare Opens and Clicks:** Examine whether recipients who opened the email also interacted with its links.
- **Identify Engagement Patterns:** Look for periods of increased or decreased engagement to understand when interactions occurred.
- **Evaluate Campaign Content:** If the campaign records opens but relatively few clicks, consider whether the message and call to action encouraged recipients to take the intended next step.

```
Note: Engagement peaks indicate when activity was recorded. They do not necessarily identify the best time to send future emails. Consider audience behavior, campaign content, and additional reporting data before making scheduling decisions.
```

---

## **How to Access the Email Statistics Summary Page**

Accessing the individual campaign statistics page allows you to review a specific email send rather than the combined performance of multiple campaigns. Selecting the correct campaign ensures that the delivery, engagement, and conversion data you analyze belongs to the intended email.

Follow these steps:

1. Navigate to **Marketing → Emails** in your HighLevel sub-account.
2. Select the **Campaigns** tab to view your email campaigns.
3. Locate the sent email campaign you want to analyze.
4. Click the **three-dot menu (⋮)** next to the campaign name.
5. Select **Statistics** from the menu.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083298457/original/qEOsV3gDYXMpwH1eZgWZlFwG5oAF3qZdLg.png?1791977225)
6. In the statistics side panel, click **Load More Statistics**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083298546/original/GxeKBZ3WCh0w_soyPXpsYXd1NMRWQZAB2w.png?1791977267)
7. On the full statistics page, select the **Summary** tab.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083298924/original/__1MaXuAwnu-yxXrjav_mcESE5__qPSTXw.png?1791977410)
8. Review the available delivery, engagement, and conversion metrics.
9. Open the **Details** tab as you scroll down when you need to review activity associated with individual recipients.

```
Note: Campaign statistics become available as sending and engagement events are recorded. Some metrics may take additional time to appear, and reporting availability depends on the sending provider and tracking configuration.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why are some email statistics missing even though my campaign was sent?**

Missing statistics can result from the configured email provider, tracking settings, or unavailable reporting events. Some SMTP providers expose only open and click information, while LC Email and Mailgun support more comprehensive delivery reporting. Confirm the sending method and provider configuration if expected metrics are missing.

**Q: Why does my campaign show opens but no clicks?**

Recipients may open an email without clicking its links. Also, open tracking and click tracking use different events, so their results may not match. Review your email's links and confirm that the sending configuration supports click tracking.

**Q: Why are my open statistics higher than expected?**

Some email clients automatically load tracking images or use privacy features that can generate recorded open events. As a result, open statistics may not precisely represent the number of people who actually read the email.

**Q: Why does my conversion summary show $0 even though recipients clicked my email?**

Clicks alone do not generate attributed revenue. The campaign must receive credit for an eligible purchase under HighLevel's attribution rules. Revenue can remain at zero if no eligible purchase was recorded, the purchase occurred outside the attribution window, or another campaign received attribution.

**Q: What is the difference between Skipped, Failed, and Bounced emails?**

Skipped generally means the email was not sent because of an applicable restriction or processing issue. Failed indicates an error during sending or processing. Bounced means the email encountered a delivery failure, which may be temporary (soft bounce) or permanent (hard bounce).

**Q: Why does the number of delivered emails differ from the number of targeted recipients?**

Some recipients may have been skipped, encountered sending errors, or experienced delivery failures. Review the Details tab to investigate the available status information for those contacts.

**Q: Why do campaign-level statistics differ from the unified Email Statistics dashboard?**

The campaign Summary Page focuses on one individual email campaign, while the unified Email Statistics dashboard can combine data from Email Campaigns, Workflows, and Bulk Actions. Different source selections and reporting date ranges can also affect the results displayed.

**Q: Can I download email statistics for analysis outside HighLevel?**

Yes. Available recipient-level statistics can be reviewed and exported from the campaign Details area. For broader reporting, the unified Email Statistics dashboard supports CSV exports, with download links delivered to the specified email addresses.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Guide to Email Campaign Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002176)
- [Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001215386-email-statistics)
- [Understanding Email Conversion and Revenue Attribution](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001701-understanding-email-conversion-and-revenue-attribution)
- [All-in-One Dashboard for Email Marketing](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005552-how-to-access-the-all-in-one-dashboard-for-email-marketing)
- [Exporting Email Campaign Data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007499-exporting-email-campaign-data)
- [Troubleshooting Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001208601)
