**Q: I don’t see Labs—what should I check?**Verify you’re in the correct context (Agency vs. sub-account) and that your role has permission to access Settings. If you still don’t see Labs, contact your account admin.

**Q: Can I disable a Labs feature later?**Yes, you can just toggle Off the feature from where it was enabled.

**Q: What does “Live in X days” actually mean?**It’s an estimated timeline to general availability and can change based on feedback and development.

**Q: Where should I report bugs vs. feature requests?**Use Submit Feedback on the card for product input and small issues. For urgent support needs that block your team, follow your standard support/ticket workflow.

**Q: Why don’t I see a specific Labs feature in a sub-account?**

A: On eligible plans, your agency may have set the feature to **Hidden** (visibility). Ask an Agency Owner/Admin to change the feature’s visibility, then refresh the sub-account.

**Q: Do all plans have visibility controls?**

A: No. **Unlimited and Pro** support visibility defaults and per-sub-account visibility management. **Starter** keeps Labs features visible by default and does not show visibility controls.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started - Agency Launchpad Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005494)
- [Agency | Managing user roles & permissions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002543)
- [Understanding the Agency Owner Role in Your Agency Account: What You Need to Know](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001237517)
- [How To Connect Stripe To Your Agency Dashboard](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001171910)

title_en: How to Personalize Review Requests Using Custom SMS Templates
source_md:
This article explains how to use custom SMS templates in Reputation Management to send recurring review requests. You’ll learn how to personalize messages with custom tokens, add dynamic images, and manage multiple templates to match your brand’s style. By following these steps, you can create consistent, engaging requests that boost customer responses and grow your reviews.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Custom SMS Template?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Custom-SMS-Template?)
- [Key Benefits of Using Custom SMS Templates for Recurring Review Requests](#Key-Benefits-of-Using-Custom-SMS-Templates-for-Recurring-Review-Requests)
- [How to Set Up Custom SMS Templates for Review Request Campaign](#How-to-Set-Up-Custom-SMS-Templates-for-Review-Request-Campaign)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Custom SMS Template?**

A custom SMS template in HighLevel’s Reputation Management allows you to design and manage the exact messages sent in recurring review requests. You can personalize each message with custom tokens, unique text, and dynamic image links so every recipient gets a message that feels tailored to them. This level of customization helps increase engagement and encourage more customers to leave reviews.

By using custom SMS templates, you can maintain consistent branding, speak in your business’s voice, and deliver visually appealing messages that stand out. Whether you choose a pre-built design or create one from scratch, you have full control over the content and presentation of your review requests.

---

## **Key Benefits of Using Custom SMS Templates for Recurring Review Requests**

Custom SMS templates give you complete control over the look, feel, and personalization of your review requests. You can:

- **Personalized Messaging:** Personalize each SMS with custom tokens and brand-specific language

- **Dynamic Image Personalization:** Add dynamic image URLs that update with contact-specific data, using NiftyImages compatibility for personalized visuals that make requests more eye-catching

- **Flexible Design Options:** Choose from pre-built templates or create one from scratch

- **Simplified Template Management:** Quickly create, edit, and assign templates by customizing the name, message, tokens, and image URLs, ensuring consistent, on-brand follow-ups

- **Streamlined Campaigns:** Automatically assign your preferred recurring SMS template to follow-up campaigns

---

## **How to Set Up Custom SMS Templates for Review Request Campaign**

Follow these steps to configure your custom SMS templates:

**Access Reputation Settings**

From the left-hand menu, select **Reputation** and then click the **Settings** tab at the top of the page. This will open the area where you can manage and customize your SMS review request templates.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051455822/original/eUXZPVyU27fX_1z7NgM7wT01wUP1Pu9G1A.png?1755009716)

**Open SMS Requests**

In the left-hand menu under **Reputation Settings**, select **SMS Requests**. This section contains all options for scheduling, customizing, and managing your recurring SMS review request templates.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051455847/original/t3Z2uDHEsy_61-bTl9eswugt6j0COu00Mw.png?1755009731)

**Enable SMS Review Requests**

Turn on the **SMS Review Requests** toggle to activate template management. This setting allows you to create and customize SMS templates for recurring review requests. If the toggle is off, template creation and editing will be disabled.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051455874/original/aeMjGSNlUdBOISACYMXyMDJ_zer_ZGLKBw.png?1755009745)

**Set SMS Send Timing**

Use the **When to send SMS after check-in?** dropdown to decide how soon a review request is sent after a customer’s check-in. You can choose options like Immediately, 1 Hour, 2 Hours, 4 Hours, or set a Custom delay that fits your follow-up strategy.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051455986/original/F7F2Cejvkrx5yX4RGLaqzYQhVRsDQ8dsEw.png?1755009794)

**Set Repeat Frequency**

In the **Until clicked, repeat this every** dropdown, choose how often the SMS review request should be resent until the recipient interacts with it. Options include fixed intervals like 3 Days, 1 Week, or 1 Month, as well as a Custom option for more flexibility.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456002/original/cA7rasFJl4Yg1SNPfdJ4r7uxDopKNv6rIA.png?1755009814)

**Customize Repeat Interval**

If you selected **Custom** for the repeat frequency, set the exact number and unit of time here. Use the plus/minus buttons to adjust the number, and choose between **Hours** or **Days** to match how often you want follow-up messages to be sent.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456027/original/9cJThKIoIq0OL5dsdbHlK6B8YcJXER_8HQ.png?1755009838)

**Set Maximum Retries**

Use the **Maximum retries** dropdown to choose how many times the system should resend the SMS review request if there’s no interaction. You can select between 1 and 5 retries, depending on how persistent you want your follow-up process to be.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456037/original/dXaVVUyPta9bIpgtqT8gUff1iw8wXWoQ_w.png?1755009855)

**Open Template Settings**

Click **Set SMS Templates** to assign which template will be used for each stage of your recurring review request sequence. This is where you control the exact messages sent at different retry points.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456050/original/090hcvJqjTYcm0VrM3EEPE8WEBMkKd7r6Q.png?1755009876)

**Assign Templates to Each Retry**

In the **Set SMS Templates** window, choose a template for each retry stage in your recurring sequence. You can assign the same template to multiple retries or use different ones to vary your follow-up messages. Once selections are made, click **Save** to apply the changes.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456124/original/Yyo61UKjohz7In32Kv0wedEPEi2fkmwWgA.png?1755009908)

**Create a New Template**

Click **Create New** to start building a fresh SMS template. This option lets you design your own message from scratch or base it on a pre-built template, giving you full control over the content and personalization.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456134/original/D9V78FE1WH-5lINSnjgAAvkem3S8_3RomA.png?1755009926)

**Choose Template Type**

In the **Create a New SMS Template** window, select either **Create New from Scratch** to fully customize your message, or **Select from Pre-Built Templates** to use an existing design as your starting point. This choice determines how you begin building your template.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456138/original/3O2IB2BAoK55mhy0_dfHHFvwKRaGxexbdQ.png?1755009943)

**Build Your Template from Scratch**

When you choose **Create New from Scratch**, you’ll enter the SMS Template Builder where you can design every part of your message:

1. **Name Your Template:**Enter a clear, descriptive name to easily identify the template later.
2. **Enable Image Option:**Toggle **Request with Image** on if you want to include an image in your message.
3. **Upload an Image:**Click to upload an SVG, PNG, or JPG file to visually enhance your request.
4. **Add a Custom Image URL:**Optionally paste a dynamic image link, such as one from NiftyImages, to personalize visuals.
5. **Write Your Message:**Craft your SMS content, using custom tokens (like {{contact.first\_name}}) to personalize text.
6. **Save the Template:**Once satisfied, click **Save** to store your template for future use.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456158/original/1uTQ6yNz2BabHDrEuYF4vVopLooqGKgGWg.png?1755009959)

**Select and Edit a Pre-Built Template**

When you choose **Select from Pre-Built Templates**, the SMS Template Library opens with ready-made options:

1. **Search Templates** – Use the search bar to quickly find a template by name or keyword.
2. **Preview & Choose** – Review the available pre-built templates and select the one that best matches your message style.
3. **Edit if Needed** – Click **Edit Template** to customize the selected template’s content, tone, and personalization before saving.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456190/original/1KHjKaa64tycxIDL-z6rQzIRkOvOpfEXjA.png?1755009976)

**Manage Existing Templates**

In the **Manage Your SMS Templates** section, you can work with your saved templates:

1. **Duplicate a Template** – Click the copy icon to create a duplicate of an existing template, allowing you to refine or modify it without changing the original.
2. **Edit a Template** – Click the pencil icon to open the template in the editor and make updates to its content, images, or personalization settings.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155051456205/original/FJwTulGiXfLiiXPzavbCcZR2fx93cBnWWQ.png?1755009994)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I use different SMS templates for each retry in a recurring review request sequence?**

Yes. In the **Set SMS Templates** window, you can assign a specific template to each retry stage (Retry 1, Retry 2, etc.). This allows you to vary your follow-up messages for better engagement, while still keeping all messages within the same recurring sequence.

**Q: What’s the difference between “Request with Image” and “Add Custom Image URL” in the SMS Template Builder?**

**Request with Image** lets you upload a static image file (SVG, PNG, JPG) that will appear in your SMS. **Add Custom Image URL** lets you insert a link to a hosted image—this can be a dynamic image URL (e.g., from NiftyImages) that changes based on contact-specific data, allowing for more personalized visuals.

**Q: If I choose “Custom” for the repeat frequency, can I use hours instead of days?**

Yes. When you select **Custom** in the “Until clicked, repeat this every” setting, you can choose the exact number of **hours** or **days** between messages. Use the plus/minus buttons to set the desired number, then select your preferred time unit from the dropdown.

**Q: Can I duplicate an existing template and make changes without affecting the original?**

Yes. In the **Manage Your SMS Templates** section, click the copy icon next to a template to create a duplicate. The duplicate is separate from the original, so you can edit it without impacting the original template’s content or settings.

---

## **Related Articles**

- **[How to Send Review Requests](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/48001222668?portalId=48000045315)**
- **[Reputation Management: Personalize Recurring Emails with Custom Templates](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000004716?portalId=48000045315)**
- **[Multi-Channel Review Requests](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000004803?portalId=48000045315)**

title_en: Automatic Company Creation and Enrichment
source_md:
Companies • Contacts • CRM Automation

Automatic Company Creation and Enrichment

HighLevel can automatically associate Contacts with the correct Company using the Contact's Business Name, business email domain, or both. When no matching Company exists, HighLevel can create one and populate its domain, name, and logo. Existing Company associations remain unchanged.

What You'll Learn

Learn how to enable Company automation, choose the recommended matching settings, process existing records, understand the matching order, enrich Companies, and exclude domains.

Important

Turning these settings off stops future automatic processing but does not reverse Companies, associations, domains, or logos that were already created. Remove an incorrect association or Company manually when needed.

# What Is Automatic Company Creation and Enrichment?

Automatic Company Creation and Enrichment connects Contacts to Company records without requiring users to create and associate every Company manually.

Depending on the enabled settings, HighLevel can:

- Associate a Contact with an existing Company.
- Add the Contact's business email domain to an existing Company that does not have one.
- Create a Company when no suitable match exists.
- Populate the new Company's name and logo.
- Apply matching to eligible Contacts and Companies already stored in the sub-account.

## Key Benefits

Automatic matching reduces manual CRM maintenance while helping preserve existing Company records and prevent unnecessary duplicates.

- **Automatic Association:** Connect Contacts to Companies using Business Name or business email domain.
- **Automatic Company Creation:** Create a Company when no appropriate record exists.
- **Existing Record Preservation:** Reuse established Companies before creating new records.
- **Duplicate Prevention:** Keep one Company per domain when duplicate prevention is enabled.
- **Company Enrichment:** Populate the Company Name and Logo when enrichment data is available.
- **Existing-Data Processing:** Add missing domains and associate eligible Contacts already in the CRM.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Review the matching and domain rules before enabling automation so Contacts are associated with the intended Companies.

- Company automation is configured under **Settings → Objects → Companies → Automations**.
- Contacts need business email addresses for email-domain matching.
- A Contact already associated with a Company is not automatically moved.
- Free email domains such as Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook, and iCloud are always excluded.
- Domain matching is exact. For example, `acme.com` and `mail.acme.com` are different domains.
- Each Company can hold one domain.
- Business Name matching ignores letter case, but spelling, spaces, punctuation, and legal suffixes still matter.
- Enrichment is best effort and does not prevent Company creation when a name or logo cannot be found.

## How To Set Up Automatic Company Creation

Configure the automation settings that determine which Contact data is used, whether Companies are enriched, and whether duplicate domains are allowed.

1. Go to **Settings → Objects → Companies**.
2. Under **Automations**, select the settings you want to use:

- **Automatically create and associate companies from contact business names:** Uses the Contact's Business Name.
- **Create companies from contact's email domain:** Uses the domain after the `@` in the Contact's email.
- **Enrich companies automatically:** Attempts to populate the Company Name and Logo.
- **Automatically prevent duplicate companies:** Prevents more than one Company from using the same domain.

3. Select **Save changes**.

> **Default settings:** Create companies from contact’s email domain is turned on by default for new agencies. For existing agencies it stays off until an admin turns it on.

![Company automation settings showing Business Name, email domain, enrichment, and duplicate-prevention options](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081819486/original/A1WqmY1b6BOHjesVyMTrFKiIGwCyQFDXFQ.png?1790312398)

**Recommended configuration:** Enable **Create companies from contact's email domain**, **Enrich companies automatically**, and **Automatically prevent duplicate companies**. Leave Business Name automation off when you want domain matching to remain the primary method.

For details about the domain field and duplicate rules, see [Company domain name field and duplicate prevention](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008829-company-domain-name-field-and-duplicate-prevention).

## How Existing Companies and Contacts Are Processed

When email-domain matching is enabled, HighLevel can update eligible Company and Contact records that already exist in the sub-account. Both processing options are selected by default.

- **Fill in domains for existing companies:** Adds a domain to eligible Companies that do not already have one.
- **Apply to existing contacts:** Associates eligible Contacts with Companies and creates a Company when no suitable match exists.

![Existing-data options for filling Company domains and applying matching to existing Contacts](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081819493/original/i1--ptukqi6sM-uFZmVZxOgdKKAWhx7omQ.png?1790312418)

If both options are selected, HighLevel fills in Company domains first and processes Contacts afterward. This gives Contacts a better chance of matching Companies that already contain Opportunities, notes, associations, or other CRM history.

Domain backfill skips:

- Domains entered manually.
- Free email-provider domains.
- Social and website-builder addresses such as Facebook, LinkedIn, Wix, Squarespace, and Linktree.
- Values that are not valid domains.
- Companies that would conflict by sharing the same domain.

**Background processing:** Processing time depends on the number of records. You can continue working while the update runs.

## How Contacts Are Matched to Companies

HighLevel checks available Contact and Company data in order and stops when the first suitable Company is found.

1. **Existing association:** If the Contact is already associated with a Company, nothing changes.
2. **Business Name:** If Business Name automation is enabled, HighLevel uses or creates a Company with the matching Business Name.
3. **Existing domain:** If a Company already has the Contact's email domain, the Contact is associated with it.
4. **Existing Company without a domain:** If the domain resolves to an existing Company name, HighLevel can reuse that Company and save the domain to it.
5. **No match:** HighLevel creates a Company and stores the domain on the record.

**Matching priority:** If Business Name automation resolves the Company first, later email-domain steps do not run. The domain is not added through that match, which can leave the Company outside domain-based duplicate prevention.

### Example

A Contact with a business email domain is automatically associated with the matching Company.

![Contact record showing an automatically associated Company](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081819524/original/l8uGCgkIn92loDxylfKjZVXNkJINi44rEg.png?1790312456)

The Company record contains the matched domain and, when available, its enriched name and logo.

![Company record showing the Company Name, Logo, and Domain Name](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081819528/original/7a6MEOByoBGT8UzONsrmf2cvT4om0UICeg.png?1790312473)

## Company Enrichment and Domain Exclusions

Enrichment improves newly created Company records, while domain exclusions prevent internal, personal, shared, or unwanted domains from creating Companies.

### Company Names and Logos

- When enrichment succeeds, HighLevel populates the Company Name and Logo from the domain.
- If the domain is not recognized, the Company is still created with its domain.
- When no enriched name is available, the Company name is derived from the domain.
- A missing logo does not prevent Company creation.
- To run a one-time enrichment update for existing Companies, turn **Enrich companies automatically** off, save the change, then enable and save it again.

### Exclude Domains From Automatic Association

Add your own business domain, partner domains, testing domains, or other domains that should not create or associate Companies.

1. Go to **Settings → Objects → Companies**.
2. Under **Create companies from contact's email domain**, select **Exclude domains from automatic association**.
3. Enter the domain by itself, such as `acme.com`.
4. Add it to the exclusion list.
5. Select **Save changes**.

![Company automation settings showing Exclude domains from automatic association](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081820176/original/uKTQQQ6qs-1-noFpf0qrH4TcEroHP438mg.png?1790313838)

**Business Name exception:** Domain exclusions apply to email-domain matching. If Business Name automation is also enabled, a Company can still be created from the Contact's Business Name.

## Troubleshooting

Most unexpected results are caused by excluded domains, existing associations, Business Name priority, or incomplete Company domain data.

**No Company was created**

Confirm the Contact has a business email, the domain is not excluded or a free provider, and the Contact is not already associated with a Company.

**A Company was created from an excluded domain**

Check whether Business Name automation is enabled. The Company may have been created from the Business Name instead of the email domain.

**A duplicate Company was created**

Review the existing Company's domain and Business Name. Differences in spacing, punctuation, legal suffixes, or domain values can prevent a match.

**A Company has no logo**

The domain may not have been recognized, enrichment may have been disabled, or the Company may have existed before enrichment was enabled.

**A Company still has no domain after backfill**

The Company may not have a usable website, may use a free, social, or website-builder domain, or may conflict with another Company using the same domain.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I need a workflow to create Companies from Contact email domains?

No. Once **Create companies from contact’s email domain** is turned on, matching and Company creation run automatically without a workflow.

Q: Should I use Business Name or email-domain matching?

Email-domain matching is recommended for cleaner Company data because domains are less likely to vary between Contacts. Business Name automation remains available when required.

Q: What happens when a Contact has both a Business Name and business email?

If Business Name automation is enabled and resolves the Company, that match takes priority and later email-domain matching does not run.

Q: Does this work with Gmail, Yahoo, or other personal email addresses?

No. Common free email-provider domains are permanently excluded from domain-based Company creation.

Q: Does turning on duplicate prevention merge existing Company records?

No. It prevents new duplicate domains. Existing duplicate Company records must be reviewed and resolved manually.

Q: Will domain backfill overwrite a domain I entered manually?

No. Manually entered Company domains are preserved.

title_en: Conditional Logic in Surveys (v2)
source_md:
Conditional Logic v2 in HighLevel allows you to create personalized surveys that adapt to respondents' answers and product selections. You can show or hide fields, products, and individual product variants, redirect respondents, display custom messages, disqualify leads, or guide users to different survey slides. These capabilities help you build smarter surveys and Order Forms without creating separate experiences for every customer.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Key Benefits of Conditional Logic in Surveys](#Key-Benefits-of-Conditional-Logic-in-Surveys)
- [Available Conditional Logic Actions](#Available-Conditional-Logic-Actions)
- [Product-Level Conditional Logic](#Product-Level-Conditional-Logic)
- [Supported Fields and Operators](#Supported-Fields-and-Operators)
- [How to Set Up Conditional Logic in Surveys](#How-to-Set-Up-Conditional-Logic-in-Surveys)
- [Rule Behavior and Important Considerations](#Rule-Behavior-and-Important-Considerations)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles%E2%80%8B)

---

## **Key Benefits of Conditional Logic in Surveys**

Conditional Logic makes surveys more interactive and relevant by automatically adjusting questions, products, and outcomes based on user responses.

- **Personalized Experiences:** Display relevant questions, products, and content based on customer selections.
- **Smarter Order Forms:** Dynamically show or hide individual products and variants.
- **Automated Lead Qualification:** Qualify or disqualify respondents based on their answers or selected products.
- **Flexible Survey Branching:** Guide respondents to different slides, messages, or URLs.
- **Improved Completion Experience:** Reduce unnecessary questions and irrelevant product options.
- **Simplified Rule Management:** Manage complex conditions using an intuitive rule builder.

---

## **Available Conditional Logic Actions**

Conditional Logic determines what happens when a respondent's answers or selections meet specific conditions. HighLevel supports five actions for creating dynamic survey experiences.

| Action | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Show/Hide Fields | Show or hide fields, elements, individual products, or product variants. |
| Display Custom Message | Display personalized messages based on responses or product selections. |
| Redirect to URL | Redirect respondents to a specific webpage. |
| Disqualify Lead | Disqualify respondents based on predefined criteria. |
| Jump To | Direct respondents to another slide within the survey. |

**Note:** Product-based IF conditions are supported for Redirect to URL, Display Custom Message, Disqualify Lead, and Show/Hide Fields. Jump To remains a separate survey navigation action.

---

## **Product-Level Conditional Logic**

Product-Level Conditional Logic lets you create personalized Order Forms based on the products customers select. Instead of relying only on answers from regular survey fields, you can now use individual products as conditions to control survey outcomes and product visibility.

**Product-Based Conditions**

Individual products can be used as IF conditions across four Conditional Logic actions:

- **Redirect to URL:** Direct customers to a specific webpage based on their selected product.
- **Display Custom Message:** Show a personalized message based on product selection.
- **Disqualify Lead:** Disqualify respondents when a particular product is selected.
- **Show/Hide Fields:** Display or hide fields and supported elements based on selected products.

**Example:** If a customer selects a consultation product, display additional questions about their business requirements.

**Show or Hide Individual Products and Variants**

Previously, Conditional Logic could show or hide the entire Sell Products element. The enhancement adds more precise visibility controls without requiring you to hide the complete product section.

You can now:

- **Show/Hide Entire Products:** Control individual products within the Sell Products element.
- **Show/Hide Product Variants:** Display only specific variations, such as sizes or colors.
- **Apply Conditional Visibility:** Change visible products based on customer responses or selections.
- **Show/Hide the Sell Products Element:** Continue using the existing functionality to control the entire element.

**Example:** An Order Form sells T-shirts in different sizes and colors. Based on a customer's preferences, ConditionalLogic can display only relevant products or variants while hiding unrelated options.

**Availability:** Product-Level Conditional Logic is supported in both old and new Forms & Surveys.

---

## **Supported Fields and Operators**

Conditional Logic supports different field types and operators to evaluate respondent inputs. Choosing the appropriate operator ensures your rules respond correctly to answers and selections.

| Field Type | Supported Operators |
| --- | --- |
| Text | Equal To, Not Equal To, Contains, Starts With, Ends With, Is Empty, Is Filled |
| Number, Score, Monetary | Equal To, Greater Than, Less Than, Between, Is Empty, Is Filled |
| Date | Equal To, Before, After, Between, Is Empty, Is Filled |
| Dropdown, Radio, Checkbox | Equal To, Not Equal To, Is Empty, Is Filled |
| Terms & Conditions | Is Checked, Is Not Checked |
| File Upload, Signature | Is Empty, Is Filled |

Additional supported visibility elements include Text, HTML, Images, and product-related elements.

```
Note: Calendar fields are not supported. Product-based conditions use the available product selection options in the Conditional Logic builder.
```

---

## **How to Set Up Conditional Logic in Surveys**

Configuring Conditional Logic allows you to control how respondents navigate a survey and which products or fields they see. Before creating rules, ensure the required survey questions, products, variants, and slides are configured.

**Step 1: Open the Survey Builder**

1. Navigate to **Sites > Surveys** in HighLevel.
2. Open an existing survey or create a new one.
3. Add the required questions, slides, and Sell Products element if needed.
4. Click **Conditional Logic** in the Survey Builder.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084140334/original/kH-u_pby8vFjxcuM0J-yK7TD6wXFL3LGHg.png?1792928604)

**Step 2: Create a Conditional Logic Rule**

1. Click **Add New Condition**.
2. Select an action: Show/Hide Fields, Redirect to URL, Display Message, Disqualify Lead, or Jump To.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084140345/original/47yvSUYzPnxxk3NOcP19KBsriq7prWpWGw.png?1792928638)
3. Configure the IF condition using:

   - **Select Field:** Choose a supported survey field or product.
   - **Select State:** Choose the appropriate comparison operator.
   - **Provide Value:** Enter or select the matching value, when required.
4. Add additional conditions using AND or OR if needed.

**Note:** A single rule supports either AND or OR conditions, but not both.

**Step 3: Configure Product Visibility**

To dynamically show or hide products and variants:

1. Select **Show/Hide Fields** as the action.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084140354/original/IbV6T91mGcmtuyje5KWLV9rNt_ENaUKtdA.png?1792928677)
2. Configure the conditions that determine when the rule applies.
3. Choose the visibility target:

   - Entire Sell Products element
   - Individual product
   - Specific product variant
4. Select whether the target should be shown or hidden.
5. Save the rule.

**Example:** If a customer selects "Premium Package," show the premium product options and hide unrelated products.

**Step 4: Save and Test Your Rules**

1. Save the configured conditions.
2. Open the survey preview.
3. Test different responses and product selections.
4. Verify that fields, products, and variants appear or disappear correctly.
5. Test redirects, custom messages, disqualification, and slide navigation where applicable.

---

## **Rule Behavior and Important Considerations**

Conditional Logic evaluates rules in a defined order to determine which actions should occur. Understanding rule priority and feature availability helps prevent unexpected results.

- **Rule Priority:** Rules are evaluated from top to bottom.
- **Submission Actions:** Redirect, Display Message, and Disqualify use the first matching rule.
- **Show/Hide Rules:** Later matching rules can override earlier visibility rules.
- **Jump To:** Rules are evaluated when respondents advance to another slide.
- **AND/OR Conditions:** Each rule supports one connector type.
- **Survey Compatibility:** Conditional Logic v2 is available for newly created or cloned surveys.
- **Product Compatibility:** Product-Level Conditional Logic is available in old and new Forms & Surveys.
- **Snapshots:** Conditional Logic rules are not included in account snapshots.
- **Query Keys:** Survey fields should have unique Query Keys to prevent configuration issues.

**Best Practice:** Preview every survey path and product selection combination before publishing, especially when 

multiple visibility rules control the same products or variants.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I create conditions based on individual product selections?**

Yes. You can use individual products as IF conditions for Redirect to URL, Display Custom Message, Disqualify Lead, and Show/Hide Fields.

**Q: Can I hide individual products without hiding the entire Sell Products element?**

Yes. You can now control individual products while keeping the Sell Products element visible.

**Q: Can I show or hide specific product variants?**

Yes. Conditional Logic supports variant-level visibility, allowing you to display relevant product options based on configured conditions.

**Q: Is Product-Level Conditional Logic available in older Forms and Surveys?**

Yes. The product-level enhancement supports both old and new Forms & Surveys.

**Q: Can I still hide the entire Sell Products element?**

Yes. Existing Show/Hide functionality for the complete Sell Products element remains available.

**Q: Can product selections trigger Jump To actions?**

The product-level enhancement specifically documents four supported actions: Redirect to URL, Display Custom Message, Disqualify Lead, and Show/Hide Fields. Product-based Jump To conditions are not specified in this update.

**Q: What happens when multiple visibility rules match?**

Rules are evaluated from top to bottom, and later matching Show/Hide rules can override earlier ones.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Conditional Logic V2 in Forms](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001314-conditional-logic-v2-in-forms-and-surveys-)
- [Math Calculations in Forms/Surveys](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003634)
- [Survey Create Contact on Partial Completion](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004191)
- [Forms, Surveys & Quizzes - On Submit Message Customisation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007202-forms-surveys-quizzes-on-submit-message-customisation)
- [Getting Started - Create & Sell Products](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005071-getting-started-create-sell-products)

title_en: Tax support in Communities
source_md:
HighLevel Communities now supports tax collection for eligible paid community purchases using the tax settings configured in HighLevel Payments. This helps businesses collect applicable taxes for paid memberships, courses, paid events, and event subscriptions while giving members a clearer checkout experience. Use this guide to understand how Communities tax support works, which settings to review, and how to test tax behavior before selling.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Tax Support in Communities?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Tax-Support-in-Communities?)
- [Key Benefits of Tax Support in Communities](#Key-Benefits-of-Tax-Support-in-Communities)
- [Supported Communities Payment Types](#Supported-Communities-Payment-Types)
- [Automatic Taxes in Communities Checkout](#Automatic-Taxes-in-Communities-Checkout)
- [Manual Tax Rates for Communities Payments](#Manual-Tax-Rates-for-Communities-Payments)
- [Payments and Product Settings to Review](#Payments-and-Product-Settings-to-Review)
- [How To Setup Tax Support in Communities](#How-To-Setup-Tax-Support-in-Communities)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Tax Support in Communities?**

Tax Support in Communities allows eligible Communities payments to use the tax configuration already available in HighLevel Payments. Instead of creating a separate tax setup for Communities, businesses can rely on their existing Payments tax settings for supported paid community purchases.

When taxes are configured in HighLevel Payments, Communities checkout experiences can apply applicable taxes to paid community memberships, courses purchased through Communities, paid Community Events, and event subscriptions. This includes support for automatic taxes based on customer and nexus information, as well as manual tax rates attached where applicable.

---

## **Key Benefits of Tax Support in Communities**

Tax-ready Communities checkouts help businesses monetize memberships, courses, and events with clearer pricing and fewer manual workarounds. Members can review applicable taxes before completing payment, while admins can manage tax setup from the same HighLevel Payments settings used for other payment flows.

- **Transparent pricing:** Members can see applicable taxes before completing checkout.
- **Reduced under-charging:** Taxes can be included upfront, helping businesses charge the correct total at the time of purchase.
- **Centralized tax setup:** Communities uses tax configurations from HighLevel Payments instead of requiring a separate Communities-only tax setup.
- **Support for multiple monetization flows:** Paid memberships, courses purchased through Communities, paid events, and event subscriptions can follow the business’s tax configuration.
- **Flexible tax handling:** Businesses can use automatic taxes, manual tax rates, or a combination of both where applicable.
- **Improved regional selling:** Automatic tax settings can use customer address and nexus configuration to help determine applicable tax.

---

## **Supported Communities Payment Types**

Communities tax support applies to the core ways businesses monetize their communities. Reviewing each supported payment type helps ensure the correct tax settings are applied before members purchase access, register for an event, or enroll in paid learning content.

Supported Communities payment types include:

- **Paid Community Memberships / Paid Groups:** Admins and owners can charge users for access to public or private Community groups. Paid Groups support community monetization through paid access.
- **Courses purchased through Communities:** Community owners and admins can sell courses directly inside Communities through paid course options.
- **Paid Community Events:** Community Events can be free or paid and can be used for workshops, launches, meetups, Q&A sessions, and similar event experiences.
- **Event subscriptions / recurring event access:** When a paid event flow supports recurring access, applicable tax behavior can follow the configured Payments tax setup.

---

## **Automatic Taxes in Communities Checkout**

Automatic taxes help calculate applicable tax based on the customer’s address and the business’s configured tax settings. This is useful for businesses selling across multiple regions because the tax calculation can account for where the customer is located and where the business has configured nexus.

Communities can honor automatic tax settings when automatic taxes are enabled in HighLevel Payments. Automatic taxes in HighLevel are configured from **Payments → Settings → Taxes** and can use nexus addresses, customer location, tax categories, and tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive behavior.

Automatic taxes may consider:

- Customer billing address
- Business nexus addresses
- Product tax category or tax code, where applicable
- Global tax behavior, such as tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive pricing
- Any relevant tax IDs or registrations configured in Payments

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072995457/original/zSNprn-PCArwNbmeDIgw2tQ4zkKPYCD3iw.png?1780657101)

---

## **Manual Tax Rates for Communities Payments**

Manual tax rates are useful when a business needs to apply predefined tax percentages or manage scenarios that are not covered by automatic tax calculation. These rates are created in HighLevel Payments and can be attached to products where applicable.

Manual tax rates are created from **Payments → Settings → Taxes**. HighLevel’s manual tax setup allows users to create a tax name, rate, description, tax ID, and tax agency where needed. Manual rates can also be attached to products using the **Attach Tax Rates** option.

Manual tax rates may be helpful when:

- A specific flat tax rate must be applied
- Automatic tax does not apply to a specific region or scenario
- A business wants additional control over product-level tax behavior
- A product needs one or more manual tax rates attached

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072995536/original/rihONtNm_gohtatiHl0mgf8XeQCZsrJmAQ.png?1780657122)

```
Note: When automatic taxes and manual taxes are both configured, manual rates may help cover scenarios where automatic tax does not apply. Keep invoice-specific exceptions in mind when reviewing behavior across different HighLevel payment flows.
```

---

## **Payments and Product Settings to Review**

Communities tax support depends on correct setup in HighLevel Payments. Reviewing payment settings, tax rules, addresses, and product configuration helps ensure taxes calculate as expected during checkout.

| Setting | What to Review |
| --- | --- |
| **Payment Provider Connection** | Confirm Payments is connected and ready to process community purchases. |
| **Automatic Taxes** | Confirm whether automatic taxes should be enabled under **Payments → Settings → Taxes**. |
| **Nexus Addresses** | Add or review the regions where the business collects tax. |
| **Business Address** | Confirm the location’s business address is accurate. |
| **Product Tax Category** | Review the tax category or tax code for products where applicable. HighLevel tax categories help apply more accurate tax calculations across products, subscriptions, and transactions. |
| **Manual Tax Rates** | Confirm whether manual tax rates should be attached to relevant products. |
| **Tax-Inclusive or Tax-Exclusive Behavior** | Review whether taxes should be included in displayed prices or added on top at checkout. |

Avoid assuming that every paid Communities item uses the exact same product setup path. Review the payment and product configuration connected to each paid Communities item where applicable.

---

## **How To Setup Tax Support in Communities**

Proper setup helps taxes apply correctly before members purchase paid community access, courses, or events. Review your Payments tax settings, then test checkout to confirm the expected total.

1. Go to **Payments → Integrations** and confirm your payment provider is connected.
2. Go to **Payments → Settings → Taxes** and enable **Automatic Taxes** if needed.
3. Add or review your **nexus addresses**, **business address**, and **tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive pricing** settings.
4. Create or review **manual tax rates** if your business uses predefined tax percentages.
5. Review the paid Communities item, such as a paid membership, course, event, or event subscription.
6. Check the related product or payment configuration where applicable, including tax category and attached manual tax rates.
7. Run a test Communities checkout and confirm the subtotal, tax, and final total appear as expected.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072995610/original/8NwlFPH4APkEIhpGwaSggH9tu5v1K8pPrA.png?1780657150)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need to create a separate tax setup for Communities?**  
No. Communities tax support uses tax settings configured in HighLevel Payments for eligible paid Communities purchases.

**Q: Which Communities purchases can support taxes?**  
Supported flows include paid Community memberships, courses purchased through Communities, paid Community Events, and event subscriptions.

**Q: Do taxes apply automatically if I have not configured taxes in Payments?**  
No. Taxes need to be configured in HighLevel Payments before they can apply to eligible Communities checkout experiences.

**Q: Can I use automatic taxes and manual tax rates together?**  
Yes. Businesses can use automatic taxes and manual tax rates where applicable. Manual tax rates may help cover scenarios where automatic taxes do not apply.

**Q: What address is used for automatic tax calculation?**  
Automatic taxes generally use the customer’s address along with the business’s configured nexus addresses and tax settings.

**Q: Why is tax not showing during checkout?**  
Tax may not appear if automatic taxes are disabled, nexus addresses are missing, the customer address is incomplete, manual rates are not attached where needed, or the paid item’s tax configuration has not been reviewed.

**Q: Can taxes be included in the displayed price?**  
Yes. Tax-inclusive pricing can be configured in HighLevel Payments where supported. Review your tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive settings before launching paid Communities offers.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Configure International Automatic Taxes in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005563-how-to-setup-and-use-international-automatic-taxes?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [How-to Add Taxes Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001224104-how-to-add-taxes-overview?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Set Up Taxes for Course Offers in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007801-how-to-set-up-taxes-for-course-offers-in-highlevel?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Paid Groups](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001233-paid-groups?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Paid Courses inside Communities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002135-paid-courses-inside-communities?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: How to Analyze an Agency's Spending on LC Communications
source_md:
Billing & Usage

Agency Spend Analytics for LC Communications

Track, analyze, and manage your agency's spend on LC Phone, LC Email, and WhatsApp — all from one dashboard.

Overview

In your agency account, we provide features that help you analyze your agency's spend on LC Communications (LC Phone, LC Email, WhatsApp, etc.).

## How to check your agency's credit balance

Step 1

Switch to Agency View

Switch to your **Agency View** from the account switcher.

![Switching to Agency View](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48262037925/original/oeNjlf3jhoA6LeYvFAc8lHr15QgtLTe7fw.png?1667918295)

Step 2

Open Agency Settings

Click on **Agency Settings**.

![Agency Settings menu](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48261834015/original/W6NvyvEwHqCuc1MnNr_YRXbTxpLGGJgHjg.png?1667850709)

Step 3

Go to Billing → Wallet & Transactions

Click on the **Billing tab** > **Wallet & Transactions** to see your current credit balance.

![Wallet and Transactions page](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005371766/original/B-yiXc9rcjilpNwHRemOlg3Z_fbhTWyr0Q.png?1692215238)

## What does my agency's credit balance mean?

When you use communication features like SMS, Calls, Voicemail drops, emails, or WhatsApp messages, the cost associated with those communications is deducted from this credit balance. This is sometimes also referred to as a **wallet**.

Please also refer to:

- [LC Phone pricing structure](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001223556-lc-phone-pricing-structure)
- [LC Email pricing structure](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001220605-what-is-lc-email-i-want-to-know-more#LC---Email-Pricing)
- WhatsApp pricing structure (coming soon)

Note

As of Nov 1, 2022, our rates in the US are 10% cheaper than Twilio and approximately 8% cheaper than Mailgun. Thank you to our agencies for the overwhelming response — more power to you.

## Viewing a historical summary of your spend

You can see a detailed, message-by-message log of transactions by clicking on **Detailed Transactions**.

![Detailed Transactions button](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005371794/original/Vr9Y1Zm7N14yg1nZe5hycpBCyV6A6IYQSg.png?1692215282)

This page gives you:

- A unified view of all logs across all your sub-accounts (locations)
- A summary of your month-over-month spend for the last 3 months, broken out by category

![Spend summary by category](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005371944/original/Hc8PqLNSu7EaPOHkxFBYT0iQ2kUMbzgyog.png?1692215382)
![Month-over-month spend detail](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005371932/original/0d46HEaKXh-4VKKHZH0x_qDEnwJwZ8-a6w.png?1692215338)

Expanding all categories gives you a summary of your spending by month for each individual category.

Note

Summary data refreshes once daily, so you may need to wait up to 24 hours for the most accurate reporting.

## Drilling down into a single transaction

We provide a detailed drill-down of each transaction or message, accessible by clicking the transaction ID in the log table.

![Transaction log table](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005372049/original/_pDVo1dTOvElF8Ada-sce5wC_gkGPVmNCQ.png?1692215652)
![Transaction detail drill-down](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005372259/original/xV7_CNrZa7u-aYsXs43_lDOl0I_b8fKVoA.png?1692216263)

## How and when is my card charged?

Based on your auto-recharge rules on the **Agency Settings → Billing** page, we charge your card with the **recharge amount** once your credit balance falls below the **threshold**.

Example 1

![Auto-recharge example 1](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005371956/original/bTjK9GY6rbnURLKw3qJYbHoAjA03txZmeQ.png?1692215425)

This is also the default setting. Here, once your credit balance goes below $10, your agency's credit card is charged $10 to bring your balance up to $20.

Example 2

![Auto-recharge example 2](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005371999/original/Pibi0RvAq-2lS-RffH8af9tSImjAdY1qZQ.png?1692215539)

Here, your agency's card is charged $200 once your credit balance goes below $50, bringing your balance up to $250.

Important

When a charge to your credit card fails, we notify **all agency admins** on the account. SMS, calls, emails, and other communications for all your clients are interrupted if your credit balance drops below $0.

Heads Up

Delays in payment processing can result in a one-time charge for double the recharge amount if your balance falls below $0. If your balance goes negative, the first recharge charge is applied to bring it back above $0. If that charge doesn't raise your balance above the set threshold, a second charge equal to the auto-recharge amount is applied. In total, this could result in a charge of double the recharge amount.

## How can I rebill usage to my clients?

If you're on the Pro plan or higher

LC Communications is designed to work better with SaaS than Twilio or Mailgun. Some inherent benefits include:

- Instantaneous billing (no lag from Twilio webhooks)
- A built-in ramp for new sub-accounts (locations) so a new client doesn't spike your bill — helping your agency's cash flow
- Error rate and bounce rate monitoring to identify bad lists
- Opt-out and unsubscribe monitoring for spam reduction
- Carrier complaint and violation monitoring for AUP violations, protecting sender reputation

On the Pro plan or higher, you can rebill this usage to your clients using SaaS Mode (Phone & Email rebilling), including a markup to make a profit on the rebilling.

What Changed

We no longer apply a markup when rebilling **carrier charges** and **A2P 10DLC charges** — the original charges pass through without any additional markup. If you expected earnings to be exactly 2x, 3x, or 3.5x your spend, note that compliance and carrier fee charges are excluded from markup.

Please refer to:

- [Connecting your agency's Stripe account to collect rebilling payments](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001171910-how-to-connect-stripe-to-your-agency-dashboard)
- [How to enable email rebilling](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001188579-email-re-billing)
- [General SaaS Mode setup and phone rebilling](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001177740-activate-saas-mode-request-payment-and-configure-twilio-rebilling)

Rebilling works so that the platform invoices you for usage, then invoices your clients on your behalf. Funds you collect from clients are deposited into your connected Stripe account.

![Rebilling invoice flow](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48261853138/original/CX077tEWPXWK2FNhPjTfqMc_nCO_fDxkrg.jpg?1667859306)

- Your agency receives an invoice from the platform with platform branding
- Sub-accounts (your client locations) receive an invoice from you, with your logo and branding as configured in your Stripe account

This system is always prepaid, meaning your agency collects money upfront and maintains positive cash flow.

If you're on the Starter or Freelancer plan

You can download a CSV report for the month and charge your clients using platform invoices or an external billing platform.

Note

LC Communication rebilling without markup for Freelancer accounts is planned for a future release.

## How can I download all transactions as a CSV?

You can download all LC Communication (Phone, Email & WhatsApp) charges as a CSV by clicking the export button in the top right.

![Export button for transactions](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005372008/original/XBLz8LAIdJcYErtnYvRi7xhrvykahEQ6Gg.png?1692215595)
![CSV export preview](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005372066/original/82KcMZk5JfAtG-NaW6PUU4Ovi5wYAWlsYQ.png?1692215674)

Pro Tip

This data is for agency users only. Don't share these reports directly with clients — they will see your discounted pricing (platform-to-agency pricing).

![Transaction export sample](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48262038776/original/xNHy_3v37JouzCN7rDB8cwfqYEoIZZcIxg.png?1667918416)

Note

We can provide the last 1,000,000 (1 million) transactions due to storage limits.

## Further analyzing this data

A walkthrough with instructions for deeper cost analysis is coming soon — check back shortly.

## Paying both LC Communications and a previous provider (Twilio or Mailgun/SMTP)

By design, LC Communications (LC Phone & LC Email) is enabled for your clients going forward. This means your existing clients may still be on the old provider (Twilio for calls and SMS, Mailgun/SMTP for emails). During this transition, you may be invoiced both for LC Communications usage and by Twilio, Mailgun, or other SMTP providers for usage on older sub-accounts.

The easiest way to resolve this is to move all existing clients over to LC Phone & LC Email and close out your accounts with other providers.

Important

Certain assets, like call recordings, do not migrate over. If you need access to call recordings or logs for compliance or HIPAA regulations, keep your Twilio account operating in a dormant state.

## FAQ

Q: What happens if a payment fails?

If SMS and email charges are left unpaid, we stop all outbound emails and SMS.

Q: What happens to my balance if I cancel?

We can refund the credit to the credit card linked to your agency account.

Q: My wallet has a balance, but I can't send SMS or email — why?

Your balance needs to stay at or above 50% of your configured "when balance is lower than" threshold for LC Phone and LC Email. If it drops below 50% of that threshold, outbound emails and SMS are stopped.  
  
If your agency sends high volume, raise this threshold so auto-recharge kicks in sooner — otherwise you risk running out of headroom before the recharge triggers.
![Auto-recharge threshold setting](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155005372072/original/kkMQhM9I0LM7_6ejO8X4YfM_BT0bnp_5Wg.png?1692215699)
For example, if "when balance is lower than" is set to $10, your wallet needs to stay above $5 to send outbound emails and SMS. This safeguards the account from going negative.

Q: Can I customize my auto-recharge amount and threshold?

Yes. Both values are configurable from Agency Settings → Billing, so you can tune how often and how much your card is charged based on your sending volume.

Q: Does my credit balance expire?

No, credit balances don't expire — they carry forward and are drawn down as communications are sent across your sub-accounts.

Q: Can I see spend broken out by individual sub-account?

Yes. The detailed transactions log and CSV export both include a unified view across all sub-accounts (locations), so you can filter or sort by client.

title_en: What is CNAM?
source_md:
CNAM (Caller Name Presentation) is a feature in the U.S. public telephone network that associates your phone number with a business or personal name. When you make an outgoing call, this name may be displayed on the recipient’s device. This article explains CNAM requirements, registration steps, and why name display or spam-label removal is not guaranteed.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is CNAM?](#What-is-CNAM?)
- [Key Benefits of CNAM](#Key-Benefits-of-CNAM)
- [CNAM, A2P, SHAKEN/STIR, and Voice Integrity](#CNAM,-A2P,-SHAKEN/STIR,-and-Voice-Integrity)
- [CNAM Registration Requirements](#CNAM-Registration-Requirements)
- [How To Register for CNAM](#How-To-Register-for-CNAM)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is CNAM?**

CNAM, or Caller Name Presentation, is a feature of the U.S. public telephone network that associates a phone number with a registered business or personal name. It adds an identification layer to outbound calling so recipients may see who is calling instead of only seeing a phone number.

When you make an outbound call, the receiving carrier may retrieve the CNAM information associated with your number and display the registered name on the recipient’s device.

```
Important: CNAM name display is not guaranteed. The recipient’s carrier, device, caller ID service, and other carrier policies can affect whether the registered name appears.
```

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080303670/original/GjQJyhvn_U71AjV6S1rka5xmvOT_dvryFQ.png?1788798384)

---

## **Key Benefits of CNAM**

- **Improved caller recognition:** Helps recipients identify the business associated with an outbound phone number.
- **Increased trust:** A recognizable business name can make legitimate calls easier for recipients to identify.
- **Better answer rates:** Clear caller identification may increase the likelihood that contacts answer your calls.
- **Consistent business identity:** Associates your outbound phone number with the business name submitted during registration.

---

## **CNAM, A2P, SHAKEN/STIR, and Voice Integrity**

CNAM is one part of HighLevel’s broader calling trust and compliance tools. Understanding the difference between these registrations helps ensure you use the correct process for your goal.

- **A2P registration:** Supports compliant business messaging and should be completed before beginning the CNAM registration workflow described below.
- **CNAM:** Associates your U.S. phone number with a registered business or personal name.
- **SHAKEN/STIR:** Authenticates caller ID information and helps carriers verify that the caller is authorized to use the number.
- **Voice Integrity:** Helps eligible U.S. phone numbers address reputation and spam-labeling issues with caller ID analytics providers.

CNAM is a separate registration and does not replace A2P, SHAKEN/STIR, or Voice Integrity.

```
Note: For a broader overview of how these calling tools work together, see Branded Calling: Improve Your Phone Number Reputation.
```

---

## **CNAM Registration Requirements**

Accurate business information helps carriers and verification systems validate your CNAM registration. Use information that matches your official business records whenever possible.

Before starting CNAM registration, prepare the following:

- A valid Employer Identification Number (EIN).
- Your exact legal business name.
- Business type.
- Business industry.
- Business email address.
- Business website URL.
- Business region of operations.
- Registered business address.
- Contact information for an authorized representative.
- The business name you want to use as your CNAM display name.

You can also upload your IRS CP575 document in PDF format during registration. HighLevel can use this document to automatically populate information such as your business name, EIN, and address.

**Important registration guidelines:**

- Enter the legal business name exactly as it appears on your tax documents, including suffixes such as LLC or Inc.
- The business registration number/EIN must contain nine digits.
- EINs issued within the last 15 days may be rejected during verification.
- Use an email address on your business domain when possible. Personal email addresses such as Gmail or Yahoo may result in longer approval times.
- Do not use a P.O. Box as the street address.
- For U.S. businesses, the submitted address should match the address shown on the CP575 document.

---

## **How To Register for CNAM**

Completing each registration field accurately helps reduce verification issues and ensures the CNAM record represents the correct business. Follow the Trust Center workflow carefully and make sure your business information matches your official documents.

### **Step 1:** Open CNAM Voice in the Trust Center

1. Log in to the sub-account.
2. Go to **Settings**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/0eXtBos4kGkEW9DXMuTm+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.31.29.png)
3. Open **Phone System**.
4. Go to **Trust Center**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/2FG1DREf2uBLDKSV4sXZ+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.33.40.png)
5. Confirm that your A2P registration has been completed.
6. Locate **CNAM Voice**.
7. Click **Start Registration**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/m5NMlRorLLZgYhVJWIuF+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.37.44.png)

### **Step 2:** Complete Your Business Details

1. Upload your **CP575 PDF**, if available, to automatically populate supported business information.

   You can also enter the information manually.
2. Enter your **Legal Business Name** exactly as it appears on your tax documentation.
3. Select your **Business Type**, such as:  
     
   - Corporation
   - Limited Liability Company
   - Sole Proprietorship
   - Nonprofit Corporation
   - Partnership
   - Cooperative
4. Select your **Business Industry**.
5. Enter your nine-digit **Business Registration Number/EIN**.
6. Enter your **Business Email**.
7. Enter your **Website URL**.
8. Select your **Business Region of Operations**.
9. Click **Continue**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/tf5LDzO45Xzp95d2Gkeq+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.39.11.png)

### **Step 3:** Enter Your Business Address

1. Select the **Country**.
2. Select the **State or Province**.
3. Enter the **Street Address**.
4. Enter the **City**.
5. Enter the **Postal or ZIP Code**.
6. Click **Continue**.

```
Note: Do not enter a P.O. Box as the street address. For U.S. businesses, the address should match the address shown on your CP575 documentation.
```

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/DyhNB674Oq2PTPUUMLtw+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.46.27.png)

### **Step 4:** Add the Authorized Representative

1. Enter the representative’s **First Name**.
2. Enter the **Last Name**.
3. Enter the **Email Address**. (You need to complete OTP verification for email address validation)
4. Enter the **Phone Number**.
5. Enter the representative’s **Job Position**.
6. Click **Continue**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Btc77yxSbLKiEK0FCBE6+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.47.41.png)

### **Step 5:** Complete the CNAM Details

The phone numbers associated with the CNAM registration are automatically linked during the registration workflow.

1. Enter the **CNAM Display Name** you want associated with your outbound calls.
2. Review the certification statement.
3. Check the certification box confirming that:  
     
   - The associated business profile is the originator of the phone calls.
   - The submitted display name represents your business.
4. Click **Submit**.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/3zqCBCleGvwjUbz6tsga+/Screen+Shot+2026-09-07+at+22.49.42.png)

### **Step 6:** Wait for Verification

After submission, the CNAM registration is sent for verification. Once approved, the registered business name may appear when you place outbound calls.

Carrier and device behavior can vary, so approval does not guarantee that every recipient will see your business name.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does CNAM guarantee that customers will see my business name?**

No. CNAM associates a registered name with your phone number, but the receiving carrier, device, service, and caller ID provider determine whether that name is displayed.

**Q: Does CNAM remove a “Spam Likely” label?**

No. CNAM is used for caller-name identification and does not directly remove spam or nuisance labels. If your number has reputation issues, review HighLevel’s Voice Integrity guidance.

**Q: Is CNAM the same as SHAKEN/STIR?**

No. CNAM associates a name with your phone number, while SHAKEN/STIR authenticates caller ID information and helps carriers verify that the caller is authorized to use the number.

**Q: Do I need an EIN to register for CNAM?**

Yes. An EIN is required for the documented CNAM registration process in HighLevel.

**Q: Can a sole proprietor register for CNAM?**

Yes. A sole proprietor can register if they have the required business registration information, including an EIN.

**Q: What happens if my EIN was recently issued?**

An EIN issued within the last 15 days may be rejected during the registration process because verification systems may not yet recognize the new information.

**Q: Can I use a Gmail or Yahoo email address for registration?**

You can enter the requested business email information, but using an email address associated with your business domain is recommended. Personal email domains may result in longer approval times.

**Q: Why is my business name still not showing after CNAM approval?**

CNAM information is retrieved and displayed by receiving carriers, and not every carrier or device handles CNAM data the same way. Approval therefore does not guarantee that the registered name will appear on every call.

**Q: Should I use CNAM if I already have SHAKEN/STIR?**

Yes, they perform different functions. SHAKEN/STIR authenticates caller information, while CNAM provides caller-name identification.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Branded Calling: Improve Your Phone Number Reputation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008284-branded-calling-improve-your-phone-number-reputation?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [What is SHAKEN/STIR?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006429-what-is-shaken-stir-?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Improve Your Phone Number's Reputation with Voice Integrity](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005566-improve-your-phone-number-s-reputation-with-voice-integrity?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Why Are My Calls Marked as Spam, and How Can I Avoid It?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001231665?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Remediate “Spam Likely” on Your Caller ID Using Free Caller Registry](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005891-remediate-spam-likely-on-your-caller-id-using-free-caller-registry?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Why Doesn't My Business Name Display After CNAM Registration?](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006099-why-doesn-t-my-business-name-display-after-cnam-registration-?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

title_en: Domain Redemption Period: Why a Redemption Fee Is Required and How Recovery Works
source_md:
When a domain expires, there is often still a limited window where it can be recovered before it is released permanently. This recovery stage is called the redemption period, and it usually includes an additional redemption fee on top of the standard renewal cost. Understanding why this fee exists, who sets it, and how the recovery process works can help you act quickly and avoid losing your domain.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Domain Redemption Period?](#What-is-Domain-Redemption-Period?)
- [Key Benefits of Understanding Domain Redemption](#Key-Benefits-of-Understanding-Domain-Redemption)
- [Why a Redemption Fee Is Required](#Why-a-Redemption-Fee-Is-Required)
- [Typical Redemption Fee Range](#Typical-Redemption-Fee-Range)
- [Who Sets the Redemption Fee?](#Who-Sets-the-Redemption-Fee?)
- [How To Recover a Domain During the Redemption Period](#How-To-Recover-a-Domain-During-the-Redemption-Period)
- [What Happens If the Domain Is Not Recovered in Time?](#What-Happens-If-the-Domain-Is-Not-Recovered-in-Time?)
- [How To Avoid Redemption Fees in the Future](#How-To-Avoid-Redemption-Fees-in-the-Future)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Domain Redemption Period?**

The domain redemption period is a time-sensitive recovery stage that can happen after a domain expires. It gives you a final opportunity to restore ownership before the domain is deleted and may become available for someone else to register.

When a domain is not renewed on time, it does not always become publicly available right away. In many cases, the domain first enters a redemption period, which is a temporary status that allows the previous owner to request recovery.

Here is what that means in simple terms:

- The domain has already expired
- The standard renewal window has passed
- The domain may still be recoverable, but not through a normal renewal alone
- An additional redemption fee is usually required to restore it
- Recovery must happen quickly because the redemption window is limited

The redemption period exists to give domain owners one last chance to recover an expired domain before it is removed completely.

---

## **Key Benefits of Understanding Domain Redemption**

Knowing how domain redemption works helps you make faster decisions, avoid surprises, and set the right expectations if your domain has already expired.

- **Faster Action:** Understanding the redemption period helps you move quickly before the domain becomes unrecoverable.
- **Clear Cost Expectations:**Knowing that a redemption fee may apply reduces confusion when recovery costs are higher than a normal renewal.
- **Better Planning:**Understanding the domain lifecycle helps prevent accidental loss of important business domains.
- **More Confidence:** Knowing that the redemption fee is set by the registry or registrar helps explain why the charge cannot usually be waived.
- **Reduced Downtime Risk:** Prompt recovery can help minimize disruption to your website, email, and connected services.

---

## **Why a Redemption Fee Is Required**

A redemption fee is charged because recovering a domain during this stage is different from completing a normal renewal. The domain has already moved into a special recovery status, and restoring it usually involves additional processing through the registrar and registry.

A redemption fee is not the same as a standard domain renewal fee. Once a domain enters the redemption period, it typically requires extra steps to restore it to an active state.

**Important Points to Understand**

- The fee is generally charged because the domain has moved beyond the regular renewal stage
- Recovery often requires additional actions between the domain registrar and the domain registry
- This is an industry-standard type of charge for expired domains in redemption
- The fee is not arbitrarily created by HighLevel
- In most cases, the fee cannot simply be removed because it is tied to the recovery process itself

This is why recovering a domain during redemption costs more than renewing it before expiration.

---

## **Typical Redemption Fee Range**

Redemption fees can vary depending on the registrar, registry, and domain extension. That is why the total cost is usually higher than a normal yearly renewal and may not be identical for every domain.

Customers often ask why the fee seems high. The most important thing to know is that redemption fees are usually based on third-party domain infrastructure costs, not an optional service charge created by HighLevel.

**Typical Expectations:**

- Some registrars, such as Cloudflare, may show redemption-related costs in the range of about $44 to $50
- HighLevel’s standard recovery fee is typically around $55.50
- Final pricing may vary depending on the specific domain and recovery requirements
- The redemption fee is usually separate from the normal renewal cost, if renewal is also required as part of recovery

```
Use this as a general expectation-setting range, not a universal fixed price for every domain.
```

---

## **Who Sets the Redemption Fee?**

Understanding who controls the redemption fee helps explain why it is not something HighLevel can simply waive on request. These charges are usually tied to domain providers and the infrastructure used to restore expired domains.

The redemption fee is generally set by the domain registry and/or registrar, not by HighLevel as an arbitrary platform charge.

Here is the simplest way to think about it:

- **Registry:** The organization responsible for managing a domain extension, such as .com or .net
- **Registrar:**The provider that manages domain registration services and submits domain actions
- **HighLevel:**The platform helping facilitate domain-related workflows for customers using supported domain services

Because the recovery cost is tied to the domain ecosystem itself, HighLevel typically cannot treat it like a discretionary fee that support can remove on request.

---

## **How To Recover a Domain During the Redemption Period**

Recovering a domain during redemption is a time-sensitive process. Acting quickly improves the chances of successful recovery before the domain moves closer to permanent deletion.

Follow these steps to recover a domain that is in the redemption period:

1. Check the domain’s current status through your HighLevel workflow or with the support team handling the request.
2. Contact the appropriate support channel or follow the HighLevel recovery process to request restoration of the expired domain.
3. Confirm the applicable redemption fee and any renewal charges that may also be required as part of the restoration.
4. Once the required charges are approved, the recovery request can be processed through the registrar and registry workflow.
5. Recovery is not always instant. The request must be processed through the applicable domain provider systems.
6. After recovery is completed, confirm that the domain has returned to an active status and that any connected services are working properly.
7. Check your website, funnels, email, DNS records, and related settings to make sure everything is functioning as expected after the domain is restored.

---

## **What Happens If the Domain Is Not Recovered in Time?**

The redemption period is meant to be a final recovery window, not an open-ended holding period. Missing this deadline can lead to permanent loss of the domain and possible disruption to your business presence online.

If a domain is not recovered during the redemption period:

- The domain may move closer to deletion
- It may eventually become available for public registration again
- The original owner may lose the ability to recover it
- Your website, email, and other connected services may remain unavailable or become more difficult to restore

This is why it is important to act as soon as you learn that a domain is in redemption.

---

## **How To Avoid Redemption Fees in the Future**

Preventing expiration is the best way to avoid the added cost and urgency of domain recovery. A small amount of planning can help protect your domain and reduce the risk of downtime.

**Best Practices Include:**

- Renew domains before the expiration date
- Monitor billing methods to avoid failed renewal payments
- Keep account and contact information up to date
- Consider multi-year registration for important business domains
- Review renewal reminders promptly instead of waiting until the last minute

For important domains connected to active websites, funnels, and email accounts, proactive renewal management is strongly recommended.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is the domain redemption period?**A: It is a limited recovery window after a domain has expired and passed the normal renewal stage, but before it is deleted permanently.

**Q: Why is the redemption fee higher than a normal renewal fee?**A: Because the domain is no longer in a normal renewal state. Restoring it usually requires additional recovery processing through the registrar and registry.

**Q: Is the redemption fee created by HighLevel?**A: No. The fee is generally tied to the registrar and/or registry recovery process and is not an arbitrary fee created by HighLevel.

**Q: Can the redemption fee be waived?**A: In most cases, no. Since the fee is usually tied to third-party domain recovery costs, it typically cannot be waived like a normal discretionary charge.
