### **Step 5: Configure DNS Records and Verify**

1. Copy the DNS records displayed during domain setup.
2. Open your domain's DNS provider.
3. Add the required DNS records as displayed.
4. Return to HighLevel.
5. Complete the domain verification process.

DNS changes may take time to propagate. If verification is unsuccessful, check that the DNS records match the required values.

### **Step 6: Confirm the Domain Configuration**

Return to the Notification Section and review the brand's notification domain.

Confirm that:

- The correct notification domain is associated with the brand.
- The domain verification status indicates successful verification.

**You're All Set!**

Once the domain is configured and verified, system-generated notification emails for that brand use its notification domain.

Repeat these steps for any other brand that needs its own sender identity.

---

## **Understanding the Notification Section**

The **Notification Section** provides a centralized location for managing notification email domains across your SaaS brands.

You can:

- View notification domains configured for each brand.
- Check domain verification status.
- Identify brands that don't have a notification domain.
- Verify notification domains independently.
- Update an existing brand's notification domain.
- Remove a brand's notification domain.

---

### **How Domain Configuration Affects Each Brand**

| Configuration | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Brand has a configured notification domain | System-generated notification emails use that brand's domain. |
| Brand has no configured notification domain | Notification emails use the default brand's notification domain. |
| Brand's notification domain needs verification | Review its verification status and complete the required configuration. |

### **Manage Notification Domains Independently**

Each brand's notification domain configuration is managed independently.

You can verify, update, or remove a notification domain for one brand without changing another brand's configuration.

**Tip:** To maintain a separate notification email sender identity for every brand, configure and verify a notification domain for each one.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q. How many brands can have their own notification email domain?**

SaaS Multi-Brand Management supports up to two brands. Each brand can have its own notification email domain.

**Q. What happens if a brand doesn't have a notification email domain?**

System-generated notification emails for that brand use the default brand's notification domain.

To maintain a separate sender identity, configure a notification domain for the brand.

**Q. Can I configure a different domain for each brand?**

Yes. Each brand supports an independent notification email domain configuration, allowing you to use a separate domain or subdomain for each brand.

**Q. Can I use a subdomain for notification emails?**

Yes. You can configure a domain or subdomain for a brand, such as notify.brandname.com.

**Q. Where do I configure notification email domains?**

Navigate to Agency Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain and IP → Notification Section.

**Q. Can I update or remove an existing notification domain?**

Yes. You can update or remove notification domains independently for each brand.

**Q. How can I check whether a notification domain is verified?**

Open the Notification Section under Dedicated Domain and IP to view the domain verification status for each brand.

**Q. What should I do if my domain isn't verifying?**

Confirm that the required DNS records have been added to your DNS provider and that their values match the records provided during setup.

Allow time for DNS propagation, then check the domain verification status again.

**Q. Will changing one brand's notification domain affect another brand?**

No. Notification domain configurations are managed independently for each brand.

**Q. Do I need to configure a notification domain for every brand?**

You don't need to configure a separate domain for every brand. However, brands without their own notification domains use the default brand's notification domain.

For distinct sender identities, configure a notification domain for each brand.

title_en: How to create a LinkedIn ad campaign in Ad Manager
source_md:
Ad Manager organizes LinkedIn advertising into a **three-level hierarchy**:

- **Campaign Group** : The top-level container.
- **Campaign** : Defines budget, audience, and scheduling.
- **Ad** : Defines creatives (media, text, CTA, forms).

```
Note: HighLevel currently organizes LinkedIn ads using Campaign Group > Campaign > Ad. In LinkedIn Campaign Manager, LinkedIn has updated this terminology so a Campaign Group may appear as a Campaign, while a Campaign may appear as an Ad Set. The underlying hierarchy remains comparable even though the terminology differs.
```

This guide walks you through **creating a Campaign Group** and then building campaigns and ads inside it.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Step 1: Create a Campaign Group](#Step-1%3A-Create-a-Campaign-Group)
  - [Budget & Schedule](#Budget-&-Schedule)
  - [Bidding](#Bidding)
- [Step 2: Create a Campaign Inside the Group](#Step-2%3A-Create-a-Campaign-Inside-the-Group)
  - [Fields Defined at Campaign Level](#Fields-Defined-at-Campaign-Level)
  - [Audience Targeting(learn more: here)](#Audience-Targeting(learn-more%3A-here))
- [Step 3: Create Ads Inside the Campaign](#Step-3%3A-Create-Ads-Inside-the-Campaign)
  - [Fields Defined at Ad Level](#Fields-Defined-at-Ad-Level)
  - [Creative Fields](#Creative-Fields)
  - [Lead Gen Forms (if Objective = Lead Generation)](#Lead-Gen-Forms-(if-Objective-=-Lead-Generation))
- [Step 4: Review & Publish](#Step-4%3A-Review-&-Publish)
- [Step 5: Viewing Campaign Group Performance](#Step-5%3A-Viewing-Campaign-Group-Performance)
- [Best Practices](#Best-Practices)

## --- ``` IMPORTANT: Use a campaign template: LinkedIn campaigns can also be created from an Ad Manager template. Select Ad Manager Templates, choose a LinkedIn template, review its details, and click Continue. Supported campaign configurations are pre-filled from the selected template. ```

## **Step 1: Create a Campaign Group**

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813131/original/uRfzv4cSE3Z5FmBhbyxg_HMV_vH1te9ApQ.png?1759145783)**

A **Campaign Group** is the top-level container for your LinkedIn campaigns.

- **Campaign Group Name:** Choose a descriptive name (e.g., “Q4 SaaS Leads”).
- **Objective Selection:** Select between:

  - **Lead Generation** - capture leads with LinkedIn forms
  - **Website Traffic** - Drive users to an external website or landing page. This corresponds to LinkedIn's **Website Visits** objective.
- ### **Budget & Schedule**

  - Define the daily or lifetime budget for the campaign group.
  - **Schedule** : Set start and end dates for the campaign group.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813145/original/Qgl8GjQ1tt1w3kx_OPJLJZVUgmylJOzwUw.png?1759145800)**

- ### **Bidding**

  - Manual bid input for Cost Per Lead (Lead Gen) or CPC (Traffic).

**Tip**: Campaign Groups help you organize campaigns by business goals.

---

## **Step 2: Create a Campaign Inside the Group**

Once your group is created, you can add **Campaigns**.

### **Fields Defined at Campaign Level**

- **Campaign Name** : This will have a unique identifier.
- **Media Type** : Single image, video or carousel type of media.
- **Language**
- **Geographic location**and
- Optional: **Intended Audience**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813264/original/NTT-StjHux21FptKzUJLqkBC1Yub-zZ1ew.png?1759145841)

---

### **Audience Targeting**(learn more: [here](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006454-audience-targeting-for-linkedin-campaigns-in-ad-manager))

- **Mandatory**: Location (include/exclude).
- **Optional Filters**: Job Title, Industry, Company Size, Seniority, Skills, Education, Interests & Traits.
- **Logic Builder**:

  - Add up to **3 attribute groups**.
  - **OR logic** inside groups.
  - **AND logic** between groups.
  - Include and Exclude supported.

Example:

- Group 1 - Job Title = Marketing Manager **OR** Director
- Group 2 - Industry = Healthcare
- Exclude - Interns

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813301/original/WK-tnfdbNLY4LWiXpQQpGcbPOCRy0IowUQ.png?1759145860)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813310/original/-N51skvsrRuahcBy4coM0l-tHez-dei8Ow.png?1759145871)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813351/original/0MJRgKTWJ57YK3Bymy4P8HdrS-xXgKhZig.png?1759145884)

---

## **Step 3: Create Ads Inside the Campaign**

Each campaign can contain multiple ads.

### **Fields Defined at Ad Level**

- **Ad Name** : Internal identifier.
- **Media Type** (chosen at campaign level):

  - **Single Image Ad** - Upload one image.  
    ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813485/original/QmnWmEx8Gg3X-75XN-cSNX1-ZYGpLJu4IA.png?1759145930)
  - **Single Video Ad** - Upload a video.
  - **Carousel Ad** - Display multiple image cards in a swipeable carousel.

    Each card can include:

    - Image
    - Headline
    - Destination URL
  - LinkedIn carousel ads support between **2 and 10 image cards**. Videos are not supported within carousel cards.

    - ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813548/original/7J6OptbpOQCPgW5F8CcwMEIHIbe0dIaUgw.png?1759145952)

---

### **Creative Fields**

- **Introduction Text** – Up to 3,000 characters. Keep the primary message concise because longer text may be truncated depending on placement.
- **Headline** – Keep headlines concise; LinkedIn recommends approximately 70 characters to minimize truncation.
- **Description** – Up to 300 characters. Shorter descriptions may display more consistently across placements.
- **Call-to-Action** : Choose from LinkedIn CTA list (Learn More, Download, Apply, etc.).
- **Destination URL** : Required for all ads. HighLevel auto-prepends `https://` if missing.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813647/original/SZnwjnD_pYo5omDVodCyLQYqfPVa_Y0bwA.png?1759146022)

---

### **Lead Gen Forms (if Objective = Lead Generation)**

- **Form Name** : Auto-generated, editable.
- **Headline & Description** : Shown prominently in the form.
- **Pre-filled Fields** : Up to 12 (Name, Email, Job Title, etc.).
- **Custom Questions** : Up to 3 (short answer or multiple choice).
- **Hidden Fields** : Up to 20 (UTM tags, campaign IDs).
- **Privacy Section** : Mandatory privacy URL + optional disclosure text.
- **Consent Checkboxes** : Up to 5.
- **Confirmation Page** : Thank-you message + optional CTA (Visit Website, Download, Call).
- Learn more about **LinkedIn lead forms and how to create it**: [here](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006453-how-to-create-a-linkedin-lead-form-in-ad-manager)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813821/original/sKpAqAyVXAxfQn76GFg9WVJCC3XwD_XCQA.png?1759146093)

---

## **Step 4: Review & Publish**

Before launching, you’ll land on the **Review & Publish screen**:

- Campaign objective, budget, schedule and optimization mode.
- Full creative preview (desktop & mobile).
- Validation: ensures URLs are valid, budgets meet LinkedIn’s minimums, and required fields are filled.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813627/original/VwKBvycIXafWlrvoIOSqHDhxqgVvYLDQcQ.png?1759146007)

---

## **Step 5: Viewing Campaign Group Performance**

After publishing, performance can be tracked in **Statistics > LinkedIn**. Learn more about LinkedIn statistics in detail in this help document: [LinkedIn ad statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006455-understanding-linkedin-statistics-in-ad-manager)

- **Campaign Group Level** : Spend, Impressions, Clicks, CTR.
- **Campaign Level** : Conversions, audience effectiveness, CPL.
- **Ad Level** : Creative performance (CTR, CPC, CPL, Conversions).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813836/original/ZY_GHPa2WnAzjkPO4jX55zI49UNHjrHi3w.png?1759146111)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813860/original/l_72_qSJegeIBxB1w4jjXemcimodFFO7BA.png?1759146121)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155054813868/original/D6jRE_7VwgXguFsaBbvIGCWPEvMev9_3eg.png?1759146128)

---

## **Best Practices**

- Organize by **business objective** (e.g., Awareness, Lead Gen).
- Keep Campaigns focused (1 audience definition each).
- Run **multiple ads per campaign** to compare creatives.
- Start broad and then refine with filters.
- Lead Gen : shorter forms convert better.
- Traffic: always enable UTM tagging for analytics.

title_en: GoKollab Affiliate Program for Communities
source_md:
Turn your most passionate members into a growth engine with Community Affiliates in GoKollab. This article explains how the program works, who’s eligible, and how both owners and members access their affiliate tools. You’ll learn where to set the commission %, how tracking appears in dashboards, and how owners manage payouts directly (not by Kollab).

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Community Affiliates?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Community-Affiliates?)
- [Key Benefits of Community Affiliates](#Key-Benefits-of-Community-Affiliates)
- [Member Referral Commissions](#Member-Referral-Commissions)
- [Auto‑Generated Referral Links](#Auto%E2%80%91Generated-Referral-Links)
- [Commission Settings & Payout Ownership](#Commission-Settings-&-Payout-Ownership)
- [Access for Community Owners](#Access-for-Community-Owners)
- [Access for Referrers (Community Members)](#Access-for-Referrers-(Community-Members))
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Community Affiliates?**

Community Affiliates enables an internal referral program for GoKollab communities. When activated, paid members receive personal invite links. When an invitee joins and pays for membership, the referrer earns a commission based on the percentage set by the community owner. This aligns incentives so growth comes from authentic member advocacy.

Community Affiliates is available exclusively on GoKollab and is designed to keep setup simple while giving owners clear control over commissions and payouts.

---

## **Key Benefits of Community Affiliates**

Knowing the core advantages helps you position the program to your team and members, ensuring everyone understands how referrals convert into revenue and rewards.

- **Word‑of‑mouth growth:** Recommendations from trusted members lead to higher‑quality sign‑ups.
- **Lower acquisition costs:** Shift spend from ads to performance‑based commissions you control.
- **Member loyalty:** Reward engaged advocates for contributing to community growth.
- **Owner control:** Set the commission %, monitor results, and manage payouts yourself.
- **Clear attribution:** Personal invite links attribute paid joins to the correct referrer.

---

## **Member Referral Commissions**

Clear rules around when commissions are created reduce disputes and make the program easier to administer.

- Commissions are credited when a new member uses a referrer’s invite link **and completes a paid membership**.
- The **commission %** is defined by the community owner and applies to eligible referrals.
- Earnings accumulate and are paid when the owner processes payouts.

---

## **Auto‑Generated Referral Links**

Easy‑to‑use invite links encourage participation. Make sure members know where to find their link and how referrals are tracked.

- Each **paid** member can access a unique invite link for your community.
- Members can copy and share their link across social channels, email, or direct messages.
- Announce the program with a pinned post and onboarding email to drive early momentum.

---

## **Commission Settings & Payout Ownership**

Owners define the incentive structure and retain full control of payout timing and method, ensuring flexibility for different business processes.

- **Commission %:** Owners set the global commission percentage for referrals that convert to paid memberships.
- **Payouts owned by you:** Payouts are **managed directly by community owners, not by Kollab**. Choose how and when to pay (e.g., bank transfer) based on your internal processes.
- **Status updates:** Owners manually mark payouts as **Completed** or **Failed** so referrers see accurate status in their dashboards.

---

## **Access for Community Owners**

Use these steps to locate affiliate controls, set your commission %, and monitor referral performance so you can process payouts confidently.

**How to Set Commission %**

1. Go to **Kollab Studio**.
2. Click the **kebab menu (three dots)** next to your community.
3. Select **Affiliates**.
4. In the top right, set your **Commission %** (the reward given per referral) and save.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056054086/original/W8zf1uzK3cgEyEgIlmFTlHisLvg4bPQaeg.png?1760532214)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056054217/original/kTwXykd9KepgNUewf858N_gJJDGyIVG1Hg.png?1760532237)

**Understanding the Dashboard (Owners)**

- **Revenue from affiliates:** Additional membership revenue generated from referrals.
- **Total payouts:** Total commissions you’ve already paid to affiliates.

**Referral Table Fields**

- **Invitee name:** The new member invited.
- **Referred by:** The existing community member who sent the invite.
- **Joining status:** Shows **Invited** until the invitee pays; updates to **Joined** after payment.
- **Total Payouts:** Amount you’ve paid so far for that referral.
- **Pending Payouts:** Amount left to be paid for that referral.

**Payout Status:**

- **Completed** → You’ve marked the payout as paid.
- **Pending** → Not yet paid / Payment is processing.
- **Failed** → Transfer didn’t go through (e.g., incorrect bank details).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056056137/original/4EkiYAtHeh9QnBsK0pYcKurd_HZ87DS_ow.png?1760533121)

**Actions**

- Manually update payout statuses by clicking **tick (Completed)** or **cross (Failed)**. The referrer’s dashboard updates accordingly.

**Getting Bank Details of Members**

- At the top right of the referrals table, click **Download CSV** to retrieve the bank details needed to process payouts.

---

## **Access for Referrers (Community Members)**

Members can view their referral performance and payout status so they always know what they’ve earned and what’s pending.

**Accessing Your Affiliate Dashboard**

1. Click your **Profile Icon** in the top‑right corner to open the account menu.
2. Click **Affiliates**.
3. You’ll only see communities that offer affiliate commissions.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056059503/original/anzEYz5n41wbm_mle2DtMygRiZMalokz2A.png?1760534679)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056054680/original/3zNV9jTX7mZE55DwW2BxEvQHNd0-FoJf7g.png?1760532402)  
  

**Your Dashboard Shows**

- **Account Balance:** Money you are yet to receive.
- **Earnings:** Total money already received.

```
Important: Enter your bank details before you start referring so you can get paid.
```

**Referral Table Fields (Members)**

- **Invitee name:** The member you invited.
- **Joined Status:** **Invited** if not purchased; **Joined** if paid.
- **Earnings:** Total commission earned from that referral.
- **Pending Payouts:** Commission not yet paid by the community owner.

**Payout Status:**

- **Completed** → You’ve been paid.
- **Pending** → Payment not yet processed.
- **Failed** → Payment didn’t go through (contact your community owner for clarity).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155056056613/original/SMzi3nhfRmxgfe78TKQPU1T4CGrS2O9xiQ.png?1760533347)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q. Who can get an invite link?**  
Paid members in the community receive personal invite links.

**Q. When is a commission created?**  
When an invitee joins via a member’s link and completes a **paid** membership.

**Q. Where do I set or change the commission %?**  
Owners: **Kollab Studio → kebab menu (three dots) → Affiliates → Commission %** (top right).

**Q. Who handles payouts?**  
Payouts are handled directly by **community owners**, not by Kollab.

**Q. How do owners update payout status?**  
In the referrals table, click the **tick** to mark **Completed** or the **cross** to mark **Failed**.

**Q. Can referrers see payout status updates?**  
Yes. Referrers see **Completed**, **Pending**, or **Failed** in their Affiliate dashboard.

**Q. How do owners get member bank details for payouts?**  
Click **Download CSV** at the top right of the referrals table.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Manage Your Communities and Courses with GoKollab Studio](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005899-manage-your-communities-and-courses-with-gokollab-studio)
- [How to Setup, Customize, and Manage Your Communities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000280-how-to-setup-customize-and-manage-your-communities)
- [GoKollab for Communities (Overview/Marketplace)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005900-gokollab-for-communities-overview)
- [Kollab Mobile Apps – Getting Started](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005901-kollab-mobile-apps-getting-started)

title_en: Device Width Preview in Funnel & Website Builder
source_md:
Device Width Preview gives you more control when reviewing responsive Funnel and Website pages inside the HighLevel builder. Enter an exact pixel width to see how your page looks at different screen sizes while staying within the selected desktop, tablet, or mobile breakpoint. The preview changes only the builder canvas and does not alter saved styles or the published page.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is Device Width Preview?](#What-Is-Device-Width-Preview?)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](#Prerequisites-and-Limitations)
- [Supported Device Width Ranges](#Supported-Device-Width-Ranges)
- [How to Use Device Width Preview](#How-to-Use-Device-Width-Preview)
- [Adjust Row & Column Widths in Desktop & Tablet Views](#Adjust-Row-&-Column-Widths-in-Desktop-&-Tablet-Views)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is Device Width Preview?**

Device Width Preview lets you enter an exact pixel width for the Funnel and Website Builder canvas.

Instead of reviewing your design at only one predefined canvas width, you can test different widths within the selected desktop, tablet, or mobile breakpoint.

The custom width changes only the canvas preview. Your selected device mode still determines which responsive styles you edit and save.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Device Width Preview is designed for responsive testing inside the builder. Understanding how it interacts with device modes helps prevent preview changes from being confused with responsive styling changes.

**Keep the following behaviors in mind:**

- Device Width Preview changes only the builder canvas preview.
- It does not create a new responsive breakpoint.
- The selected **Desktop**, **Tablet**, or **Mobile** mode determines which responsive styles are edited and saved.
- Custom preview widths apply only to the current builder session.
- Custom widths reset when you reload the builder or navigate to another page.
- Preview widths are not saved in page data.
- Preview widths do not change the published page.
- Preview widths do not generate or apply separate responsive styles.
- The width you enter must fall within the supported range for the selected device mode.

---

## **Supported Device Width Ranges**

Each device mode supports a defined range of preview widths. Select the appropriate device mode before entering a custom width.

| **Device Mode** | **Supported Width** |
| --- | --- |
| **Desktop** | 1025–3000 px |
| **Tablet** | 768–1024 px |
| **Mobile** | 320–767 px |

Entering a width outside the selected device mode's range displays inline validation feedback.

---

## **How to **Preview**Device Width**

Device Width Preview is available directly in the Funnel and Website Builder. Open the page you want to review, select the appropriate responsive mode, and enter the screen width you want to preview.

### **Step 1:**Open a Funnel or Website Page

1. From the **Sub-Account View**, select **Sites** in the left menu.
2. Select **Funnels** or **Websites**.
3. Open the Funnel or Website you want to edit.
4. Open the applicable step or page in the builder.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082802738/original/9ULOfP7ARHFztTMwon_KNmUrjWbEUbQP5A.png?1791435528)

### **Step 2:** Select a Device Mode

Choose the responsive breakpoint you want to review:

- **Desktop**
- **Tablet**
- **Mobile**

The selected device mode determines which responsive styles are active while you edit the page.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082802006/original/DnH8RQ2SR9krvXax36WGeudWLp3Sqz7Ubg.png?1791433954)

### **Step 3:** Enter a Custom Device Width

Locate the **Device Width** control beside the device switcher.

Enter a pixel width that falls within the supported range for the selected device mode.

For example, when **Tablet** is selected, enter a value between **768 px and 1024 px**.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082802136/original/jME6E4QR6ZRxDjz7dogmS5sPifkaRKHDiQ.png?1791434257)

### **Step 4:**Apply the Preview Width

Apply the entered width by either:

- Clicking **Apply**
- Pressing **Enter**

The builder canvas updates to the requested width while remaining within the selected responsive breakpoint.

### **Step 5:** Review the Page Layout

Review how your sections, rows, columns, elements, spacing, and content appear at the selected width.

If the canvas becomes wider than the available builder workspace, scroll horizontally to review the full layout.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082802548/original/4zz2T3KoFpBw4Xkgehsub1H8Fxv6X5yJnA.png?1791435089)

### **Step 6:**Test Additional Widths

Enter additional supported widths to test how the layout responds across the selected breakpoint.

If you need to test another breakpoint, switch to **Desktop**, **Tablet**, or **Mobile**, then enter a width supported by that mode.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082802466/original/cD6JieDvfPi_1RiDD0Vs-OTD8Dk_PK0Ngw.png?1791434930)

### **Step 7:**Reset the Preview

Use the reset option to return the canvas to the default preview width for the active device mode.

Resetting the preview width does not change the responsive styles you have already edited or saved.

---

## **Adjust Row & Column Widths in Desktop & Tablet Views**

The Funnel and Website Builder allows you to customize row and column widths separately for Desktop and Tablet views. By default, Tablet inherits Desktop widths until you customize them.

### **How to Adjust Row and Column Widths**

1. Open a funnel or website page in the builder.
2. Use the device switcher to select **Desktop** or **Tablet** view.
3. Select a row and adjust its width using the **Width** setting.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083128675/original/IEHJxYbUzEszKjpRUVxYicCoiBRTIwbAZw.gif?1791820022)
4. To resize adjacent columns in **Tablet** view, drag the handle between the columns to adjust their widths.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083128695/original/n_f1ZC0LS6mxcbypeIDubGGnnCVTMswJjA.gif?1791820042)
5. Switch between **Desktop** and **Tablet** views to review your layouts, then save your changes.

```
Note: Changes made to Tablet widths do not affect the Desktop layout. Tablet-specific widths are retained after saving and reloading the builder.
```

**Important Notes:**

- **Width inheritance:** Tablet inherits Desktop row and column widths until customized.
- **Reset Tablet row width:** Set the Tablet row width to match the Desktop value to remove the override and restore inheritance.
- **Mobile view:** Rows remain full width, the row-width control stays hidden, and columns stack vertically.
- **Existing pages:** Pages without Tablet-specific widths remain unchanged. No migration is required.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does entering a custom Device Width create a new breakpoint?**

No. Device Width changes only the canvas preview. Desktop, tablet, and mobile remain the responsive breakpoints used for editing and saving styles.

**Q: Does the custom preview width affect my published page?**

No. Preview widths are not saved in page data and do not affect the published page or its generated styles.

**Q: Will my custom Device Width be saved for the next time I open the builder?**

No. Custom preview widths are session-only and reset after reloading the builder or navigating to another page.

**Q: What happens if I enter a width outside the selected breakpoint's range?**

The builder displays inline validation feedback. Enter a width within the supported range for the selected device mode.

**Q: Can I preview a width that is larger than my available builder workspace?**

Yes. When the canvas exceeds the available workspace, you can scroll horizontally to review the full preview.

**Q: Does changing the Device Width change which responsive styles I am editing?**

No. The selected desktop, tablet, or mobile mode determines which responsive styles are edited and saved.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Creating Mobile-Responsive Designs Made Easy: Funnel & Website Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000001482)
- [Create Pages in the HighLevel Page Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000008367)
- [Websites Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000001633)
- [Using the New Revamped Sidebar in Funnel & Website Builders](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005422)

title_en: WhatsApp FAQs
source_md:
# WhatsApp Frequently Asked Questions

Answers to common questions about subscriptions, migrations, frequency capping, business verification, and conversation charges.

Table of Contents

[Subscriptions & Account Status](#subscriptions) [Number Migration & Coexistence](#migration) [Frequency Capping (India)](#frequency-capping) [Business Verification](#verification) [Deliverability Best Practices](#deliverability) [Conversation Charges](#billing) [Onboarding Errors](#onboarding-errors)

---

Subscriptions & Account Status

Q: Failed to send a message because this user's phone number is part of an experiment

Starting June 14, 2023, roughly 1% of WhatsApp users will not receive marketing template messages from any business unless one of the following conditions is met:

- A customer service window exists between the customer and the business.
- An open marketing conversation exists between the customer and the business.
- An open free-entry point conversation exists between the customer and the business.

If you send a marketing template message to a customer who is part of the experiment group, your message will not be sent and you will not be billed for it since no conversation was created.

Q: Will unsubscribing from WhatsApp affect my phone numbers and templates?

No, unsubscribing from WhatsApp will not impact your WhatsApp phone numbers or templates. When you resubscribe, all your numbers and templates will be restored as they were before unsubscribing.

Q: What happens to my WhatsApp numbers and templates if I switch between "Location Purchase" and "Agency Direct Deploy"?

Switching between "Location Purchase" and "Agency Direct Deploy" will not affect your WhatsApp phone numbers or templates. Once you resubscribe, everything will appear as it was before the change.

Q: Can I send or receive messages while my WhatsApp subscription is inactive?

No, messages cannot be sent or received while the WhatsApp subscription is inactive. However, all data, including phone numbers and templates, will remain intact and will be restored upon resubscription.

Q: What should I do if I face issues after resubscribing to WhatsApp?

If your phone numbers or templates do not appear after resubscribing, please reach out to our support team for assistance.

Q: Will my workflows and automations linked to WhatsApp templates be preserved during the unsubscribed period?

Yes, all workflows and automations linked to your WhatsApp templates will remain intact. Once you resubscribe, these workflows will function as before.

```
Note: Ensure you resubscribe promptly to avoid disruptions in your messaging workflows.
```

---

Number Migration & Coexistence

Q: What steps do I need to take to use my existing WhatsApp number?

To use your existing number, you need to delete the existing WhatsApp account associated with that number. Follow these steps:

1. Open WhatsApp.
2. Go to Settings > Account > Delete my account. For more information, refer to the guide on how to [migrate an existing WhatsApp number to a Business Account](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/get-started/migrate-existing-whatsapp-number-to-a-business-account/).

Q: Can I use my number on both the WhatsApp Business Platform and WhatsApp Business App simultaneously?

Yes, using the WhatsApp Coexistence feature. Coexistence allows businesses to use their existing WhatsApp Business App account alongside the CRM's advanced tools powered by the WhatsApp Cloud API. [Read more about Coexistence here](#).

Q: Will I lose my data after migrating my WhatsApp number to the WhatsApp Business Platform?

Yes, you will lose all data associated with WhatsApp after migration. Meta does not allow data transfers between platforms. It is highly recommended to take a backup of your data before proceeding with the migration.

Q: How do I backup my data before migrating my WhatsApp number?

To backup your data:

1. Open WhatsApp.
2. Go to Settings > Chats > Chat backup.
3. Follow the prompts to back up your data to your preferred location (e.g., Google Drive or iCloud).

---

Frequency Capping (India)

Q: What is Meta's new update for the WhatsApp Business Platform (API)?

Meta has introduced Frequency Capping to limit the number of marketing messages sent to WhatsApp users with Indian phone numbers. This restricts the number of marketing messages a person can receive from any business in a given period. Meta introduced frequency capping to reduce spamming and over-sending of messages, improving the overall user experience and giving businesses a better opportunity to engage with customers effectively.

Q: How does this impact your deliverability?

Frequency capping works on a first-come, first-served basis. Marketing messages will be delivered until the limit is reached. Any messages beyond this limit will not be delivered.

Q: What kind of messages are exempt from Frequency Capping?

Frequency capping only applies to promotional and marketing template messages that require opening a new conversation. It does not apply to:

- **Session Messages:** Support messages within existing customer service interactions.
- **Click to WhatsApp Ads:** Conversations initiated by users clicking on WhatsApp ads.

Q: Does Frequency Capping affect all users?

No, Frequency Capping only applies to marketing messages sent to users in India (+91 country code).

What determines the capping for a WhatsApp Business Account with multiple phone numbers?

The restriction is based on the total number of messages received by individual users from any business. It is not determined by the number of messages received from one specific business.

---

Business Verification

Q: What are the benefits of verifying my Facebook Business Manager account?

Once Meta verifies your Facebook Business Manager account, you can initiate unlimited business conversations on WhatsApp.

Q: What can I do if my Facebook Business Manager account is not yet verified?

While your verification is pending, you can:

- Initiate up to 250 business conversations in a 24-hour rolling window.
- Respond to customer-initiated conversations without any restrictions.
- Have two WhatsApp business numbers in an unverified Facebook Business Manager account.

Q: What happens if my business verification is unsuccessful?

If your business verification is unsuccessful, you can continue using your WhatsApp business number with the restrictions mentioned above (i.e., 250 business conversations in a 24-hour period and responding to customer-initiated conversations without restrictions).

Q: How do I request verification for my Facebook Business Manager account?

To request verification, you need to provide proof of your legal entity and access to the business. Detailed instructions can be found in the guide on [Verifying Your Business in WhatsApp Business Manager](#).

---

Deliverability Best Practices

Q: What are the recommended best practices to improve deliverability?

✓**Opt-In Engagement:** Send messages only to customers who have explicitly opted in.

✓**Segment Your Contact List:** Group your audience based on common characteristics to send targeted messages.

✓**Personalize Recommendations:** Use customer behavior and purchase patterns to send personalized product recommendations.

✓**Emphasize Quality Over Quantity:** Ensure your messages add value and resonate with your customers' needs.

✓**Engage via Two-Way Conversations:** Create meaningful interactions to keep customers engaged and interested in your brand.

---

Conversation Charges

Q: WhatsApp is free to use for personal messaging. So, what do "WhatsApp conversation charges" refer to?

While the WhatsApp app and WhatsApp Business app are free, businesses using the WhatsApp Business API to communicate with customers at scale are subject to conversation charges.

These charges apply when a business sends notifications to customers via the WhatsApp Business platform, especially if the customer has not responded within the last 24 hours. The cost depends on the customer's country code. We bill these charges to you based on the actual cost, with no additional surcharge.

---

Onboarding Errors

Q: What does "Last onboarding failed! This WABA is already onboarded at this Location ID" mean?

This message indicates that the WABA (WhatsApp Business Account) you're trying to onboard is already connected to another Location ID, as shown in the error message or screenshot. If you'd like to onboard this WABA to a different Location ID, you'll first need to disconnect it from the current location. Once it's removed, you can proceed with onboarding it to the desired Location ID.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155045415633/original/skP_FQdW4Ni7-aBEvmTDOeCEU4GuXcxnrg.png?1745299749)

title_en: Communities - Analytics
source_md:
Community Analytics gives community admins and owners a centralized dashboard to track revenue, membership, traffic, and engagement. This article shows you how to access the dashboard, filter data by date range, and understand key performance metrics and activity trends. You'll also learn how to identify and export inactive members.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Community Analytics?](#What-is-Community-Analytics?)
- [Limitations and Important Considerations](#Limitations-and-Important-Considerations)
- [How To Access Community Analytics](#How-To-Access-Community-Analytics)
- [Understanding the Community Analytics Dashboard](#Understanding-the-Community-Analytics-Dashboard)
  - [Selecting a Date Range](#Selecting-a-Date-Range)
  - [Understanding Key Performance Metrics](#Understanding-Key-Performance-Metrics)
  - [Analyzing Traffic Sources](#Analyzing-Traffic-Sources)
  - [Identifying Peak Activity Hours](#Identifying-Peak-Activity-Hours)
  - [Tracking Community Engagement](#Tracking-Community-Engagement)
  - [Exporting Inactive Members](#Exporting-Inactive-Members)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Community Analytics?**

Community Analytics is a dedicated dashboard in HighLevel Communities that provides visibility into how your community is performing. It brings together earnings, membership activity, traffic sources, peak activity hours, and engagement metrics in one place.

Community admins and owners can compare performance across different date ranges, understand member participation, identify inactive members, and make informed decisions about growing and managing their communities.

---

## **Limitations and Important Considerations**

- **Historical traffic:** Visits recorded before traffic tracking became available are not backfilled.
- **Activity-based reporting:** Inactive members are determined by tracked activity within the selected date range.
- **Period comparisons:** Percentage changes depend on data from the previous equal-length reporting period.
- **Community timezone:** Time-based analytics use the community's timezone instead of UTC.

---

## **How To Access Community Analytics**

Community Analytics is accessible from your group's settings. Once you reach the dashboard, you can review performance metrics and choose the reporting period that best fits your needs.

1. Log in to your account.
2. Select **Memberships** from the left-hand navigation menu.
3. Select **Communities**.
4. Select **Groups**.
5. Locate the group you want to review and select **Login to your group**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/fECpHAPNywp43qKtgW6m+/Screenshot+2026-10-30+at+19.13.02.png)
6. Inside the community, select **Settings** from the top navigation menu.
7. From the settings sidebar, select **Analytics**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/yUyhFYty4e9BPvGwGQGV+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-30+at+19.23.48.png)

---

## **Understanding the Community Analytics Dashboard**

The dashboard organizes performance information into reporting cards, charts, and activity visualizations. Each area provides a different view of your community's earnings, membership, visitors, or engagement.

### **Selecting a Date Range**

Date filters help you review community performance over a specific period. The dashboard uses the selected range across its reporting cards, making it easier to compare metrics consistently.

The available date filters are:

- **Today**
- **Yesterday**
- **7 days**
- **30 days**
- **90 days**
- **12 months**
- **Custom**

By default, the dashboard displays the last **30 days**.

You can select another preset or use **Custom** to specify a reporting period.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/zFKoaAahI2uRvUBKdlPV+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-30+at+19.49.09.png)

---

## **Understanding Key Performance Metrics**

The performance cards provide a snapshot of your community's financial activity, membership, inactivity, and pending invitations.

#### **Total earnings**

Total earnings represents net transaction revenue attributed to your community.

The value includes purchases after subtracting refunds and chargebacks. Earnings are displayed in the sub-account or location currency.

#### **Total members**

Total members represents the current active membership roster of your community.

The dashboard also displays the number of new members who joined during the selected reporting period.

This helps distinguish the current membership total from membership growth during that period.

#### **Inactive members**

Inactive members are members of the current active membership roster who have no tracked analytics activity during the selected date range.

The dashboard displays the inactive-member count and a visual comparison of active versus inactive members.

The activity-based calculation is:

**Active members = Total members − Inactive members**

This activity classification helps identify members who may need additional engagement.

#### **Invitation pending**

Invitation pending shows email invitations that remain outstanding as of the end of the selected reporting period.

This metric helps community owners and admins monitor invitations that have not yet been cleared.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/FU9UvGCcrTxSnAJAxD7U+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-30+at+19.52.02.png)

---

## **Analyzing Traffic Sources**

Traffic analytics help you understand where community visits originate. You can review the traffic total, compare reporting periods, and examine the contribution of individual sources.

The dashboard supports the following traffic categories:

- **Direct**
- **Instagram**
- **YouTube**
- **Facebook**
- **LinkedIn**
- **Other**

The dashboard displays up to four named traffic sources based on their volume. Remaining sources are grouped under **Other**.

Each displayed source includes its contribution to traffic and a comparison with the previous reporting period.

Automated bots and crawlers are excluded from traffic capture.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Xae60Ib7BSmk1U5s0g7E+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-30+at+19.53.08.png)

---

## **Identifying Peak Activity Hours**

Peak activity hours help you understand when community members are most active. You can use these insights to plan announcements, discussions, and other activities around periods of higher participation.

The dashboard displays a heat map organized by day of the week and hour of the day.

- **Darker cells:** Indicate higher activity levels.
- **Lighter cells:** Indicate lower activity levels.
- **Busiest block:** Highlights the day and time with the highest recorded activity.
- **Timezone:** Activity is displayed using the community's timezone rather than UTC.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/VGMnEqlOHe4DPWbltzOV+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-30+at+19.54.48.png)

---

## **Tracking Community Engagement**

Engagement analytics show how members interact with content in your community. These metrics help you understand participation levels and monitor changes over time.

The **Engagement** card displays a breakdown of three interaction types:

- **Posts:** The number of posts created during the reporting period.
- **Comments:** The number of comments recorded during the reporting period.
- **Reactions:** The number of reactions recorded during the reporting period.

A chart displays the distribution of these interactions, including their share of the reported breakdown.

The **Engagement trend** chart shows how total interactions change throughout the selected period.

Together, these visualizations help identify participation patterns and changes in community engagement.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/em0kYg3OxCu8hD8VUWcQ+/Screenshot+2026-10-23+at+12.22.56%E2%80%AFPM.png)

---

## **Exporting Inactive Members**

Community Analytics allows admins and owners to download inactive-member data for the selected reporting period. This export can help teams identify members for re-engagement or maintain records of community activity.

To export inactive members:

1. Select the date range you want to review using the filters at the top of the dashboard.
2. Locate the **Inactive members** card.
3. Click **Export** to download the inactive-member data as a CSV file.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/bqsjHjd4g6B52Tb98yw2+/Screen+Shot+2026-10-30+at+19.58.01.png)

---

### **Related Articles**

- [How to Setup, Customize, and Manage Your Communities](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000280-how-to-setup-customize-and-manage-your-communities)
- [Communities - How to Manage Members Inside Groups](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000289-how-to-manage-members-inside-groups)
- [Communities: How to Manage Content](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000297-communities-how-to-manage-content)

title_en: Moving US numbers from Twilio to LeadConnector(LC)
source_md:
LC Phone

# Moving US Phone Numbers from Twilio to LC Phone

Migrate your US phone numbers from your Twilio account to HighLevel's LC Phone system and manage calling, SMS, and messaging registration in one platform.

What You'll Learn

This guide walks you through migrating US local and toll-free phone numbers from your Twilio account to HighLevel's LC Phone system.

You'll learn what information to gather before migration, how to submit a migration request, what moves with the phone number, and how to verify calling, SMS, and messaging registration after the cutover.

## What is Phone Number Migration?

Phone number migration transfers control of a US local or toll-free phone number from one phone system provider to another. When you migrate a phone number from your Twilio account to HighLevel's LC Phone system, the number becomes managed by LC Phone for all future calling, SMS, and messaging functionality.

This migration process changes which platform manages the number but does not automatically move historical data, call recordings, or messaging registration from your Twilio account.

HighLevel Support coordinates the migration end-to-end after you provide the required account and phone number identifiers.

## Key Benefits

Migrating your US phone numbers from Twilio to LC Phone centralizes phone management inside HighLevel and provides access to native LC Phone features.

**Centralized Phone Management** — Manage calling and messaging directly inside HighLevel without switching between platforms.

**Native HighLevel Features** — Use LC Phone functionality such as call tracking, workflows, and messaging automation.

**Simplified Billing** — Manage phone usage and number charges through HighLevel.

**Streamlined Support** — Troubleshoot LC Phone issues through HighLevel Support.

## What Moves with the Phone Number?

Moving a phone number changes which phone system manages the number. It does not automatically migrate historical phone-system data from the original Twilio account.

| Asset | Migration Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Phone number | Moves to LC Phone |
| Future calls and SMS | Route through LC Phone after cutover |
| Historical Twilio recordings | Do not automatically migrate |
| Historical voicemails | Do not automatically migrate |
| Contacts and Conversations | Are not transferred as part of phone number migration |
| A2P / Toll-Free registration | Must be verified after migration and may require re-registration |

Important

A2P registration may need to be completed again after moving from your own Twilio account to LC Phone. Existing A2P registration from Twilio does not automatically migrate to LC Phone. After migration, complete or verify A2P registration in HighLevel and confirm each applicable US local number is associated with the correct approved Campaign before resuming A2P messaging.

Toll-Free Numbers

After migration, confirm the number's Toll-Free Verification status before resuming messaging. Verification status should not be assumed to transfer automatically.

## Before the Migration

Preparing the destination location and preserving information you may need later reduces disruption during the cutover.

Checklist Item

Confirm the destination Sub-account ID

Identify the HighLevel Sub-account ID (Location ID) where the phone number will reside after migration.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080012211/original/pPDXz1VZqFxEPZgeOfM1L_pGevfoEioNtQ.png?1788439872)

Checklist Item

Confirm the losing Twilio Account SID

Locate the Twilio Account SID currently holding the phone number. This identifier is required for the migration request.

Checklist Item

Create a list of all numbers being migrated

Format phone numbers in E.164 format (e.g., +1XXXXXXXXXX) when possible.

Checklist Item

Download any Twilio recordings or voicemails that must be retained

Historical recordings and voicemails do not automatically migrate to LC Phone. Export and save any critical assets from your Twilio account before migration.

Checklist Item

Review the number's A2P or Toll-Free registration status

Check whether the number has active A2P 10DLC or Toll-Free Verification in Twilio. You may need to re-register or verify the number in HighLevel after migration.

Checklist Item

Note existing call-forwarding or routing behavior

Document how the number currently routes calls and SMS so you can replicate this configuration in LC Phone.

Checklist Item

Identify workflows or integrations that reference the phone number

Check HighLevel workflows, third-party integrations, and automations that may use the phone number. Update these configurations after migration if needed.

Checklist Item

Choose a preferred low-traffic cutover window

Include a preferred migration time in your HighLevel Support request to minimize impact on calling and messaging.

Note

For non-US numbers, use the [international number migration guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com).

## How to Move a US Number from Twilio to LC Phone

HighLevel Support coordinates the migration end-to-end after you provide the required identifiers and cutover preferences.

Step 1

Locate the Twilio Account SID currently holding the phone number

Find the losing Twilio Account SID in your Twilio console. This identifier is required to initiate the migration.

Step 2

Locate the destination HighLevel Sub-account ID (Location ID)

Identify the HighLevel Sub-account ID where the phone number will reside after migration.

Step 3

Open a HighLevel Support ticket

Submit a support request through the HighLevel Help Center. Include the following information:

- Phone number(s) you want to migrate (preferably in E.164 format, e.g., +1XXXXXXXXXX)
- Losing Twilio Account SID
- Destination HighLevel Sub-account ID (Location ID)
- Preferred cutover window (date and time)  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080012571/original/9msPvePhifZRdTEUw-p_1ZB6VnKoUNMq7g.gif?1788439990)  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080012762/original/IaQIz83Oq1zjqTRdKU2P-S11rwKujtRWYg.png?1788440069)

Step 4

HighLevel Support coordinates the migration and confirms when the number is live

HighLevel Support processes the migration request and notifies you when the phone number has been successfully moved to LC Phone.

Step 5

Test inbound and outbound calling and SMS after completion

Verify that the phone number is functioning correctly in LC Phone by testing calls and messages.

Migration Timing

Migration timing depends on receiving all required information and the scheduled cutover. HighLevel Support will confirm the migration window once the request is ready to process.

## Verify the Number After Migration

Testing the number immediately after cutover confirms that voice, SMS, routing, and messaging registration are working correctly in LC Phone.

Verification Step

Confirm the number appears in the correct HighLevel sub-account

Check the phone numbers list in the destination sub-account to verify the number has been added.

Verification Step

Place an outbound call

Make a test call from the migrated number to confirm outbound calling works.

Verification Step

Place an inbound call

Call the migrated number from an external phone to verify inbound calling routes correctly.

Verification Step

Send an outbound SMS

Send a test message from the migrated number to confirm outbound SMS works.

Verification Step

Send an inbound SMS

Send a message to the migrated number from an external phone to verify inbound SMS routing.

Verification Step

Verify call forwarding or routing

Confirm that call forwarding and routing rules match your intended configuration.

Verification Step

Verify the number assignment to the correct user or team

Check that the number is assigned to the correct user or team in HighLevel.

Verification Step

Confirm A2P Campaign association for applicable local numbers

For US local numbers, verify that the number is attached to an approved A2P Campaign in HighLevel's Trust Center before resuming A2P messaging.

Verification Step

Confirm Toll-Free Verification for applicable toll-free numbers

For toll-free numbers, confirm the Toll-Free Verification status before resuming messaging. Verification status should not be assumed to transfer automatically.

Verification Step

Review workflows and integrations that use the number

Check HighLevel workflows and third-party integrations to confirm they reference the correct phone number after migration.

Post-Migration Success

Once all verification steps are complete, the phone number is ready for production use in LC Phone.

title_en: How to Add and Reuse Images in Forms, Surveys & QR Codes with Media Picker
source_md:
Media Picker & Media Storage Integration provides a unified way to manage and insert images across forms, surveys, quizzes, and QR codes. It connects these builders directly to HighLevel’s centralized Media Storage, allowing you to browse, upload, and reuse assets from a single location.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Media Picker & Media Storage Integration?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-Media-Picker-&-Media-Storage-Integration?)
- [Key Benefits of Media Picker & Media Storage Integration](#Key-Benefits-of-Media-Picker-&-Media-Storage-Integration)
- [Media Picker & Media Storage](#Media-Picker-&-Media-Storage)
- [Image-Based Elements](#Image-Based-Elements)
- [Rich Text Editors](#Rich-Text-Editors)
- [Quiz Result Builder](#Quiz-Result-Builder)
- [QR Codes](#QR-Codes)
- [How to Use Media Picker & Media Storage Integration](#How-to-Use-Media-Picker-&-Media-Storage-Integration)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Media Picker & Media Storage Integration?**

Media Picker & Media Storage Integration connects image selection in Forms, Surveys, Quizzes, and QR Codes to HighLevel’s centralized Media Storage (Media Center).

The Media Picker is a pop-up window that opens when you click options like “Change Image” or the image icon in builders, allowing you to select or upload media from Media Storage.

Whenever you add or change an image, the Global Media Picker opens, giving you access to your full media library, including folders, uploads, and external sources where supported. This ensures a consistent and organized experience when working with images across different tools.

---

## **Key Benefits of Media Picker & Media Storage Integration**

### 

- **One consistent image experience across HighLevel:**Forms, surveys, quizzes, QR codes, funnels, and websites use the same Global Media Picker, creating a familiar and predictable workflow.

- **Faster and more intuitive image selection:**Browse folders, search files, preview images, and select assets without switching between different upload interfaces.

- **Reuse existing assets instead of re-uploading:**Access previously uploaded logos, backgrounds, and graphics from Media Storage, reducing duplication and saving time.

- **Centralized media management:**All images are stored in one place, where you can organize files using folders, rename assets, and manage unused media.

- **Improved brand consistency:**Teams can reuse approved brand assets across multiple builders, helping maintain a consistent visual identity.

- **Compatibility with Media Storage features:**Images selected through the picker can benefit from features like file filtering, image editing, and external integrations available in Media Storage.

---

## **Media Picker & Media Storage**

The Global Media Picker acts as the interface for accessing Media Storage when inserting images.

When you open the Media Picker, you can:

**Browse Media Storage**

Navigate folders, switch between grid or list views, and review image details such as dimensions.

**Search and filter assets**

Locate files quickly using search and available filters.

**Upload new images**

Drag and drop files directly into the picker to add them to your Media Storage library.

**Preview before inserting**

Open images to review them before adding them to your builder.

**Edit images (where supported)**

Use built-in editing tools in Media Storage to adjust images before inserting them.

---

## **Image-Based Elements**

Image-based elements in forms, surveys, and quizzes use the Global Media Picker for selecting visuals.

When working with these elements, Clicking Change Image opens the Media Picker. Selected or uploaded images are stored in Media Storage. The same image can be reused across multiple builders

Example workflow:

- Open your builder (e.g., Form Builder)
- Select an image element
- Click Change Image
- Choose or upload an image from the Media Picker
- Insert the image and save

---

## **Rich Text Editors**

Rich Text Editors (RTEs) support inserting images directly within text fields.

You can Click the image icon in the editor toolbar, Open the Media Picker, Select or upload an image, Insert it inline within the text. This is useful for adding logos, instructions, or visual context inside descriptions and messages.

---

## **Quiz Result Builder**

The Quiz Result Builder supports images for different outcomes, allowing you to visually enhance results. For each result, Image selection opens the Global Media Picker. You can reuse existing assets or upload new ones. The same image can be applied across multiple results or quizzes. This helps maintain consistency across quiz experiences.

---

## **QR Codes**

QR Code configurations support adding logos or image overlays using the Media Picker. When adding a logo,Click the image or logo option, Open the Media Picker, Select or upload a logo from Media Storage, Insert and adjust as needed.

Using shared assets ensures consistent branding across campaigns.

---

## **How to Use Media Picker & Media Storage Integration**

### 

### **Step 1: Organize your Media Storage**

Open Media Storage from the sidebar  
Create folders (e.g., Logos, Forms, Quizzes, QR Codes)  
Upload commonly used assets

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069797528/original/8ul4zORUojcEfPAX6GnGAZJxBC8EyCjBhA.png?1776949083)

### **Step 2: Open a supported builder**

Navigate to Form Builder, Survey Builder, Quiz Builder, or QR Codes  
Create or edit an asset

The screenshot below shows how the Media Picker is accessed in the Form Builder using the image icon in a Rich Text Editor.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069798107/original/cGZwQbHybzFIVuhjppAlQjH4Efx2s-K5mQ.png?1776949431)

### 

### **Step 3: Insert or change an image**

After clicking the **image icon** or **Upload**, the **Media Picker** opens as a pop-up within the builder. From here, you can browse your existing media, search for specific files, or upload a new image.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069799793/original/kWPaSyBN6HcuaxdMh0cEi5nce6JPh6dC5w.png?1776950240)

Select the image you want to use, then click **Insert Media** to add it to your form, survey, quiz, or QR code.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069799945/original/_U-8pBT9Gg4uMXKHyK_GWiy0blr-dxsJfg.png?1776950302)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155069800120/original/8IdxLMVoxcvRmK-OhYQBeHM6coU--erxOQ.png?1776950417)

### **Step 4: Maintain your media library**

Rename or move files in Media Storage

Remove unused assets. Edit images when needed and reuse updated versions

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need to enable the Media Picker?**

No. The Global Media Picker is available by default in supported areas.

**Q: Where are uploaded images stored?**

All images are stored in Media Storage for your sub-account and can be reused across different modules.

**Q: Does this affect files uploaded by contacts?**

No. Contact-submitted files follow separate storage processes. This integration applies to images used in builders.

**Q: Can I use external sources like Google Drive?**

Yes. Supported external sources can be accessed through the Media Picker.

**Q: What happens to existing images?**

Existing images remain unchanged and continue to function as expected.

**Q: Can I rename or organize images already in use?**

Yes. Changes made in Media Storage reflect wherever the image is used.

**Q: Are there file size or type limits?**

Yes. Limits are based on Media Storage and the specific builder being used.

**Q: Can I edit images inside the Media Picker?**

Image selection happens in the picker. Editing is available through Media Storage’s built-in editor.

**Q: What is the difference between Media Center and Media Storage?**

Media Storage is the library where files are stored, while the Media Picker (Media Center interface) is how you access and select those files.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Complete Guide to Media Storage](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002707-complete-guide-to-media-storage-)

￼

- [Media Storage File Upload Limits](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001216629-media-storage-file-upload-limits)￼

- [Google Drive Integration with Media Storage](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004190-google-drive-in-media-storage)**￼**
